concepts.name: Quantum Thermalization
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes an exact, rigorous correspondence (Eq. 2) linking the long-time thermalized steady-state magnetization of a driven spin to its short-time linear-response spectrum, providing a rare exact statement about quantum thermalization. This result holds even when the steady state differs substantially from the initial state and is independent of the microscopic details of the system-bath coupling. It further demonstrates that thermalization can be confined to a metastable sector of Hilbert space, as shown for the repulsive Fermi polaron branch.

concepts.name: Kubo Linear-Response Theory and Fermi's Golden Rule
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that the Fermi's Golden Rule transition rate spectrum, a short-time near-equilibrium quantity, encodes information about long-time non-equilibrium thermalization through an analytic continuation of the spectral correlation function. The key mathematical step is evaluating the Fourier-transformed transition rate at the imaginary time point t = -iβ, connecting equilibrium spectroscopy directly to the thermalized steady state. This extends the utility of linear-response spectroscopy far beyond its conventional short-time domain.

concepts.name: Fermi Polaron Physics and BCS-BEC Crossover
concepts.contribution: The paper uses ultracold 6Li impurity atoms coupled to a Fermi sea as a tunable experimental platform to test the correspondence across the BCS-BEC crossover, where strong correlations make independent theoretical calculation of both the spectral function and thermalization extremely challenging. It experimentally confirms that the zero crossing Δ0 predicted from linear-response spectra matches the directly measured thermalized magnetization across a wide range of interaction strengths. The experiment also reveals a quantitative scaling Δp - Δ0 ∝ Γ^2.2 relating the deviation between spectral peak and thermalization zero crossing to the spectral linewidth.

concepts.name: Detailed Balance and Fluctuation-Dissipation Relations
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a detailed-balance relation connecting the forward (R↓) and reverse (R↑) transition spectra of the spin, showing R↑(Δ) = e^{-β(Δ-Δ0)} R↓(Δ), which is a manifestation of thermal equilibrium with the bath. This relation is used to construct a symmetrized form of the correspondence that avoids numerical difficulties from exponential amplification of spectral tails, enabling a practical and complete experimental verification. The result generalizes the standard fluctuation-dissipation theorem to a non-equilibrium driven setting via the thermalization assumption.

concepts.name: Tensor Networks
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a categorical generalization called the pro-tensor network, where vector spaces on edges are replaced by enriched categories and linear maps at nodes are replaced by profunctors. Contraction of tensors is generalized via the coend construction, a categorical analogue of index summation. This provides a rigorous graphical framework for studying collections of many-body theories simultaneously rather than individual systems.

concepts.name: Topological Order and Levin-Wen String-Net Models
concepts.contribution: The paper recovers the Levin-Wen model as a special 'uniform' pro-tensor network built from a monoidal category C, generalizing the construction beyond the usual assumptions of finiteness, semisimplicity, and rigidity. The evaluation map derived from the Frobenius structure of the input category reproduces the plaquette term of the Levin-Wen Hamiltonian. This also extends naturally to fermionic string-net models by working over super vector spaces.

concepts.name: Topological Defects and Anyonic Excitations
concepts.contribution: The paper characterizes particle-like defects in string-net models as modules over a renormalization algebra, and proves a generalized Kitaev-Kong theorem identifying five equivalent descriptions of the defect category including lax module profunctors, Tambara modules, and promonad modules. This generalization removes the assumptions of semisimplicity, finiteness, and rigidity required in the original Kitaev-Kong result, substantially broadening the classification of topological excitations.

concepts.name: Topological Holography and Symmetry
concepts.contribution: The paper interprets the string-net pro-tensor network simultaneously as a space of symmetric tensor networks (encoding 1+1D generalized symmetry) and as a 2+1D topological order, providing a concrete pro-tensor network realization of the holographic duality between symmetry and SymTFT. The tube promonad is shown to have a representation category equivalent to the Drinfeld center of the free cocompletion of C, extending the holographic correspondence to non-finite and non-semisimple symmetry categories such as representations of compact Lie groups.

2605.06653v1.title: From Baby Universes to Narain Moduli: Topological Boundary Averaging in SymTFTs

concepts.name: Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT)
concepts.contribution: The paper proposes using SymTFTs as the organizing framework for ensemble averaging in holography, identifying the ensemble variable with topological boundary conditions rather than with local dynamical data. It demonstrates that fixing the SymTFT and physical boundary while averaging over topological boundary conditions (caps) reproduces known ensemble averages, providing a unified structural explanation for why certain gravitational path integrals compute ensemble moments.

concepts.name: Ensemble Averaging in Holography
concepts.contribution: The paper reinterprets ensemble averaging not as an average over arbitrary boundary dynamics but as an average over topological completions of a fixed relative theory, controlled entirely by the SymTFT. This is concretely demonstrated in two cases: the Marolf–Maxfield topological model, where the groupoid sum over finite-set caps reproduces Poisson/Bell-polynomial moments, and Narain moduli space averaging, where integrating over Lagrangian topological boundary conditions of an R-valued BF theory with Haar measure reproduces the standard Narain average and Siegel–Weil result.

concepts.name: Narain Moduli Space
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a SymTFT derivation of the Narain moduli space as the space of compact topological boundary conditions of a 3D R-valued BF theory, with the moduli (metric G and B-field) appearing as coordinates on Lagrangian subgroups of the defect group. The Zamolodchikov measure on Narain moduli space is derived as the Haar measure induced by the O(c,c;R) automorphism group of the SymTFT, giving an intrinsic topological origin to both the moduli space geometry and its natural integration measure.

concepts.name: Baby Universes and Spacetime Wormholes
concepts.contribution: The paper reframes the baby-universe mechanism for non-factorization in terms of SymTFT caps: at a fixed topological boundary condition the theory factorizes, while non-factorization arises entirely from averaging over distinct caps. In the Marolf–Maxfield model, the wormhole contribution (variance of the partition function) is reproduced as the variance of the finite-set cardinality over the groupoid of topological boundary conditions, giving a purely topological account of the connected two-boundary correlator.

2605.06636v1.title: What You Don't Know Won't Hurt You: Self-Consistent Hierarchical Inference with Unknown Follow-up Selection Strategies

concepts.name: Hierarchical Bayesian Inference
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the follow-up selection probability P(F|D,x) cancels term-by-term in the posterior when inference conditions on all original catalog data and all follow-up data, producing Equation 5 as the core result. This means self-consistent population inference is achievable without explicitly modeling the follow-up decision process, even when that process strongly correlates with the latent parameters of interest. Coverage tests across multiple follow-up strategies confirm the posteriors are correctly calibrated and unbiased.

concepts.name: Inhomogeneous Poisson Point Processes with Selection Effects
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the standard thinned Poisson process framework used in astrophysical population inference to include a second layer of thinning representing follow-up selection, deriving the joint likelihood via both top-down and bottom-up approaches. It shows that marginalizing over undetected events and unobserved follow-up data yields a likelihood that depends only on the primary detection selection P(D|Λ), not on the follow-up selection. This cleanly separates the well-characterized survey selection function from the uncharacterizable follow-up decision process.

concepts.name: Gravitational-Wave Cosmology and Bright Sirens
concepts.contribution: The paper applies its framework to the bright sirens method for measuring the Hubble constant H0, showing that unbiased constraints are recovered regardless of which events are chosen for electromagnetic follow-up, despite the follow-up decision being made in real time by humans with incomplete information. It quantifies that strategic follow-up selection (e.g., preferring high-mass or low-mass events) can improve posterior precision by up to a factor of ~1.5 compared to random selection at fixed observational cost. This clarifies a long-standing implicit assumption in the GW cosmology community that independent GW and EM noise justifies multiplying single-event likelihoods.

concepts.name: Population Mixture Models and Contaminant Classification
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that when an initial survey catalog contains contaminants, modeling the full population as a mixture of subpopulations within the hierarchical framework allows simultaneous inference of both the target and contaminant populations without modeling follow-up selection. In a worked Gaia-inspired example, the true astrophysical mixing fraction of rare dark-companion systems (7.4%) is correctly recovered as 3.9+5.4-2.4% even though contaminants comprise 79% of the detected catalog but only 26% of the followed-up sample. The paper identifies model misspecification of the contaminant distribution as the primary remaining risk when applying this approach.

2605.06633v1.title: Machine Learning Approaches to Building Quantum Circuits for Sets of Matrices

concepts.name: Quantum Circuit Decomposition
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a universal, shortest analytic quantum circuit decomposition for arbitrary diagonal unitary matrices of any size, achieving algorithmic complexity of O(2^n) in the number of CNOT gates, compared to O(2.5^n) for prior numerical methods. It introduces two recursive circuit architectures—a 'Strange Fractal' and a 'Binary Tree'—for constructing the CNOT gate sequence, and proves that the mapping between diagonal matrix phase parameters and circuit rotation parameters is strictly linear.

concepts.name: Cartan Decomposition of Unitary Groups
concepts.contribution: The paper applies the Cartan subalgebra structure of SU(2^n) to parameterize diagonal matrices via exponential maps, establishing that the relevant Cartan subgroup coordinates transform linearly into quantum circuit parameters. It further exploits the Weyl chamber representation to show that diagonal two-qubit operators have vanishing hz coordinate, formally proving that two CNOT gates are both necessary and sufficient for their implementation.

concepts.name: Gate Universality and the Solovay-Kitaev Theorem
concepts.contribution: The paper situates its decomposition results within the framework of universal gate sets, distinguishing between approximate universality (finite gate sets, Solovay-Kitaev) and exact universality (continuous SU(2) rotations plus CNOT). By working with continuous single-qubit rotations, it achieves exact rather than approximate decompositions, directly minimizing the dominant source of hardware error by reducing two-qubit CNOT gate count.

concepts.name: Quantum Decoherence and Circuit Depth Optimization
concepts.contribution: The paper directly addresses decoherence by motivating circuit depth and two-qubit gate count minimization, citing an order-of-magnitude difference in error rates between one-qubit (99.7%) and two-qubit (96.5%) gates. The derived O(2^n) CNOT-count decomposition for diagonal matrices provides a concrete reduction in circuit depth relative to general-purpose numerical decomposers, improving the practical fidelity of executing diagonal operators on near-term quantum hardware.

2605.06626v1.title: Integrable perturbations of polynomial Hamiltonian systems

concepts.name: Hamiltonian Integrability
concepts.contribution: The paper proves that any real-analytic Hamiltonian system with a non-degenerate, nonresonant equilibrium can be made completely integrable by adding an arbitrarily high-order perturbation term F. This extends the classical notion of integrability near equilibria by showing that complete integrability is always achievable up to any prescribed order, and moreover globally on all of R^2n.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian Normal Forms
concepts.contribution: The paper employs and extends normal form theory by constructing a symplectic coordinate change that reduces the Hamiltonian to a normal form whose integrals in involution are the standard quadratic polynomials associated with the linearized system. The key technical advance is using continuous averaging to realize this coordinate change as a flow generated by an auxiliary Hamiltonian, enabling the transformation to be extended globally rather than only locally.

concepts.name: Perturbation Theory of Hamiltonian Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper contributes a constructive perturbation scheme showing that the difference between the integrable normal form and the original Hamiltonian can be made as small as desired near the equilibrium (order M+1 for any chosen M). The global version of the result, achieved via a Gaussian damping trick on the averaging Hamiltonian, ensures the perturbation F is real-analytic on all of R^2n, going significantly beyond standard local perturbation results.

concepts.name: Symplectic Geometry and Canonical Transformations
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs a global real-analytic symplectic diffeomorphism of R^2n to itself by flowing along a modified Hamiltonian that is exponentially decaying at spatial infinity, ensuring the flow converges to a well-defined limit map. This provides a concrete global canonical transformation that simultaneously respects the symplectic structure and achieves the desired normal form, with an extension to compact real-analytic symplectic manifolds via the Grauert embedding theorem.

2605.06613v1.title: The Phases of the Scalar S-Matrix Island

concepts.name: S-Matrix Bootstrap
concepts.contribution: The paper tightens two-sided non-perturbative bounds on the four-dimensional scalar 2-to-2 scattering amplitude using both dual (fixed-t dispersion relation) and primal (crossing-symmetric ansatz) bootstrap methods. It extends the numerical precision of the allowed region in the space of low-energy Wilson coefficients and introduces Regge moments as a new diagnostic tool for extracting emergent high-energy behavior from finite-truncation bootstrap solutions.

concepts.name: Regge Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that extremal bootstrap amplitudes exhibit emergent Regge behavior—power-law growth T(s,t) ~ β(t)s^α(t)—over a parametrically growing energy window as the truncation order increases, despite the ansatz having trivial asymptotics at any finite order. It classifies the boundary arcs by their Regge intercepts: marginal (α→0) along the AB arc and positive (α≈1) along the AC and BC arcs, revealing distinct UV regimes.

concepts.name: Virtual States and Resonance Poles
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies infinite towers of virtual states (second-sheet poles below two-particle threshold) as the universal spectral signature of the AB phase, providing quantitative agreement with perturbative λϕ⁴ predictions for their masses. It also tracks the full resonance spectrum along all boundary arcs, uncovering two distinct decoupling mechanisms: energy decoupling of a strongly coupled Regge sector along AC, and large-N_c-like suppression of residues at fixed mass along BC.

concepts.name: Effective Field Theory UV Completion
concepts.contribution: The paper interprets the three boundary arcs as distinct universal phases corresponding to different UV mechanisms by which a gapped scalar EFT can be consistently completed: asymptotically weak scattering with logarithmic running (AB), energy decoupling of a strongly interacting higher-spin Regge sector (AC), and large-N_c-like decoupling where resonance masses remain fixed while couplings vanish (BC). It connects these phases to candidate microscopic theories such as confining gauge theories with a light pseudoscalar and brane-localized Goldstone modes.

2605.06602v1.title: Quasi-homogeneous black hole geometrothermodynamics in Einstein-Maxwell theory

concepts.name: Quasi-Homogeneous Thermodynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper formally establishes that the fundamental equations of Reissner-Nordström, Kerr, and Kerr-Newman black holes are quasi-homogeneous functions with specific scaling weights, rather than the standard degree-one homogeneous functions of laboratory thermodynamics. It derives a generalized Euler identity and Gibbs-Duhem relation appropriate for these systems, resolving the inconsistency that arises when standard extensivity is naively applied to self-gravitating systems. This quasi-homogeneity is shown to be a mandatory physical requirement, not merely a mathematical convenience, for building a consistent thermodynamic and geometric framework.

concepts.name: Geometrothermodynamics (GTD)
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the GTD formalism by explicitly incorporating quasi-homogeneous scaling coefficients into the construction of the equilibrium manifold metrics, yielding three classes of Legendre-invariant metrics applicable to non-extensive systems. It demonstrates that the metric gII correctly identifies phase transitions in black holes by producing curvature singularities that coincide exactly with the divergences of the heat capacity, while metrics gI and gIII capture additional phase transition conditions tied to other response functions. This provides a unified, potential-independent geometric description of black hole thermodynamics that broadens the classical Davies criterion.

concepts.name: Black Hole Phase Transitions
concepts.contribution: The paper proves analytically, for the Reissner-Nordström, Kerr, and full Kerr-Newman black holes, that the curvature singularities of the GTD equilibrium space metric are in exact correspondence with the zeros of the heat capacity denominators that signal second-order phase transitions. Beyond reproducing Davies' original conditions, the GTD framework predicts additional types of phase transitions associated with other second derivatives of the thermodynamic potential, indicating a richer phase structure than previously recognized. The extremal black hole limit is shown to correspond to a mere coordinate singularity in the equilibrium manifold, not a physical phase transition.

concepts.name: Legendre Invariance in Thermodynamic Geometry
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies Legendre invariance as a foundational requirement that distinguishes GTD from earlier geometric approaches such as those of Weinhold and Ruppeiner, whose Hessian-based metrics change form under a change of thermodynamic potential. By constructing the phase space using contact geometry and deriving metrics whose components are unaffected by Legendre transformations, the paper ensures that all physical predictions, including curvature singularities and phase transition loci, are independent of the choice of thermodynamic potential. This invariance is shown to be directly compatible with the quasi-homogeneous structure of black hole fundamental equations.

2605.06579v1.title: Practical Log-Depth Quantum State Preparation and Circuit Verification via Tree Tensor Network Compilation

concepts.name: Tensor Network State Preparation
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a renormalization procedure that converts matrix product states into binary tree tensor networks via iterative site merges and singular value decompositions, yielding quantum circuits with O(log N) depth. An explicit truncation parameter is exposed that allows practitioners to trade a controllable, linearly-growing infidelity for dramatically reduced circuit depth, with fidelity remaining above 0.97 for up to 20 qubits even when all internal bonds are truncated to dimension 2.

concepts.name: Quantum Circuit Compilation and Transpilation
concepts.contribution: The paper benchmarks the compiled circuits against realistic hardware topologies including heavy-hex, square-grid, and all-to-all connectivity, demonstrating that the approximate decomposition reduces transpiled depths from millions of gates (exact case) to under 200 gates for 200-qubit systems. This makes the method practical for near-term noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices where circuit depth is the primary limiting factor.

concepts.name: Matrix Product Operator Vectorization
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the MPS-to-circuit compilation to matrix product operators by interpreting both input and output physical legs as sites of a larger MPS, enabling the construction of log-depth, ancilla-free verifier circuits that evaluate overlap magnitudes of the form |⟨ϕ|U|ψ⟩|² as a single computational basis amplitude. This generalizes earlier linear-depth verifier circuit constructions and subsumes the quantum SWAP test as a special case when U is taken to be the identity.

concepts.name: Quantum Device Calibration and Fidelity Estimation
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that verifier circuits derived from MPO representations of target unitaries provide a monotonically decreasing fidelity metric as hardware noise increases, validated numerically with multi-controlled-Z gates and Pauli string exponentials. This offers a structured, hardware-executable alternative to standard swap-test-based benchmarking for circuit-level device calibration without requiring ancilla qubits.

2605.06577v1.title: Entanglement generation in a two-body Schrödinger--Newton model

concepts.name: Schrödinger–Newton Equation
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the single-particle Schrödinger–Newton framework to a two-body setting by explicitly separating the nonlinear self-localization term from the nonseparable Newtonian pair potential. It demonstrates analytically that the self-field term is isospectral with respect to the Schmidt decomposition, meaning it cannot generate entanglement, while the pair potential drives all Schmidt-spectrum changes. This clarifies which physical mechanism in semiclassical gravity is responsible for entanglement generation.

concepts.name: Quantum Entanglement Generation
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a detailed numerical and analytical account of how entanglement grows during two-body gravitational scattering, showing that it depends sensitively on initial spatial configuration, wavepacket dispersion, and mass ratio. It derives a short-time expansion showing entanglement growth is quadratic in time and proportional to the variance of the nonadditive residual part of the pair potential. Highly localized self-bound profiles suppress entanglement growth, while dispersive Gaussian wavepackets amplify it.

concepts.name: Schmidt Decomposition and Separability
concepts.contribution: The paper proves that separability-preserving mean-field interactions, including the canonical two-particle Schrödinger–Newton equation, preserve the Schmidt eigenvalue spectrum by construction, and shows this follows from the Hartree projection onto the product-state manifold. It demonstrates that only a nonseparable pair operator can change the Schmidt rank of an initially factorized state, providing a clean theoretical distinction between mean-field and pair-interaction models.

concepts.name: Wigner Function Negativity
concepts.contribution: The paper uses reduced and relative-coordinate Wigner functions as phase-space diagnostics to distinguish simple wavepacket squeezing from non-Gaussian fragmentation accompanying entanglement growth. It shows that mass-asymmetric collisions with dispersive Gaussian wavepackets produce pronounced Wigner negativity, signaling non-classical phase-space structure. The relative-coordinate Wigner function is identified as the most direct diagnostic for the entangling interaction since the pair potential depends only on the relative coordinate.

2605.06569v1.title: Equidistribution of Eigenfunctions of Quantum Cat Maps

concepts.name: Quantum Ergodicity and Semiclassical Measures
concepts.contribution: The paper proves that an explicit family of short-period eigenfunctions of quantum cat maps equidistributes on the phase space torus T² in the semiclassical limit, converging to Lebesgue measure with a logarithmic rate. This extends quantum ergodicity results to a specific near-extremal family, showing equidistribution persists even when eigenfunctions are constructed to have anomalously large ℓ∞-norms.

concepts.name: Quantum Scarring
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a sharp contrast to scarring phenomena by demonstrating that short quantum periods do not necessarily produce scarred eigenfunctions. While Faure, Nonnenmacher, and De Bièvre showed short-period eigenfunctions can scar, this work exhibits an explicit short-period family that instead equidistributes, clarifying the boundary conditions under which scarring occurs.

concepts.name: Eigenfunction Localization and ℓ∞-Norms
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes that the constructed eigenfunctions exhibit strong coordinate localization, with their logarithmically large ℓ∞-norm asymptotically concentrated on a single basis coordinate, while simultaneously equidistributing in phase space. This demonstrates that coordinate-basis localization and semiclassical equidistribution are not mutually exclusive, resolving a tension suggested by prior numerical evidence.

concepts.name: Quantum Chaos and Hyperbolic Dynamics
concepts.contribution: Using the exact Egorov identity and dispersive Gauss-sum estimates, the paper exploits the hyperbolic stretching of the classical cat map—where orbit components grow like λ|s| while the period satisfies N ≍ λ^(t+1)/2—to bound the number of resonant times to a logarithmic count. This arithmetic-dynamical mechanism provides a quantitative mechanism linking classical hyperbolicity to quantum equidistribution rates.

2605.06566v1.title: A Unified SU(2) Framework for Vector Beam Transformations and Complex Beam Shaping

concepts.name: SU(2) Symmetry in Polarization Optics
concepts.contribution: The paper reformulates all polarization transformations by birefringent elements as spatially varying SU(2) operations, with Pauli operators defined basis-independently through spectral decomposition onto the six cardinal polarization states of the Poincaré sphere. This yields a closed-form, coordinate-free prescription for computing waveplate parameters directly from inner products of source and target states, which the authors claim has not previously appeared in the polarization optics literature. The framework unifies scalar beam transformations, vector beam transformations, and complex beam shaping under a single algebraic structure.

concepts.name: Doubly Inhomogeneous Waveplates (d-plates)
concepts.contribution: The paper provides an explicit constructive design procedure for d-plates—waveplates with both retardance and fast-axis orientation varying spatially—that implement a prescribed vector beam transformation exactly, including the global phase, when a specific single-plate condition on the circular polarization components is satisfied. It further shows how any d-plate can be decomposed into a finite sequence of singly inhomogeneous plates, including a QHQ configuration, making the designs physically realizable. This extends prior work by treating the full SU(2) parameter synthesis rather than special cases.

concepts.name: Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) and Spin-Orbit Coupling in Light
concepts.contribution: The paper generalizes the quantum step used in spin-orbital quantum walks beyond q-plates by allowing arbitrary input and output polarization states, including elliptical polarizations, to drive OAM shifts, not just circular polarizations. It introduces biased quantum steps where the forward and backward OAM shifts can be unequal integers, decomposed into a spiral phase plate followed by a generalized inhomogeneous waveplate sequence. This enables instantaneous multi-step quantum walk dynamics to be realized with a single engineered optical element.

concepts.name: Quantum Channels on Discrete-Variable Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the action of a d-plate on the OAM degree of freedom, with polarization as a physical ancilla, constitutes a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) map whose Kraus operators take a convolutional form in the OAM basis. Trace preservation is derived directly from pointwise unitarity of the waveplate operator combined with Parseval's theorem, providing a rigorous quantum information interpretation of classical optical elements. This establishes d-plate engineering as a concrete route to implementing structured quantum channels for OAM-based information processing.

2605.06560v1.title: $F_K/F_π$ as a precision test of a new four flavor Domain Wall Fermion action

concepts.name: Domain Wall Fermions and Chiral Symmetry on the Lattice
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a new four-flavor Möbius Domain Wall Fermion action combining 8 steps of stout link smearing with a weakened Symanzik gauge action rectangle term, achieving very small residual chiral symmetry breaking (mres < 1.5 MeV) at unusually short fifth-dimension lengths (L5 as small as 4 lattice units). This advance reduces computational cost significantly while maintaining good chiral symmetry across five lattice spacings down to a ≈ 0.05 fm, demonstrating that topological tunneling still occurs even at fine lattice spacings.

concepts.name: Meson Decay Constants and Chiral Perturbation Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper computes FK/Fπ using a next-to-next-to-leading order (N2LO) chiral perturbation theory extrapolation across 30 ensembles spanning a wide range of pion masses and lattice spacings, obtaining FK±/Fπ± = 1.1962(34) at 0.28% total precision. It also finds that non-analytic logarithmic corrections at N2LO are strongly disfavored by the data and provides a new independent determination of the NLO low-energy constant L5.

concepts.name: CKM Matrix Unitarity and Flavor Physics
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a new, fully independent lattice QCD determination of FK±/Fπ±, a critical input for relating kaon and pion leptonic decay rates to the ratio |Vus|/|Vud| used in first-row CKM unitarity tests. By using a different fermion action from the dominant HISQ-based calculations that share configurations, this result adds an independent data point to the global lattice average and helps scrutinize the persistent 2-3σ deficit in CKM first-row unitarity.

concepts.name: Lattice QCD Continuum and Infinite-Volume Extrapolation
concepts.contribution: The paper performs a Bayesian model-averaging analysis over 16 distinct chiral-continuum extrapolation models, incorporating N2LO and N3LO discretization corrections as well as NLO finite-volume corrections via modified Bessel functions, to robustly control systematic uncertainties. Stability checks under various data cuts in pion mass and lattice spacing confirm the reliability of the continuum extrapolation, with the five-lattice-spacing dataset providing strong control over discretization effects despite relatively large O(a²) corrections compared to HISQ-based calculations.

2605.06550v1.title: Hadrons in $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetric QCD from non-Abelian string on 2D black hole

concepts.name: Non-Abelian Vortex Strings as Critical Superstrings
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the identification of non-Abelian vortex strings in 4D N=2 SQCD as critical superstrings from the U(2) case to U(N) gauge theory with arbitrary even N and Nf=2N quarks. It demonstrates that the hadron spectrum derived from the string picture remains invariant in functional form across this generalization, with only the multiplicities of states changing. This universality is established through a ZK-symmetric mass deformation and an interpolation procedure connecting different gauge group ranks.

concepts.name: 2D Black Hole (SL(2,R)/U(1) Coset) and Hagedorn Thermodynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that the mass-deformed worldsheet theory of the non-Abelian string is dual to the 2D N=2 supersymmetric black hole with cigar geometry at Kac-Moody level k=1, which corresponds precisely to the Hagedorn temperature. By analyzing the black hole entropy near the Hagedorn point, the authors extract the spectral density of hadronic states, finding a universal leading Hagedorn exponent and a subleading logarithmic correction whose coefficient grows as N^2, providing a quantitative string-theoretic prediction for multiplicity growth with gauge group rank.

concepts.name: Conifold Transition and Phase Structure of N=2 SQCD
concepts.contribution: The paper argues that 4D N=2 SQCD with Nf=2N possesses two distinct phases—a perturbative Higgs phase at weak coupling and a hadronic/stringy phase at strong coupling—that are not analytically connected. The massless states in each phase belong to different representations of the global flavor symmetry group (bifundamental in the Higgs phase versus antisymmetric in the stringy phase), and the transition between them is identified from the string theory side as a conifold transition between resolved and deformed conifold geometries.

concepts.name: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking and Goldstone Bosons in Strongly Coupled SQCD
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the massless b-baryons in the stringy phase of U(N) SQCD, which live in the antisymmetric representation of SU(N), are precisely the Goldstone bosons arising from the spontaneous breaking of the global flavor symmetry SU(N)×U(1)B down to Sp(N/2) by the VEV of the b-baryon condensate. The count of Goldstone modes N(N-1)/2 is shown to match exactly the dimension of the antisymmetric representation, and is verified both algebraically via Dynkin diagram folding and numerically.

2605.06547v1.title: Affine Subcode Ensemble Decoding for Degeneracy-Aware Quantum Error Correction

concepts.name: Quantum Error Correction and Stabilizer Codes
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a formal mathematical framework for degeneracy sets, defining them as cosets of the stabilizer subspace that partition all errors sharing the same syndrome and logical effect. It proves that appending linearly independent rows (splitters) to the check matrix subdivides each degeneracy set into equal-sized disjoint subsets, providing a rigorous tool for controlling the degeneracy search space. This directly advances the theory of degeneracy-aware decoding for stabilizer codes.

concepts.name: Belief Propagation Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies degeneracy as a structural cause of BP non-convergence and trapping sets in quantum LDPC codes, and demonstrates that reducing the effective degeneracy set size per decoding path improves convergence. By combining quaternary BP with overcomplete check matrices and ensemble diversity, the approach nearly eliminates Type I failures on tested codes. Simulation results on toric and generalized bicycle codes show the method outperforms correlated minimum-weight perfect matching and BP with OSD post-processing.

concepts.name: Ensemble Decoding and Diversity in Channel Coding
concepts.contribution: The paper extends affine subcode ensemble decoding, previously developed for classical linear block codes, to the quantum setting by exploiting the algebraic splitting of degeneracy sets to generate structurally diverse decoding paths. It demonstrates that increasing the number of independently constructed check-matrix batches yields greater performance gains than increasing paths per batch, attributing this to inter-batch diversity. The framework enables parallel decoding without requiring post-processing steps such as ordered statistics decoding.

concepts.name: Overcomplete Parity-Check Matrices
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that the additional rows introduced as splitters for degeneracy partitioning also expand the pool of available redundant rows for constructing overcomplete check matrices, enabling sparser overcomplete matrices with fewer short Tanner-graph cycles across ensemble paths. This dual-purpose use of splitters tightens the connection between algebraic code structure and graph-based decoder design. Numerical evidence confirms that decoding with overcomplete matrices consistently reduces logical error rates compared to standard check matrices.

2605.06543v1.title: A Rayleigh criterion for mechanical instability: inducing activity by chemo-mechanical coupling

concepts.name: Rayleigh Criterion for Instability
concepts.contribution: The paper generalizes Rayleigh's original thermoacoustic phase criterion—that heat addition in phase with pressure drives self-sustained oscillations—to chemo-mechanical systems. It derives an analogous condition expressed in terms of the phase relation between entropic and frenetic contributions, specifying precisely when chemical driving produces sustained rotational or active mechanical motion. This extends a classical acoustics result into the domain of nonequilibrium statistical mechanics and biophysics.

concepts.name: Frenesy (Time-Symmetric Dynamical Activity)
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the time-symmetric sector of dynamical fluctuations—frenesy, captured by the reactivities of the Markov jump processes—is the direct enabler of negative linear friction in the probe dynamics. It shows that the friction coefficient decomposes into an entropic part (always positive, tied to the fluctuation-dissipation relation) and a frenetic part (which can be negative), with the latter allowing chemical driving to inject energy into mechanical motion. This concretely illustrates how frenesy, not dissipation alone, governs the onset of mechanical instability.

concepts.name: Chemo-Mechanical Coupling and Emergence of Active Matter
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a thermodynamically consistent framework—using local detailed balance and semi-reciprocity—under which a passive Newtonian probe coupled to driven Markov jump processes acquires active behavior without any externally imposed nonconservative mechanical forces. It derives explicit criteria for when this coupling produces a bimodal velocity distribution and limit-cycle dynamics characteristic of active particles, connecting microscopic chemical driving to macroscopic mechanical activity. This bridges nonequilibrium statistical mechanics with mechanobiology by showing activity emerges from the interplay of entropy production and dynamical activity.

concepts.name: Nonreciprocal Forces in Nonequilibrium Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that when two probes are each coupled to the same driven chemical bath, an effective interaction emerges that contains both a reciprocal potential part and a non-reciprocal non-potential part proportional to the position-dependent reactivities. The non-reciprocity, quantified by an asymmetric Jacobian of the induced forces, vanishes at equilibrium and requires both nonzero chemical driving and spatial phase differences in the reactivities. This provides a mechanistically transparent derivation of non-reciprocal forces from a thermodynamically consistent chemo-mechanical coupling.

2605.06542v1.title: de Sitter Wavefunction from Quadrangular Polylogarithms: Chain Graphs

concepts.name: Cosmological Wavefunction in de Sitter Space
concepts.contribution: The paper derives the first explicit, closed-form expression for the n-site chain graph contribution to the cosmological wavefunction for conformally coupled φ³ theory in de Sitter space. This reduces what were previously complex nested integrals to a compact two-line formula expressed in terms of well-defined transcendental functions, valid for all n.

concepts.name: Cluster Algebras and Symbol Calculus
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the wavefunction coefficients for chain graphs satisfy a property stronger than cluster adjacency called total cluster compatibility, where every symbol letter in a given word must reside within a single cluster of the A₂ₙ₋₂ cluster algebra. This sharper constraint, absent in flat-space SYM amplitudes, is shown to be the defining structural feature organizing de Sitter cosmological observables.

concepts.name: Quadrangular Polylogarithms
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies the first direct physical application of Rudenko's quadrangular polylogarithms, mathematical objects previously studied only in pure mathematics in the context of Goncharov's depth conjecture and hyperbolic volumes. It proves that these functions form a natural and complete basis for de Sitter chain wavefunction coefficients by directly matching their coproduct structure to the recursive differential equations satisfied by the wavefunctions.

concepts.name: Multiple Polylogarithms and Hopf Algebra Coproduct
concepts.contribution: The paper exploits the Hopf algebra coproduct structure of multiple polylogarithms, specifically the (n−1,1) coproduct component encoding total differentials, as the central proof mechanism. By rewriting the known recursion relations for wavefunction coefficients in terms of cluster cross-ratios, the authors show it maps exactly onto Rudenko's coproduct formula for quadrangular polylogarithms, enabling an all-n inductive proof.

concepts.name: Threshold Bound States in Quantum Mechanics
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes sharp necessary and sufficient conditions on the potential V for a Schrödinger operator to possess a zero-energy bound state at the threshold of the essential spectrum with a finite c-th position moment. This extends previous existence results by precisely characterizing how the spatial localization of threshold eigenstates depends on the asymptotic behavior of the potential, showing that only potentials with a leading 1/|x|² term can produce eigenstates where only some moments are finite while others are infinite.

concepts.name: Spatial Localization and Position Moments of Eigenstates
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a rigorous framework for quantifying the spatial localization of threshold eigenstates beyond simple square-integrability, by analyzing the finiteness of the c-th moment ⟨ψ, |x|^c ψ⟩ for arbitrary c ≥ 0. It demonstrates that the critical potential coefficient in front of 1/|x|² directly controls which moments are finite, with the example potential showing that the c-th moment is finite if and only if c < 2(α − 1) for the parameter α characterizing the potential strength.

concepts.name: Critical and Subcritical Potentials
concepts.contribution: The paper refines the theory of critical potentials by linking criticality to the existence of threshold eigenstates with controlled moment properties, showing that for critical potentials any attractive perturbation creates a negative-energy bound state. The sharp potential bounds derived (involving iterated logarithm corrections to the leading 1/|x|² term) delineate the boundary between potentials that do and do not support threshold states with finite c-th moment, revealing a dimensional phase transition at d = 4.

concepts.name: Subharmonic Comparison Principle for Schrödinger Operators
concepts.contribution: The paper systematically applies Agmon's quadratic-form version of the subharmonic comparison principle to derive both the absence and existence of threshold eigenstates with prescribed moment properties. By constructing explicit auxiliary functions that barely fail or barely satisfy finiteness of the c-th moment, and using them as comparison sub- and supersolutions, the paper converts spectral questions about moment finiteness into pointwise comparison estimates.

2605.06497v1.title: The Hagedorn Temperature as a Nonequilibrium Dynamical Bottleneck in String Thermodynamics

concepts.name: Hagedorn Temperature
concepts.contribution: The paper reinterprets the Hagedorn temperature not merely as an equilibrium singularity of the canonical partition function, but as a nonequilibrium dynamical bottleneck in the evolution of the effective inverse temperature. It shows that the exponential growth of the string density of states broadens the energy distribution, suppressing the scalar dynamics of the intensive variable and causing the system to slow its approach to the Hagedorn scale. Crucially, the strength of this bottleneck is shown to depend on the algebraic prefactor exponent 'a' in the density of states, not just the exponential factor.

concepts.name: Steepest-Entropy-Ascent Quantum Thermodynamics (SEAQT)
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the SEAQT framework to string-theoretic systems by using the string density of states as the microscopic input for the dissipative metric and state manifold. It derives an exact scalar evolution equation for the instantaneous inverse temperature, expressed as a ratio of covariance to variance of the Hamiltonian, and identifies both classical-like higher-order fluctuation moment contributions and genuinely quantum noncommutative corrections from the Fréchet derivative of the operator logarithm. An open-system extension via a block-diagonal system–reservoir metric splitting is also developed, yielding a reduced subsystem dynamics driven by a reservoir inverse temperature.

concepts.name: String Density of States and Thermodynamic Fluctuations
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a careful construction of the multi-string microcanonical density of states, emphasizing that while the exponential Hagedorn growth is universal, the algebraic power-law prefactor is model-dependent and encodes compactification and conservation-law data. It then directly connects this density of states to the fluctuation moments governing nonequilibrium thermodynamic evolution, showing that the variance of the energy diverges near the Hagedorn boundary for exponents 'a' ≤ 3, producing a divergent thermodynamic inertia for the intensive variable in those cases.

concepts.name: Swampland Distance Conjecture
concepts.contribution: The paper proposes a structural analogy between the Hagedorn dynamical bottleneck and the Swampland Distance Conjecture, arguing that both phenomena reflect the onset of an overwhelmingly large stringy sector that obstructs naive continuation of the original effective description. In the thermodynamic language developed here, the exponentially growing tower of states associated with infinite-distance limits manifests as a strongly enhanced, potentially diverging thermodynamic inertia that pins the subsystem inverse temperature near the critical string scale. The authors are careful to characterize this connection as a structural analogy rather than a theorem, noting the distinct physical settings of the two phenomena.

2605.06473v1.title: Engineering a driven-dissipative bath of altermagnetic quantum magnons for controlling classical dynamics of spins hosting spin waves, domain walls, or skyrmions

concepts.name: Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) Equation and Magnetization Damping
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a significantly extended LLG equation containing two additional damping terms beyond the standard Gilbert damping: one that is spatially nonlocal and Markovian (a field-like torque characterized by Λnn′), and one that is both spatially nonlocal and non-Markovian (a memory kernel ηnn′(t,t′)). Unlike prior extensions that could be Taylor-expanded to yield local inertia terms, the non-Markovian term here must be handled numerically in full, representing a qualitatively new regime of magnetization dissipation engineering.

concepts.name: Schwinger-Keldysh Field Theory (SKFT) for Open Quantum-Classical Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper applies SKFT to a hybrid bilayer system where quantum localized spins (in the altermagnetic insulator layer) act as a bath for classical localized spins (in the ferromagnetic insulator layer), filling a theoretical gap for mixed quantum-classical magnetic systems. By integrating out the bosonic magnon bath to second order in the interlayer coupling JI, the authors obtain a closed-form effective action whose saddle-point equation yields the extended LLG equation with all bath-induced terms expressed analytically in terms of AMI Green's functions and magnon distribution functions.

concepts.name: Altermagnetism and Altermagnetic Magnons
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces an altermagnetic insulator as a practical, controllable dissipative bath whose chiral magnons exhibit d-wave momentum-space spin splitting, imprinting spatial anisotropy directly onto the nonlocal damping functions acting on the adjacent ferromagnet. It further demonstrates that driving the AMI layer out of equilibrium dramatically extends the spatial range of the nonlocal coupling function Λnn′ and that the d-wave anisotropy of this function is directly observable in the direction-dependent dynamics of domain walls and skyrmions.

concepts.name: Magnetic Soliton Dynamics (Spin Waves, Domain Walls, Skyrmions)
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that the AMI-induced nonlocal and non-Markovian damping terms can be exploited to tune spin wave spectra (including hybridization-induced spectral spikes and anisotropic damping), controllably accelerate or decelerate domain wall propagation depending on drive frequency and propagation direction, and induce skyrmion annihilation through many-body bath interactions rather than static disorder. Notably, driven nonequilibrium AMI magnons are shown to overcome the topological protection of skyrmions, offering a new mechanism for skyrmion erasure relevant to memory applications.

2605.06465v1.title: Non-planar corrections in the symmetric orbifold

concepts.name: Non-planar corrections and 1/N expansion in orbifold CFTs
concepts.contribution: The paper computes the subleading 1/N corrections to anomalous dimensions of quarter-BPS states in the symmetric product orbifold Sym^N(T^4), arising from intermediate multi-cycle twisted sectors. It demonstrates that these non-planar contributions lift degeneracies in the spectrum that persist to all orders in the planar (large-N) limit, even in the large-twist limit where the planar spectra of bosonic and fermionic states become identical.

concepts.name: Integrability and its breakdown in AdS3/CFT2
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes that the integrable structure found in the planar limit of the deformed symmetric orbifold—manifested as an integrable S-matrix and additional spectral degeneracies—is broken by 1/N corrections. The structural differences in how supercharges act on bosonic versus fermionic states at the non-planar level provide a concrete mechanism for why the planar degeneracy is not restored in the large-twist limit, indicating integrability is only a large-N phenomenon.

concepts.name: Quantum chaos and random matrix statistics in holographic systems
concepts.contribution: The paper provides evidence for a transition from integrable to chaotic behavior driven by non-planar effects: the planar level-spacing distribution follows Poisson statistics (characteristic of integrable systems), while the non-planar corrections exhibit level repulsion consistent with Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble random matrix theory, particularly for fermionic states. This links finite-N corrections in the orbifold CFT to the expected chaotic properties of black holes in the dual AdS3 geometry.

concepts.name: Covering map methods for symmetric orbifold correlators
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the Lunin-Mathur covering surface technique to compute three-point functions involving multi-cycle twist operators, using an explicit polynomial covering map for the w-cycle to (w-k, k) transitions. It shows that magnon-number-violating transitions to higher-magnon intermediate states, suppressed only by the short cycle length k rather than the full twist w, play a more significant role in non-planar corrections than in the planar case.

2605.06461v1.title: Quantum spin dynamics of heavy quarks and polarization observables in relativistic heavy-ion collisions

concepts.name: Quantum Spin Density Matrix Formalism
concepts.contribution: The paper develops a spin-1/2 density matrix framework specifically for heavy-quark spin dynamics in a QCD medium, deriving an explicit evolution equation with time-dependent spin-flip transition rates. Analytic solutions are obtained both for the general time-dependent case and the constant equal-rate limit, yielding an exponential decay of polarization toward an equilibrium value. This quantum formulation is shown to be consistent at leading order with prior classical stochastic (rotational Brownian motion) treatments, providing a firmer theoretical foundation.

concepts.name: Vector Meson Spin Alignment (ρ₀₀)
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs the spin-alignment parameter ρ₀₀ at the hadron level by coupling the evolved heavy-quark spin density matrix to that of the light antiquark produced during fragmentation, introducing an anti-correlation parameter β to encode spin-transfer in the fragmentation process. It demonstrates that coalescence with an unpolarized medium antiquark cannot reproduce ρ₀₀ > 1/3, identifying fragmentation-based hadronization as necessary for the observed D*+ spin alignment. A two-parameter Bayesian fit to ALICE Pb–Pb data at √sNN = 5.02 TeV extracts an effective depolarization strength κ and spin-alignment amplitude A.

concepts.name: Heavy Quark Spin Relaxation in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a phenomenological spin-relaxation timescale τs governing how quickly an initial magnetically induced heavy-quark polarization is washed out by medium interactions, and extracts τs ≈ 0.5–1 fm/c from ALICE D*+ data for representative path-length scales. The same fitted depolarization parameter is used to provide benchmark predictions for Λc⁺ and Λ̄c⁻ polarization as a function of transverse momentum, demonstrating that polarization magnitude increases with pT due to shorter effective in-medium proper times. This establishes open heavy-flavor spin observables as quantitative probes of early-time spin relaxation dynamics.

concepts.name: Polarization Harmonics and Initial-State Geometry
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces azimuthal polarization harmonics arising from path-length-dependent spin depolarization in an anisotropic fireball, expanding the spin-alignment signal and baryon polarization to first order in the geometric eccentricities εn. It shows that the nth harmonic coefficient is proportional to εn/(n+2), directly linking measurable spin observables to the initial-state fireball geometry in a manner analogous to collective flow harmonics. Numerical estimates of the second harmonic p2 for both D*+ and Λc⁺ are provided using eccentricities from Monte Carlo Glauber calculations, demonstrating decreasing harmonic strength with increasing pT.

2605.06452v1.title: Tight Contraction Rates for Primitive Channels under Quantum $f$-Divergences

concepts.name: Strong Data-Processing Inequalities (SDPI) in Quantum Channels
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes tight contraction rates for primitive quantum channels under general quantum f-divergences, showing the asymptotic SDPI constant is upper bounded by any non-commutative χ²-divergence SDPI constant. It provides a sufficient condition for this bound to be tight using quantum detailed balance, extending previously known results beyond the commutative (classical) setting.

concepts.name: Quantum f-Divergences
concepts.contribution: The paper proves that quantum f-divergences satisfy a local reverse Pinsker inequality, establishing that near the stationary state these divergences are bounded above by the squared trace norm distance. This unifies the treatment of Petz, Matsumoto, and Hirche-Tomamichel f-divergences under a single framework, yielding new results for Matsumoto divergences and strengthening bounds for Petz divergences.

concepts.name: Quantum Detailed Balance and Primitive Quantum Channels
concepts.contribution: The paper leverages quantum detailed balance conditions to establish when the upper bound on contraction rates is tight in the non-commutative setting, generalizing the classical reversible Markov chain tightness condition. It identifies that channels satisfying f-detailed balance with respect to their stationary state are self-adjoint under an inner product defined by the quantum inversion operator, ensuring real spectra and exact multiplicativity of SDPI constants under channel composition.

concepts.name: Quantum Markov Chain Mixing and Convergence
concepts.contribution: The paper characterizes the exponential rate at which time-homogeneous primitive quantum channels contract toward their stationary state, establishing that this rate equals the second-largest eigenvalue of a symmetrized channel operator under detailed balance. The uniform convergence of iterated channels in operator norm is proven using quantum Doeblin coefficients, providing the technical foundation for the asymptotic analysis.

2605.06436v1.title: Criticality around the Spinodal Point of First-Order Quantum Phase Transitions

concepts.name: First-Order Quantum Phase Transitions (FOQPTs)
concepts.contribution: The paper challenges the conventional view that FOQPTs lack critical behavior by demonstrating that genuine quantum criticality and universal scaling can emerge near the quantum spinodal point where metastability disappears. It provides a microscopic theory showing that the FOQPT dynamics is governed by an emergent critical point, bridging the long-standing gap between FOQPT and SOQPT dynamics.

concepts.name: Quantum Spinodal Point and Metastability
concepts.contribution: The paper rigorously defines the quantum spinodal point using the framework of (Δ, R)-metastability, identifying it as the parameter value at which metastability disappears for the minimum local excitation range R. It shows that at this point, resonant zero-energy local excitations generate a degenerate, kinetically constrained Hilbert subspace with emergent discrete translational symmetry, providing a precise microscopic anchor for spinodal physics in short-range quantum models.

concepts.name: Kibble-Zurek Mechanism (KZM) and Finite-Time Scaling (FTS)
concepts.contribution: The paper extends KZM and FTS, traditionally associated with second-order phase transitions, to the nonequilibrium dynamics of FOQPTs by showing that the effective Hamiltonian projected onto the spinodal subspace exhibits a genuine SOQPT with Ising universality. Numerical simulations of the tilted Ising chain confirm power-law defect scaling nkink ~ v^0.52, consistent with the Ising universality class prediction of v^0.5, validating that KZM scaling in an FOQPT context is inherited from the emergent critical point.

concepts.name: Kinetically Constrained Models and Emergent Symmetry
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the constrained Hilbert subspace arising at the quantum spinodal point is structurally analogous to Rydberg blockade models, with an emergent discrete translational symmetry Zn determined by the interaction range ρ and local excitation size R via n = ρ + R. It shows that whether this emergent symmetry can be spontaneously broken—as in the tilted Ising chain yielding a PXP-type effective model with Z2 symmetry—or is precluded by pre-existing Hilbert space constraints—as in the staggered-field PXP model—determines the presence or absence of universal scaling, unifying diverse dynamical behaviors across different FOQPT systems.

2605.06430v1.title: Revisiting the multi-mode rhombus circuit as a biased-noise qubit

concepts.name: Biased-Noise Qubits
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the rhombus circuit, operated away from half-flux-quantum frustration, functions as a biased-noise qubit where localized phase-space wavefunctions yield strongly asymmetric error rates: T1 ≈ 500 µs relaxation time versus T_φ^R ≈ 90 ns dephasing time. This experimentally validates the biased-noise regime for an interferometer-based multi-mode superconducting circuit and connects it to tailored error-correction codes that exploit noise asymmetry.

concepts.name: Charge-Parity Protection in Superconducting Circuits
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that the multi-mode rhombus circuit can approximate a single-mode cos(2φ) element with charge-parity symmetry, particularly when a large shunt capacitor is placed across opposite nodes, squeezing the phase-space wavefunction and enforcing approximate π-phase-shift symmetry. It further demonstrates that perfect charge-parity protection is not optimal in practice because it leaves the qubit vulnerable to flux and quasiparticle noise at low frequencies, motivating the intentional symmetry-breaking 'soft-rhombus' design.

concepts.name: Flux Noise and Quasiparticle Tunneling as Relaxation Mechanisms
concepts.contribution: Through a combined multi-mode Fermi's golden rule analysis and experimental coherence measurements, the paper identifies 1/f flux noise and quasiparticle tunneling as the dominant T1-limiting mechanisms at low qubit frequencies near the frustration point, with flux noise amplitude quantified as A_Φ = 4 µΦ₀. It shows that raising the qubit frequency by introducing junction asymmetry simultaneously reduces the 1/f noise spectral density at the transition frequency and lowers the relevant matrix elements, pointing to an optimal operating regime of a few GHz.

concepts.name: Aharonov-Bohm Interference in Josephson Junction Arrays
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a detailed circuit-quantization treatment of how Aharonov-Bohm interference in the four-junction rhombus loop selectively suppresses single-Cooper-pair tunneling while allowing double-Cooper-pair co-tunneling at half-flux-quantum bias, connecting the multi-mode rhombus directly to the idealized cos(2φ) Hamiltonian. It also analyzes how intentional junction asymmetry degrades but does not eliminate this interference, producing the 'soft' version that retains partial Cooper-pair pairing with practical noise advantages.

2605.06429v1.title: $\mathsf{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$ Brownian motion and stochastic PDE on entire functions

concepts.name: Stochastic Differential Equations with Logarithmic Interaction
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs the full edge scaling limit of singular values of Brownian motion on GL_N(C) from general initial conditions, showing the limiting paths solve an infinite system of SDEs with singular log-interaction between particles. It establishes that the reciprocals of the zeros of the limiting characteristic polynomial satisfy an infinite-dimensional SDE system with Brownian-motion-driven noise and pairwise logarithmic repulsion. This extends prior results that required special initial conditions (the identity matrix) to arbitrary admissible initial data.

concepts.name: Stochastic Partial Differential Equations with Multiplicative Noise
concepts.contribution: The paper derives, apparently for the first time in the literature, a closed SPDE governing the evolution of the rescaled reverse characteristic polynomial of GL_N(C) Brownian motion in the large-N limit, featuring a nonlinear multiplicative martingale noise term and a linear drift involving second-order z-derivatives. The covariation structure of the martingale term is shown to have a form reminiscent of integrable operator kernels from random matrix theory. Analogous SPDEs are also derived for two additional models whose stationary measures are given by the Hua-Pickrell and Bessel stochastic zeta functions.

concepts.name: Gibbs Line Ensembles and Brownian Gibbs Property
concepts.contribution: The paper proves that the infinite-dimensional limiting line ensemble arising from GL_N(C) Brownian motion satisfies a Gibbs resampling property with respect to exponential Brownian bridges, extending this structural property from special to general initial conditions. A general abstract framework is developed for establishing the Gibbs property under scaling limits of finite-dimensional line ensembles associated with Doob h-transform Karlin-McGregor semigroups. This framework is shown to apply broadly to diffusion bridges beyond the standard Brownian bridge setting.

concepts.name: Stochastic Zeta Functions and Random Entire Functions
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs the first explicit dynamical models for the stochastic zeta functions associated with the Hua-Pickrell and Bessel point processes, realizing them as stationary measures of Feller diffusion processes on spaces of entire functions in the Laguerre-Polya class. The convergence to equilibrium is established, showing that the evolving random entire functions converge in distribution to the respective stochastic zeta functions as time tends to infinity. This opens a new dynamical avenue for studying properties of these random entire functions, including their Taylor coefficient moments, via the limiting SPDEs.

2605.06427v1.title: Multitime memory beyond the quantum regression theorem in sequential measurement statistics

concepts.name: Quantum Regression Theorem (QRT)
concepts.contribution: The paper derives an exact decomposition of the two-time propagator into a QRT-compliant term and a memory correction term that isolates all QRT violations into system-environment correlations across the measurement intervention. It further provides an explicit second-order perturbative correction to QRT predictions in the weak-coupling regime, expressed in terms of the reduced dynamical map and bath correlation functions, and validates this correction nonperturbatively against a pseudomode embedding of the spin-boson model.

concepts.name: Non-Markovianity in Open Quantum Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that multitime non-Markovianity, as witnessed by QRT violations in sequential measurement statistics, is inequivalent to one-time non-Markovianity defined via P-divisibility of the reduced dynamical map, showing parameter regimes where one quantifier detects memory while the other does not. It further shows that multitime memory is intrinsically protocol-dependent and can become visible only at higher temporal order, with three-time statistics revealing deviations invisible at the two-time level for certain measurement sequences.

concepts.name: Sequential Measurement Statistics in Open Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a Kolmogorov-distance-based operational quantifier of QRT breakdown directly defined on joint outcome probability distributions from sequential projective measurements, providing a practically computable and physically transparent measure of multitime memory. It systematically analyzes how this quantifier depends on spectral density parameters, environmental temperature, initial state preparation, and measurement basis choice, showing that the choice of protocol determines which temporal correlations encode non-Markovian signatures.

concepts.name: Pseudomode Embedding for Non-Markovian Dynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper employs pseudomode embedding of a Lorentzian spectral density as a nonperturbative, numerically exact reference for both reduced-state dynamics and multitime sequential probabilities, extending its use beyond one-time quantities to serve as a benchmark for QRT violations at two- and three-time levels. This allows rigorous validation of the perturbative second-order correction and enables comprehensive exploration of non-Markovian regimes inaccessible to standard weak-coupling approximations.

2605.06425v1.title: Comparative Study of Potts Machine Dynamics and Performance for Max-k-Cut

concepts.name: Potts Model
concepts.contribution: The paper provides the first systematic comparative benchmarking of analog continuous-time Potts machine implementations against each other and against Ising machines on Max-k-Cut problems. It reveals that current Potts machine dynamics implement the planar Potts Hamiltonian rather than the standard Potts Hamiltonian, and that this mismatch introduces an angular separation constraint that causes significant performance degradation for k≥4 states, a fundamental limitation not previously quantified.

concepts.name: Dynamical Systems and Bifurcation Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies and analyzes three dynamical properties—connected origin-to-solution branch, enforced amplitude homogeneity, and enforced phase discretization—through stability and fixed-point analysis of the governing ODEs. It demonstrates via Jacobian eigenvalue analysis how the origin destabilizes at coupling thresholds and how solution branches bifurcate with power-law amplitude scaling, connecting these dynamical features directly to empirical optimization performance.

concepts.name: Adiabatic Annealing in Analog Computing
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes a unified adiabatic annealing framework for comparing heterogeneous Potts machine models, showing that slow parameter variation allows systems to track evolving fixed-point structures. It demonstrates that the presence or absence of a connected origin-to-solution branch determines whether a model can be annealed adiabatically at all, since models like q-PDC require fast non-adiabatic annealing to escape a persistently stable origin.

concepts.name: Combinatorial Optimization on Graphs
concepts.contribution: The paper provides empirical evidence that the anticipated advantage of native multi-state encodings in Potts machines over one-hot-encoded Ising machines does not currently hold for Max-3-Cut or Max-4-Cut, with the Ising machine achieving roughly an order-of-magnitude smaller optimality gaps. It introduces two new machine models and quantifies the performance gap across 800-vertex GSet graphs and random graphs up to 50 vertices, providing concrete benchmarks to guide future hardware design.

2605.06424v1.title: Finite-Time Optimal Control by Noisy Traps

concepts.name: Finite-Time Optimal Control
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that finite-time optimality can emerge in purely passive Brownian systems when the controller itself is dissipative, without requiring an active probe. It identifies a critical fluctuation strength above which the unconstrained optimal protocol duration collapses to zero, and shows this transition is captured by a sign change in the linear-T coefficient of the short-time work expansion. Imposing an endpoint constraint removes this zero-time transition, revealing how the admissible control manifold shapes the optimization landscape.

concepts.name: Nonequilibrium Stochastic Thermodynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper extends stochastic thermodynamics to a setting where the controller violates detailed balance, generating sustained entropy production and probability currents even at fixed deterministic control parameters. It derives a modified work functional that includes an explicit contribution from stiffness fluctuations, showing that the probe-controller energy exchange fundamentally alters the thermodynamic cost of transport and stiffening protocols. This provides a concrete mechanism by which nonequilibrium control devices change the energetics of otherwise passive systems.

concepts.name: Overdamped Langevin Dynamics with Stochastic Trapping
concepts.contribution: The paper models a Brownian particle in a harmonic trap whose stiffness evolves as a continuous-time Markov chain, coupling probe and controller dynamics in a non-separable way. Using a multiscale fast-switching expansion, it derives closed-form moment equations and reduced work functionals that depend on the stiffness only through its mean and variance. This analytical framework is extended to both white-noise and exponentially correlated (active bath) forcing, revealing a noncommutativity between fast-stiffness and fast-noise limits that suppresses the zero-time transition.

concepts.name: Quasistatic Optimality and Its Breakdown
concepts.contribution: In classical equilibrium control, quasistatic (infinite-time) protocols minimize dissipation, but this paper shows that a dissipative controller breaks this principle even for passive probes. The noisy trap injects a positive work contribution linear in protocol duration T, which competes with the negative short-time deterministic contribution, selecting a non-trivial finite optimal duration. This generalizes the known breakdown of quasistatic optimality from active probes to passive probes under nonequilibrium control.

2605.06418v1.title: On the non-radial oscillations of realistic anisotropic neutron stars: Axial modes

concepts.name: Quasi-Normal Modes of Neutron Stars
concepts.contribution: The paper provides the first complete treatment of axial (odd-parity) quasi-normal modes for realistic anisotropic neutron stars, using three physically motivated equations of state. It demonstrates that the lower w-mode frequency decreases and damping time increases with stellar mass, with softer equations of state yielding slightly higher frequencies in the range 5–9 kHz and damping times of 20–250 µs.

concepts.name: Pressure Anisotropy in Compact Stars
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that pressure anisotropy (tangential pressure exceeding radial pressure) directly couples matter and metric perturbations in the axial sector, which does not occur in isotropic stars. It demonstrates that larger anisotropy supports more massive equilibrium configurations, shifting mode frequencies lower and prolonging damping times, with quantifiable differences from the isotropic limit.

concepts.name: Matter-Metric Perturbation Coupling
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes that in anisotropic neutron stars the axial fluid displacement vector cannot be decoupled from the metric perturbation, because the Lagrangian perturbation of the radial spacelike vector is geometrically constrained by both the metric variation and the fluid displacement. This coupling produces a non-zero source term in the generalized Regge-Wheeler equation and shifts the mode spectrum to significantly lower frequencies and longer damping times compared to treatments that artificially suppress this coupling.

concepts.name: Universal Relations in Gravitational-Wave Asteroseismology
concepts.contribution: The paper derives empirical universal relations showing that both the scaled oscillation frequency and scaled damping time of the axial w-modes follow a nearly quadratic dependence on stellar compactness, remaining largely insensitive to the equation of state and the specific anisotropy model. These EOS-independent relations provide a practical framework for inferring neutron star compactness from high-frequency gravitational-wave observations with third-generation detectors.

2605.06414v1.title: A Residual-Based Quantum Linear System Algorithm with Dynamic Stopping and Applications to Elliptic PDEs

concepts.name: Elliptic Partial Differential Equations
concepts.contribution: The paper reformulates the discretized elliptic PDE problem −∇·(a(x)∇u) = f as a stable first-order ODE dynamical system, exploiting the divergence–gradient factorization Ah = Gh†Gh to achieve square-root condition-number scaling O(h⁻¹) instead of the naive O(h⁻²). It demonstrates that the spectral content of the right-hand side f, not just the worst-case condition number κ(Ah) = Θ(h⁻²), governs the practical solver cost, providing numerical evidence on a 2D Poisson problem.

concepts.name: Quantum Simulation of Non-Unitary Dynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs a non-unitary ODE generator Lh whose Hermitian part scales as O(h⁻¹) while the non-Hermitian damping scales as O(1), enabling efficient dilation to a Schrödinger equation via existing frameworks such as LCHS and Schrödинgeristion. By embedding residual variables directly into the dilated quantum dynamics, the residual block becomes a physically measurable register whose probability pres(t) serves as an on-the-fly convergence indicator without reconstructing the full solution state.

concepts.name: Quantum Linear Systems Algorithms
concepts.contribution: Rather than improving worst-case complexity bounds, the paper introduces an a posteriori residual-based dynamic stopping mechanism—analogous to classical iterative solver residual checks—into the QLSA framework, something previously absent. The constant-threshold checkpoint scheme requires only O(log(K/ν)) samples per checkpoint time, avoiding the O(ε⁻²) sampling cost that would arise from directly estimating an ε²-probability event, while the final precision is guaranteed by a deterministic coasting time Δt = O(log(1/ε)).

concepts.name: Finite Element Methods
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that the Gram factorization Ah = Gh†Gh arising naturally from Galerkin finite element discretizations provides sparse-access block encodings of the first-order gradient operator Gh with normalization αG = O(h⁻¹), directly supplying the square-root condition-number scaling needed for efficient quantum simulation. It establishes that this factorization can be assembled locally from element quadrature data, making the quantum oracle compatible with standard finite element assembly without requiring a preassembled global stiffness matrix.

2605.06412v1.title: GTMDs, orbital angular momentum, and pretzelosity

concepts.name: Generalized Transverse Momentum Dependent Parton Distributions (GTMDs)
concepts.contribution: The paper derives explicit bag model expressions for all four leading GTMDs F1,1, F1,2, F1,3, and F1,4 associated with the Dirac structure γ+ in the large-Nc limit, with F1,1, F1,2, and F1,3 being new results for this model. The theoretical consistency of these expressions is demonstrated by verifying Hermiticity properties and confirming correct reduction to known TMDs and GPDs in appropriate limits.

concepts.name: Parton Orbital Angular Momentum
concepts.contribution: The paper provides analytical proofs of both the Jaffe-Manohar and Ji sum rules for quark orbital angular momentum in the bag model, revealing a fundamental structural difference between them: the Jaffe-Manohar sum rule follows from quark wave function normalization alone, while the Ji sum rule additionally requires explicit use of the equation of motion and the virial theorem, invoking the full dynamics of the model. Numerical results show quarks carry approximately 35% of the nucleon spin as orbital angular momentum at low hadronic scales.

concepts.name: Pretzelosity TMD
