concepts.contribution: The paper deepens the known model-dependent relationship between pretzelosity h⊥1T and orbital angular momentum by showing it holds at the level of the x-integrands, not merely after integration. Furthermore, the paper extends this connection to the full five-variable GTMD level by demonstrating that Hq1,4 = 2Fq1,4 holds for all values of x, ξ, kT, and ΔT in the bag model, revealing that pretzelosity is connected to orbital angular momentum because these two GTMDs are proportional as complete functions rather than only in limiting cases.

2605.06410v1.title: Spin and Quadrupole Sectors in Nonrelativistic Gravity

concepts.name: Large-c (1/c) expansion of general relativity
concepts.contribution: The paper develops a unified ω-expansion of the ADM formulation that simultaneously encodes both the Galilean (large-c) and Carrollian (small-c) limits of general relativity from a single starting point. It derives the Galilean ADM action and Hamilton field equations systematically through next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO), extending previous NLO treatments to include nonlinear corrections essential for going beyond the leading nonrelativistic regime.

concepts.name: Nonrelativistic gravity and Newton-Cartan geometry
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies explicit stationary vacuum solutions of Galilean nonrelativistic gravity in ADM variables, showing how rotating (Kerr-type) and multipolar (Hartle-Thorne-type) relativistic geometries are encoded in the Galilean expansion fields. It confirms that the NLO Galilean ADM theory reproduces Galilean-invariant nonrelativistic gravity and provides a direct ADM-gauge form of the Hansen-Hartong-Obers non-relativistic gravity action.

concepts.name: Spin-quadrupole coupling in stationary axisymmetric spacetimes
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that at NNLO the naive superposition of the Kerr-type spin sector and the Hartle-Thorne-type quadrupole sector fails because nonlinear source terms proportional to J²Q are generated by the field equations. It derives the specific corrections to the lapse and spatial tensor required to cancel these mixed spin-quadrupole residuals, producing a new post-linear mixed weak-branch solution in ADM gauge.

concepts.name: ADM formalism for compact object spacetimes
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs both weak-branch and strong-branch stationary solutions in ADM variables, where the strong branch is organized around a nontrivial Schwarzschild-type leading geometry and naturally captures strong-field effects such as frame dragging starting at order c⁰. It provides explicit read-off maps between ADM expansion data and the metric components of the Kerr and Hartle-Thorne spacetimes, enabling reconstruction of approximate spacetime metrics that include spin, quadrupole, and mixed spin-quadrupole effects relevant to black holes and neutron stars.

2605.06399v1.title: A polar-factor retraction on the symplectic Stiefel manifold with closed-form inverse

concepts.name: Symplectic Geometry and Hamiltonian Mechanics
concepts.contribution: The paper works directly with the symplectic Stiefel manifold, whose elements form symplectic bases for subspaces of the standard symplectic vector space, a structure central to Hamiltonian mechanics. It introduces a new retraction built on the symplectic polar decomposition, providing an efficient way to move between the manifold and its tangent space while preserving the symplectic structure. This advances the computational toolkit for problems in Hamiltonian and symplectic systems, including symplectic model reduction of Hamiltonian systems referenced in the work.

concepts.name: Symplectic Model Reduction
concepts.contribution: Symplectic model reduction seeks to compress large Hamiltonian systems while preserving their geometric structure, and requires efficient parameterization of the symplectic Stiefel manifold. The new retraction with a closed-form inverse enables both the forward mapping needed in optimization and the reverse mapping needed for interpolation and averaging of reduced bases. This directly addresses a computational bottleneck in structure-preserving model reduction of physical simulations.

concepts.name: Structure-Preserving Numerical Methods
concepts.contribution: The paper contributes a numerically feasible retraction that explicitly maintains symplectic constraints throughout computation, using Hamiltonian and skew-Hamiltonian matrix structures in both forward and inverse directions. By employing the Cayley transformation as a numerically stable substitute for the matrix exponential, the method preserves the symplectic group structure at each computational step. This extends the class of structure-preserving algorithms available for physical problems governed by symplectic geometry.

2605.06397v1.title: Photonic-Implemented Efficient Deep Quantum Neural Network via Virtual-Driven Hilbert Space Expansion

concepts.name: Hilbert Space Expansion in Quantum Computing
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a method of virtual-driven Hilbert space expansion via input state replication and optical mode extension, creating an ancillary computational space without requiring additional physical qubits. This allows non-unitary transformations to be induced through partial measurement on the expanded space, circumventing the standard resource costs of ancillary qubit schemes. The approach demonstrates that effective dimensionality scaling can be achieved on a linear photonic platform by exploiting photons' multiple degrees of freedom.

concepts.name: Non-Unitary Quantum Operations in Linear Optics
concepts.contribution: The paper addresses the fundamental challenge of implementing non-unitary and nonlinear operations within an inherently linear quantum photonic system, where photon-photon interactions are negligible. It proposes the multivalue-controlled RY (MCRY) module, which uses path-degree-of-freedom expansion and post-selection to realize controlled non-unitary gates without probabilistic multi-qubit gate failures or mid-circuit measurements. This substantially improves the cascadability and success probability of deep quantum neural network layers compared to prior ancillary qubit or feedback-based methods.

concepts.name: Quantum Generative Modeling
concepts.contribution: The paper provides the first experimental demonstration of a quantum generative diffusion model (QGDM) running on a real quantum hardware device, used here to prepare quantum Gibbs states. By leveraging the ADE-QNN's enhanced non-unitary expressivity, the architecture achieves near-unity fidelity Gibbs state reconstruction in a single diffusion step, outperforming standard QNN baselines that require multiple steps. This establishes a practical pathway for quantum generative models to tackle problems in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics that are intractable classically.

concepts.name: Integrated Silicon Photonic Quantum Circuits
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates a 1.8×8 mm² silicon-on-chip device fabricated via CMOS technology that monolithically integrates four bidirectionally pumped entangled photon-pair sources, 109 thermo-optic phase shifters, and a high-dimensional programmable interferometric network. High-quality metrics are validated, including a mean Hong-Ou-Mandel visibility of 0.928 within sources and 0.964 across source pairs, confirming photon indistinguishability sufficient for multi-qubit interference. This hardware realization demonstrates that scalable, room-temperature, low-decoherence photonic platforms can support deep quantum neural network architectures with multiple entanglement layers.

2605.06396v1.title: Dynamical cooling driven by self-similar fronts in the 2D nonlinear Schrödinger model

concepts.name: Wave Turbulence and Wave Kinetic Equations
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the wave-kinetic equation (WKE) for the 2D defocusing NLS model admits a non-equilibrium cooling process driven by self-similar fronts, rather than a simple relaxation to a finite-temperature Rayleigh-Jeans equilibrium. It establishes that the evolving spectrum partitions into distinct similarity ranges—a quasi-thermal core and an ultraviolet self-similar tail—and derives the algebraic front propagation law ω+(t) ∝ t^(1/3) directly from energy conservation within the WKE framework.

concepts.name: Self-Similar Solutions and Blowup Theory in Nonlinear PDEs
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies three coexisting kinds of self-similar behavior (first-, and two instances of third-kind) governing different spectral regions of the cooling wave system, extending the classification beyond the standard first/second-kind dichotomy. It shows that infrared and bulk self-similarities inherit their scaling exponents by matching to adjacent self-similar regions rather than from conservation laws or nonlinear eigenvalue problems, providing a concrete physical realization of third-kind self-similarity previously identified only in model turbulence problems.

concepts.name: Thermalization and the Ultraviolet Catastrophe in Classical Wave Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper frames the dynamics of the 2D NLS as a dynamical analog of the ultraviolet catastrophe, where the only valid equilibrium for a finite-energy system is the zero-temperature Rayleigh-Jeans state. It quantifies the effective cooling laws T(t) ∝ t^(-1/3) and ln μ(t) ∝ -t^(1/3), showing these emerge universally from both direct NLS simulations and the differential approximation model, and clarifies that the apparent thermalization is a transient quasi-equilibrium rather than true equilibrium.

concepts.name: Differential Approximation Models (DAM) for Wave Kinetics
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the fourth-order differential approximation model (DAM), derived under the super-local interaction hypothesis, captures the essential self-similar dynamics of the full WKE while enabling access to a much wider dynamic range and cleaner numerical analysis. It also identifies a key qualitative difference from the full WKE: the DAM produces a sharp propagating infrared front absent in the NLS/WKE system, which is explained by the DAM's inability to represent the nonlocal interactions that produce an instantaneous low-frequency plateau in the true dynamics.

2605.06394v1.title: Lecture Notes on Statistical Physics and Neural Networks

concepts.name: Boltzmann-Gibbs Distribution
concepts.contribution: The paper reframes the Boltzmann-Gibbs distribution purely as a branch of probability theory, deliberately stripping away physical intuition so that readers without physics backgrounds can engage with it. It treats temperature and energy as abstract mathematical parameters rather than physical quantities, and derives thermodynamic potentials such as free energy and entropy directly from the partition function on finite configuration spaces. This framing makes the formalism immediately portable to neural network contexts like Hopfield networks and Boltzmann machines.

concepts.name: Renormalization Group
concepts.contribution: The paper presents the renormalization group as a procedure of marginalizing probability distributions by summing over (integrating out) subsets of degrees of freedom, worked out explicitly for both the 1D and 2D Ising models. It derives scaling laws and critical exponents directly from the existence of non-trivial RG fixed points with relevant perturbations, making the connection between fixed-point stability and second-order phase transitions concrete and accessible. Crucially, it draws a formal analogy between this RG integration procedure and the way hidden neurons are integrated out in restricted Boltzmann machines, providing a unifying conceptual bridge between statistical physics and machine learning.

concepts.name: Spin-Glass Models and Hopfield Networks
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes an explicit mathematical identification between the energy function of spin-glass models and the energy function governing Hopfield network dynamics, showing that renaming Ising spins as neurons and coupling constants as weights yields the same formalism. It uses this correspondence to explain associative memory in Hopfield networks as the rich ground-state structure of frustrated spin glasses. This connection motivates the probabilistic generalization to Boltzmann machines, where thermodynamic equilibrium in the spin-glass sense corresponds to the learned probability distribution over neural configurations.

concepts.name: Scaling Laws in Deep Learning
concepts.contribution: The paper draws an explicit analogy between the power-law scaling of observables near a critical temperature in statistical physics and the empirically observed power-law dependence of large language model training loss on parameters, data size, and compute. It notes that both exhibit a form of universality largely independent of microscopic details, suggesting that the theoretical machinery of critical phenomena and the renormalization group could potentially provide a framework for understanding LLM scaling laws. This is presented as an open research direction rather than a completed theory, framing it as motivation for applying statistical field theory methods to deep learning.

2605.06379v1.title: Systematic Extraction of Exact Yang-Mills Solutions via Algebraic Tensor Ring Decomposition

concepts.name: Exact Classical Solutions in Non-Abelian Yang-Mills Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces an algebraic tensor ring decomposition framework that systematically maps the nonlinear Yang-Mills PDEs into differential-algebraic systems, enabling the extraction of three new classes of exact solutions: relativistic SU(2) color waves, dynamical dyonic flux tubes, and SU(3) chaotic resonances. By treating pure-gauge backgrounds as dynamical geometric templates whose Maurer-Cartan forms generate necessary nonlinear cross-terms, the method overcomes the overdetermination that typically plagues generalized ansätze. This extends beyond traditional symmetry-reduction approaches by capturing asymmetrically coupled configurations that those methods preclude.

concepts.name: Dynamical Mass Gap Generation
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates analytically that nonlinear self-interactions in the coupled color wave branches enforce a timelike dispersion relation, generating an effective classical mass parameter meff proportional to (ω²−k²)^(−1/2) that confines stable solutions to the timelike region. Through semiclassical Background Field Method quantization, this classical condensate is shown to produce a quantum mass gap MQ ∝ g·meff via the gluon mass matrix, providing an analytical bridge between classical wave solutions and the dynamically generated mass gap observed in lattice QCD and Dyson-Schwinger studies. The algebraic bifurcation structure reveals that mass gap generation is tied specifically to branches with nonzero longitudinal Cartan deformation.

concepts.name: Savvidy Vacuum Instability and Tachyonic Suppression
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that each class of extracted solution structurally evades the Nielsen-Olesen tachyonic instability that afflicts constant magnetic background models through distinct physical mechanisms. For color waves, the spin-magnetic coupling matrix has strictly zero spacetime average because the Jacobi elliptic envelope has vanishing mean, mapping fluctuation dynamics onto a stable Mathieu equation rather than exponentially growing modes. For the flux tube, explicit calculation shows that the tachyonic spin-magnetic eigenvalues decay exponentially as modified Bessel functions at large radius, proving the instability is confined to the flux tube core and completely suppressed in the asymptotic vacuum.

concepts.name: Topological Solitons and Derrick's Theorem Evasion
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs dynamical helical flux tube configurations in SU(2) Yang-Mills theory that evade Derrick's no-go theorem without introducing external scalar fields, instead injecting time dependence through a temporal phase ω in the geometric template. The Gauss law ideal performs a topological bifurcation into four branches, with the Meissner branch yielding Bessel-type exponential screening of color-magnetic flux stabilized by a temporal dominance condition M²= Ω²∞−W̃²∞> 0. This provides a classical realization of the dyonic dual-superconductor confinement picture, where the temporal Cartan deformation supplies the positive effective mass that the static BPS reduction cannot provide.

2605.06372v1.title: Coherence limitations of a Fourier-engineered $\cos(2\varphi)$ transmon qubit

concepts.name: Cooper-pair parity symmetry and charge noise protection
concepts.contribution: The paper experimentally demonstrates that a Fourier-engineered multi-junction circuit can suppress odd harmonics of the Josephson potential to realize an effective cos(2φ) potential, which conserves Cooper-pair parity and thereby decouples the qubit from single-electron charge noise. The authors confirm the suppression of charge matrix elements between ground and excited states as the circuit is tuned toward the protected regime, validating the theoretical mechanism of parity-based protection against energy relaxation.

concepts.name: Fourier engineering of Josephson energy-phase relations
concepts.contribution: The paper implements a practical interference-based architecture using conventional SIS Josephson junctions in series to synthesize an SNS-like energy-phase relation with controllable higher harmonics, demonstrating continuous tunability between a transmon-like potential and a double-well cos(2φ) potential via external flux. This establishes that higher-harmonic engineering with standard aluminum junctions is a viable fabrication route, avoiding the need for more complex semiconductor-superconductor hybrid junctions.

concepts.name: 1/f flux noise as a decoherence mechanism in superconducting qubits
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies that the dominant coherence limitation of the interference-based cos(2φ) qubit at its flux symmetry point is 1/f flux noise, arising because the large Josephson energy scale (~40 GHz) of each SQUID arm sets the sensitivity prefactor for residual first-harmonic fluctuations even after nominal cancellation. By comparing with a fluxonium qubit using identical noise parameters, the authors show that the fluxonium's much smaller inductive energy scale (~0.8 GHz) yields a predicted lifetime two orders of magnitude longer, identifying the energy-scale mismatch as a fundamental challenge for interference-based protection schemes.

concepts.name: Effective single-mode Hamiltonians for multi-junction superconducting circuits
concepts.contribution: The paper validates a Born-Oppenheimer-inspired effective Hamiltonian that reduces the multi-junction circuit to a single phase variable while incorporating corrections from internal mode charging energies, showing excellent agreement with measured transition spectra across multiple flux bias conditions. This demonstrates that the simplified effective model is sufficient to capture the essential physics of the Fourier-engineered circuit, including the emergence of higher harmonics and the double-well potential structure, without requiring full treatment of all junction degrees of freedom.

2605.06321v1.title: Gravitational Lensing of Gravitational Waves from Astrophysical Sources: Theory, Detection, and Applications

concepts.name: Gravitational Wave Lensing Regimes (Geometric vs. Wave Optics)
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a unified theoretical framework distinguishing geometric-optics lensing (λ_GW ≪ λ_E), which produces multiple time-delayed, magnified images, from wave-optics lensing (λ_GW ≳ λ_E), which produces frequency-dependent amplification and phase shifts via diffraction. It derives the Kirchhoff diffraction integral for the amplification factor F(f) and shows explicitly how the geometric-optics limit emerges as stationary-phase contributions in the short-wavelength limit. The paper also identifies computational challenges in evaluating F(f) for non-axisymmetric lenses and for GWs propagating past black holes, where full numerical relativity is required.

concepts.name: Standard Sirens and Hubble Constant Measurement
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces two lensing-based cosmological methods — 'Bright Lensed Sirens,' which combine GW time-delay measurements with EM counterpart localizations to reconstruct the lensing potential, and 'Dark Lensed Sirens,' which use GW-only data from multiply imaged events to achieve sub-arcsecond source relocalization without EM counterparts. It quantifies that approximately 10 bright lensed siren events with third-generation detectors can constrain H0 to ~0.68% precision, while dark lensed sirens can achieve sub-1% precision within roughly two years, offering an independent probe of the Hubble tension at higher redshifts than conventional distance ladders.

concepts.name: Dark Matter Structure Probed via Gravitational Lensing
concepts.contribution: The paper details how diffractive lensing of GWs by dark matter minihalos (10^3–10^6 M☉) is sensitive to the halo density profile, distinguishing cold dark matter (NFW cusps), self-interacting dark matter (core profiles), and warm dark matter (suppressed low-mass halo abundance). It reports predicted detection rates spanning many orders of magnitude across detector generations — from ~10^-7 yr^-1 for LIGO A+ to ~189 yr^-1 for BBO under CDM — and shows that DECIGO and BBO would have sufficient sensitivity to discriminate between dark matter models, while also discussing how PBH abundance and mass can be constrained through lensing signatures.

concepts.name: Detection Rate Estimation and Search Strategies for Lensed GW Events
concepts.contribution: The paper compiles and reconciles predicted lensed GW detection rates across source types (sBBH, BNS, BHNS, SMBBH) and detector generations, showing that third-generation detectors like ET and CE should yield tens to hundreds of lensed CBC events per year. It reviews search methodologies including posterior-overlap Bayes factors, joint parameter estimation pipelines (GOLUM, HANABI), sub-threshold image searches, and microlensing waveform template matching, and quantifies false-alarm probabilities — finding that pairwise FAP of ~10^-5–10^-6 for current LVK improves to ~10^-8–10^-10 for third-generation networks, making confident lensing detections feasible in the coming decade.

2605.06312v1.title: Ablation Removal of Transport-Blocking Defects in Surface-Electrode Ion Traps

concepts.name: Ion Micromotion in Paul Traps
concepts.contribution: The paper provides spatially resolved micromotion measurements along a shuttling trajectory before and after defect removal, quantifying how a ~65 µm particulate contaminant induces a quadratically growing RF pseudopotential distortion that ultimately forces ion loss. Post-ablation measurements confirm that residual micromotion at the defect site corresponds to a maximum ion displacement of ~1.5 µm and a peak compensation field of ~88.95 V/m, both within operationally acceptable bounds, establishing a practical threshold criterion for defect-remediated trap regions.

concepts.name: Pulsed Laser Ablation
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates selective nanosecond-pulsed laser ablation (532 nm, 1.5 ns, up to 6.8 J/cm²) as a precision tool for removing discrete, macroscopic particulate defects from microfabricated electrode surfaces inside an ultra-high vacuum cryogenic system without damaging surrounding gold electrodes. By combining a co-aligned CW guide laser with a beam-expanding telescope and a motorized focusing stage, the authors achieve spatially confined fluence delivery sufficient to ablate the target while keeping fluence on neighboring electrodes well below the ~1–4 J/cm² gold damage threshold.

concepts.name: Ion Transport and Shuttling in Surface-Electrode Traps
concepts.contribution: The paper directly quantifies transport reliability before and after defect remediation, reporting a transition from 100% shuttling failure across >300 trials to a round-trip error rate of ≤1.3×10⁻⁴ across 22,500 trials following ablation. This establishes in situ laser ablation as a viable maintenance technique for preserving transport-channel integrity in multi-zone and modular ion-trap architectures where even a single obstruction halts all downstream quantum operations.

concepts.name: Surface Contamination and Defect Formation in Microfabricated Ion Traps
concepts.contribution: The paper characterizes a ~65 µm × 40 µm transport-blocking particulate defect originating after the bakeout procedure, identified via high-resolution imaging and a scanned guide-laser profilometry technique using an EMCCD camera. This extends prior work on adsorbed monolayer contaminants by addressing the largely neglected regime of large discrete particulates, providing both a diagnostic method and a remediation strategy specifically suited to defects of this scale and origin.

2605.06297v1.title: Macroscopic entanglement between two magnon modes via two-tone driving of a superconducting qubit

concepts.name: Macroscopic Quantum Entanglement
concepts.contribution: This paper demonstrates a protocol for generating entanglement between two magnon modes in millimeter-sized YIG spheres, each containing more than 10^18 spins, representing a genuinely macroscopic quantum state. By achieving a maximum logarithmic negativity of approximately 0.7 using experimentally available parameters, it pushes the boundary of quantum entanglement into the truly macroscopic regime. This advance provides a new testbed for foundational questions such as the Schrödinger's cat paradox, quantum-to-classical transition, and unconventional decoherence theories.

concepts.name: Two-Mode Squeezing Interaction
concepts.contribution: The paper shows how a two-tone microwave drive applied to a superconducting qubit can engineer an effective magnonic two-mode squeezing Hamiltonian of the form g_eff(m†_1 m†_2 + m_1 m_2)σ_z through a sequence of rotating-wave approximations and adiabatic elimination. This indirect, qubit-mediated route to two-mode squeezing is distinct from direct parametric driving approaches and does not require optical fields or magnetostrictive coupling. The effective coupling strength g_eff is analytically derived and shown to be tunable via the drive frequencies and amplitudes.

concepts.name: Adiabatic Elimination and Effective Hamiltonian Derivation
concepts.contribution: The paper applies adiabatic elimination of a far-detuned microwave cavity to reduce a full three-body cavity–magnon–qubit Hamiltonian to an effective magnon–qubit system, and then further employs the James–Jerke effective Hamiltonian formula to eliminate fast-oscillating terms and arrive at a time-independent squeezing interaction. This multi-stage perturbative reduction provides a clear analytical framework linking the physical drive parameters to the emergent entangling interaction. The validity of each approximation step is numerically verified by comparing dynamics from the original and effective Hamiltonians.

concepts.name: Quantum State Tomography via Dispersive Coupling
concepts.contribution: The paper proposes a complete detection scheme for verifying magnon–magnon entanglement by measuring the joint Wigner function of the two magnon modes using the dispersive coupling between the qubit and each magnon mode. Displacement operations are applied independently to each magnon mode, and a subsequent Ramsey measurement of the qubit yields the joint displaced parity, from which the full joint Wigner function is reconstructed. This scheme, adapted from cavity-QED tomography techniques, is shown to be compatible with current experimental setups where dispersive shifts from the two magnon modes are distinguishable.

2605.06296v1.title: From flat to narrow bands: Engineering quantum emission in a one-dimensional Lieb lattice

concepts.name: Flat-band physics in photonic lattices
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that coupling a quantum emitter to sublattices with finite flat-band wavefunction overlap activates a collective, size-independent interaction that is fundamentally distinct from dispersive-band coupling. It shows that the entire flat band acts as a single collective degree of freedom with an effective coupling strength independent of system size, leading to persistent coherent oscillations rather than irreversible decay. This provides a mechanistic explanation for why flat bands produce coherent trapping rather than enhanced emission despite their divergent density of states.

concepts.name: Non-Markovian to Markovian crossover in open quantum systems
concepts.contribution: The paper derives explicit scaling laws governing the crossover between non-Markovian coherent trapping and Markovian exponential decay as a function of the ratio between emitter-bath coupling strength g and engineered bandwidth W. It establishes that the band behaves as 'effectively flat' when g/W >> 1 and 'effectively dispersive' when g/W << 1, with a nonmonotonic decay rate at intermediate values. This quantitative framework directly explains experimentally observed accelerated spontaneous emission in moire photonic crystals as arising from the Markovian regime.

concepts.name: Atom-photon bound states in structured photonic environments
concepts.contribution: The paper analytically derives, via the Lehmann spectral representation and self-energy formalism, how the sublattice coupling configuration determines the formation mechanism of bound states in the 1D Lieb lattice. It distinguishes between bound states formed through dispersive-band coupling versus those mediated by the flat band acting as a collective mode, and shows how detuning continuously reweights these two channels. The residues of these bound states are shown to obey a universal scaling with g/W as the flat band is tuned into a narrow dispersive band.

concepts.name: Symmetry breaking and band engineering in tight-binding models
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a controlled on-site potential perturbation on the C sublattice that breaks the lattice symmetry protecting the flat band, transforming it into a narrow dispersive band with bandwidth scaling linearly as W = alphaV0. This symmetry-breaking mechanism provides a continuous and quantitatively characterized tuning knob connecting idealized flat-band physics to realistic narrow-band platforms such as moire photonic crystals. The resulting modified self-energy is derived analytically, enabling predictive scaling laws for the decay rate in the Markovian limit as Gamma ~ g^2/W.

concepts.name: Non-Invertible Symmetry
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs a new class of non-invertible 0-form symmetry defects in (2+1)d QFTs arising when a discrete Abelian 0-form symmetry with a mixed 't Hooft anomaly is gauged, requiring stacking with a TQFT to restore gauge invariance. It derives explicit fusion rules for these defects, showing they follow group-like composition except when a defect fuses with its conjugate, which produces a condensation defect implementing gauging of the dual 1-form symmetry.

concepts.name: 2-Group Symmetry
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the construction of non-invertible duality defects to theories with a non-trivial 2-group structure formed by a 0-form and a 1-form symmetry, providing the first explicit duality defect arising from half-spacetime gauging of a 2-group. It shows how the 2-group structure is reshuffled under gauging in a cyclic three-symmetry parent theory, with the 0-form and 1-form components exchanging roles between dual theories.

concepts.name: Duality Defects and Half-Spacetime Gauging
concepts.contribution: The paper generalizes the half-spacetime gauging construction of non-invertible duality defects in three dimensions to allow a non-trivial 2-group symmetry between the gauged 0-form and 1-form symmetries, extending prior work that required anomaly-free symmetries. It explicitly derives the fusion rules of the resulting duality defect, showing it absorbs 1-form and non-invertible symmetry operators and that its self-fusion yields a condensation defect summing over non-invertible defect insertions.

concepts.name: Mixed 't Hooft Anomaly
concepts.contribution: The paper uses a specific cyclic mixed 't Hooft anomaly among three discrete Abelian 0-form symmetries as the key ingredient that simultaneously generates a 2-group structure upon gauging one factor and a non-invertible symmetry upon gauging another. This anomaly structure enforces a triality among three descendant theories, which is the necessary condition for the half-spacetime gauging to produce a genuine symmetry defect rather than a mere interface.

2605.06284v1.title: Local distillation from Reed Muller codes unfolding

concepts.name: Magic State Distillation
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs new distillation factories based on quantum Reed-Muller codes with local stabilizer layouts, achieving output infidelities of 8.256×10⁻⁹ for a distance-4 2D factory and 1.1811×10⁻¹⁷ for a distance-7 3D factory given input infidelity p=10⁻³. It introduces the 'big unfolded code' as a 64-T-state-to-CCZ factory and punctured QRM7(2,2) as a 127-T-state-to-T factory, explicitly computing prefactors (8256p⁴ and 11811p⁷ respectively) for the dominant logical error probability.

concepts.name: Quantum Reed-Muller Codes
concepts.contribution: The paper reveals the algebraic product structure underlying the 'unfolding' of quantum Reed-Muller codes, generalizing a previously SAT-solver-discovered 2D layout to a systematic framework applicable to larger codes. It constructs explicit 2D planar layouts for QRM4(1,1) and QRM6(1,1) and 3D local layouts for QRM6(1,2) and QRM7(2,2) by partitioning coordinate indices into groups corresponding to spatial directions and exploiting Gray-code-ordered bases.

concepts.name: Transversal Gates and the Clifford Hierarchy
concepts.contribution: The paper explicitly characterizes the logical action of transversal T gates on QRM6(1,2), proving that it implements a product of 15 CCZ gates on the 15 logical qubits indexed by 2-element subsets of {1,...,6}. It further shows that restricting to the 'big unfolded code' projects this action to a single CCZ gate on three logical qubits, directly enabling magic state distillation with a transversal gate implementation.

concepts.name: Local Quantum Error Correcting Code Layouts for Biased-Noise Qubits
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the Z stabilizer group of several quantum Reed-Muller codes admits bases consisting entirely of geometrically local weight-4 (squares) or weight-8 (cubes) stabilizers in 2D or 3D, while leaving the X stabilizer group non-local—a property specifically suited to biased-noise platforms such as cat qubits where X errors are strongly suppressed. This provides a practical pathway to compact distillation circuits measured by physical qubit count times error-correction rounds.

2605.06271v1.title: A Comparative Study of Mass Extraction Schemes and $π^\pm-ρ^\pm$ Mixing

concepts.name: π-ρ Mixing in External Magnetic Fields
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies π±-ρ± mixing as the primary dynamical origin of the non-monotonic magnetic-field dependence of the lowest charged pion excitation observed in lattice QCD. It demonstrates that the robustness of this mixing-induced turnover depends critically on whether the charged meson is treated as a Landau-level quasiparticle, and shows that residue suppression of the rho pole enhances the effective mixing strength after canonical normalization.

concepts.name: Landau Level Quantization of Composite Hadrons
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes that projecting the meson quadratic kernel onto Landau-level eigenstates, rather than treating the charged meson as a plane-wave rest-frame excitation, is essential for reproducing lattice QCD results. It shows that schemes which impose Landau projection directly on the external meson state yield a physically distinct and more faithful charged quasiparticle spectrum compared to vacuum-inspired rest-mass constructions.

concepts.name: Quasiparticle Residues and Wave-Function Renormalization in Magnetic Backgrounds
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the magnetic-field-dependent suppression of mesonic pole residues, particularly the rapid collapse of the longitudinal rho residue Zρ(B), dramatically enhances the canonically normalized π-ρ mixing strength through the factor (ZπZρ)^{-1/2}. This makes explicit that the non-monotonic behavior is driven not by growth of the bare mixing kernel but by residue-enhanced level repulsion between pion-like and rho-like Landau modes.

concepts.name: Mass Extraction Schemes in Symmetry-Broken Backgrounds
concepts.contribution: The paper systematically compares four operationally distinct mass-extraction procedures—rest-mass reconstruction, local bosonization, direct Landau-projected determinant, and near-pole quasiparticle expansion—applied to the same microscopic NJL kernel. It demonstrates that in a magnetic background, where Lorentz symmetry is broken and charged excitations occupy discrete Landau levels, these schemes yield qualitatively different magnetic-field dependences, establishing that hadron mass in such backgrounds is intrinsically scheme-dependent.

2605.06263v1.title: Beating noise in frequency estimation with squeezing and memory in continuous-variable systems

concepts.name: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) in Open Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper derives analytical and numerical expressions for QFI in continuous-variable frequency estimation under both Markovian and non-Markovian dissipative dynamics. It demonstrates that QFI acquires a tunable higher-order (cubic) time dependence when squeezing is embedded in the Hamiltonian, partially counteracting the exponential decay imposed by environmental noise. It further shows that non-Markovian dynamics can cause QFI to temporarily exceed the unitary (noise-free) limit due to information backflow from the structured environment.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian Engineering via Squeezing
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that adding quadratic squeezing terms to a harmonic oscillator Hamiltonian modifies the time-scaling of QFI from quadratic to cubic in the short-time regime, providing enhanced metrological sensitivity without leaving the Gaussian framework. By tuning the squeezing phase, the enhancement can be made strictly positive, offering a controllable route to improved precision even under Markovian decoherence. Numerical results confirm that squeezing-induced gains can outperform non-Markovian memory effects except in the regime of very small squeezing strength and coherent amplitude.

concepts.name: Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics and Information Backflow
concepts.contribution: Using the quantum Brownian motion model with an Ohmic Lorentz-Drude spectral density, the paper demonstrates that finite bath memory induces temporary negativity in the CP-divisibility rates, signaling information backflow from the environment to the probe. This backflow enriches the parameter encoding across both first moments and the covariance matrix, enabling transient revivals in QFI that surpass the unitary limit. The paper quantifies how the degree of non-Markovianity, controlled by the ratio of cutoff frequency to system frequency, determines the magnitude and duration of these metrological enhancements.

concepts.name: Gaussian Measurement Strategies (General-Dyne Detection)
concepts.contribution: The paper evaluates the classical Fisher information achievable by homodyne, heterodyne, and optimized general-dyne measurements, identifying the conditions under which these Gaussian strategies saturate the quantum Cramér-Rao bound. It finds that without squeezing, appropriately timed quadrature measurements can achieve the QFI exactly, while increasing squeezing strength progressively widens the gap between the dyne-optimal CFI and the QFI. This growing gap suggests that strong squeezing regimes may require non-Gaussian measurement strategies, such as photon counting, to saturate the ultimate precision limit.

concepts.name: Projective Hilbert Space / Quantum State Space
concepts.contribution: The paper formalizes the identification of qubit state space with the Riemann sphere (complex projective line P1) in a functorial and lax monoidal way, replacing unit vectors modulo global phase with homogeneous coordinates. This removes the global phase ambiguity cleanly and reframes quantum state composition via the Segre embedding, providing a rigorous categorical foundation for projective quantum mechanics.

concepts.name: Magic State Distillation
concepts.contribution: The paper recasts magic state distillation protocols as meromorphic functions on the Riemann sphere, where stationary points of the function correspond to states that receive coherent error suppression. It applies this framework to the [[5,1,3]], [[7,1,3]], and [[15,1,3]] codes, explicitly computing the order of error suppression at magic states (such as F-states and H-states) from the branch-point structure of the meromorphic decoder via the Riemann-Hurwitz theorem.

concepts.name: Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (Stabilizer / CSS Codes)
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces the concept of a meromorphic decoder for a stabilizer code, a rational function encoding the logical decoder's action on single-qubit input states. For CSS codes it derives a closed-form expression for this function directly from the code's weight enumerator polynomial, and shows that code concatenation corresponds to function composition, giving a compact algebraic representation of logical state preparation.

concepts.name: ZXW-Calculus / Graphical Quantum Calculus
concepts.contribution: The paper provides an alternate projective-geometric derivation of the arithmetic GHZ/W-calculus by interpreting ZX and W spiders as meromorphic operations on the Riemann sphere (multiplication, addition, and Lorentz velocity addition). This grounds the diagrammatic calculus in classical projective algebraic geometry, explaining why the calculus naturally encodes rational arithmetic.

2605.06249v1.title: Finite-size general security for differential phase shift keying via variable-length quantum key distribution

concepts.name: Quantum Key Distribution Security Proofs
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a finite-size, composable security proof for DPSK against general (coherent) adversaries using the marginal-constrained entropy accumulation theorem (MEAT), replacing the more restrictive generalized entropy accumulation technique (GEAT). This reduces the minimum required block size by orders of magnitude, achieving positive secret key rates with only 10^5 signals at losses beyond 12 dB, compared to roughly 10^12 signals needed in prior work.

concepts.name: Differential Phase Shift Keying (DPSK) Protocols
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the general security framework for DPSK to include practical experimental imperfections such as dark counts, asymmetric coherent state modulation, and excess fiber noise, providing a more experimentally realistic security analysis. It also lifts the kilohertz-scale repetition rate constraint that was previously imposed by the GEAT-based proof structure, with the remaining rate limitation depending only on the physical speed of light in the channel rather than the security proof.

concepts.name: Rényi Entropy and Variable-Length Key Distillation
concepts.contribution: The paper applies f-weighted Rényi entropy accumulation and leftover hashing to derive variable-length secret key bounds for DPSK, allowing the key length to adapt to observed channel statistics rather than being fixed in advance. This formulation enables tighter finite-size corrections and more favorable security tolerance parameters, improving the error correction security parameter to ε_EC = 10^{-11} without sacrificing key rate.

concepts.name: Conic Optimization in Quantum Information
concepts.contribution: The paper adapts non-symmetric conic programming techniques, specifically the FastRényiQKD cone combined with Kullback-Leibler and logarithmic cones, to numerically compute optimal secret key rates and tradeoff functions for DPSK in real time. Facial reduction is applied to handle the rank-deficient key maps arising from the isometric structure of the protocol, ensuring strict feasibility of the resulting conic programs.

2605.06224v1.title: Modular wedge localization, Majorana fields and the Tsirelson limit of the Bell-CHSH inequality

concepts.name: Bell-CHSH Inequality in Relativistic Quantum Field Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a closed-form analytic expression for the vacuum Bell-CHSH correlator in terms of a single spectral weight h²(ω) associated with the modular operator, using the massive Majorana field in 1+1 dimensions as a concrete model. This reduces the abstract Summers-Werner construction to an explicit rapidity-space calculation, allowing the approach to the Tsirelson bound (2√2) to be tracked analytically. The paper shows that the supremum 2√2 is never reached by regular normalizable weights but is approached as spectral weight concentrates near ω≈0.

concepts.name: Tomita-Takesaki Modular Theory and Modular Localization
concepts.contribution: The paper provides an explicit rapidity-space realization of modular localization for wedge regions, expressing the modular operator δ and conjugation j in terms of the boost generator K=-id/dθ and analytically implementing the standard subspace conditions for the Majorana field. It connects the approach to the Tsirelson bound directly to the spectral structure of the modular operator, identifying the near-saturation regime with spectral concentration near the eigenvalue λ²=1, which corresponds to the type III₁ nature of local relativistic von Neumann algebras.

concepts.name: Majorana Fields in 1+1 Dimensions
concepts.contribution: The paper works out the complete quantization of the massive Majorana field in 1+1 dimensions in rapidity space, including the plane-wave expansion, canonical anti-commutation relations, smearing procedure, and the structure of the one-particle Hilbert space as L²(ℝ,dθ) with a Majorana real structure. It demonstrates that the Majorana condition and mass mixing of the two spinor components reduce the field to a single particle type with a scalar combination of test-function components, making it especially tractable for the Bell-CHSH construction.

concepts.name: Fermionic Twist and Klein Transformation in Quantum Field Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper explicitly implements the fermion-parity twist (Klein transformation) on the left-wedge operators to convert graded-local Majorana field operators into ordinary commuting Bell observables across the two wedges. This construction is shown to introduce a factor of -i in the vacuum cross-correlators, and the paper demonstrates that with this convention the sign pattern of inner products is precisely that required to achieve near-maximal Bell-CHSH violation.

2605.06193v1.title: Causal self-dual nonlinear electrodynamics from the Born-Infeld theory

concepts.name: Nonlinear Electrodynamics (NLED) and U(1) Duality Invariance
concepts.contribution: The paper develops an auxiliary-field formulation using the Born-Infeld theory as a seed Lagrangian, generating a broad class of U(1) duality-invariant (self-dual) NLED theories by choosing different scalar potentials W(ψ). It demonstrates that this construction provides a general solution to the self-duality equation and recovers known theories such as ModMax and ModMaxBorn as special cases.

concepts.name: Causality in Classical Field Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper proves rigorously that all NLED theories generated by the Born-Infeld auxiliary-field formulation satisfy the necessary and sufficient causality conditions identified by Schellstede, Perlick, and Lämmerzahl, provided the scalar potential satisfies W''(ψ) > 0. It further shows that the weaker condition W''(ψ) ≥ 0 still yields causal theories, extending the causality analysis to the boundary case including the ModMax theory.

concepts.name: Born-Infeld Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper elevates the Born-Infeld Lagrangian from a specific model to a structural seed for generating entire families of self-dual NLED theories via an auxiliary scalar field, exploiting its role in string theory and partial supersymmetry breaking. It also proves a non-recoverability theorem showing that the Born-Infeld theory itself cannot be reproduced by integrating out the auxiliary field within its own formulation.

concepts.name: Courant-Hilbert Method and Legendre Transform in Self-Dual Field Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper connects its Born-Infeld auxiliary-field formulation to the general Courant-Hilbert solution of the self-duality equation, establishing an explicit map between the scalar potential W(ψ) and the generating function ℓ(τ). It also derives the precise relationship between the Born-Infeld formulation and the earlier Russo-Townsend formulation via a field redefinition and Legendre transform, unifying the two approaches.

concepts.name: Analog Quantum Simulation
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces Universal Analog Quantum Simulation (UAQS), a framework that systematically expands the range of Hamiltonians accessible to a fixed analog hardware platform without decomposing dynamics into discrete gate sequences. By embedding continuous-time control optimization directly into native analog evolution, UAQS transforms hardware-specific analog devices into programmable simulators capable of reproducing dynamics beyond their intrinsic interaction structure. Numerical demonstrations on superconducting circuits and Rydberg-atom arrays confirm accurate reproduction of nontrivial many-body dynamics including transverse-field Ising, Heisenberg, XY, and Fermi-Hubbard models.

concepts.name: McLachlan Variational Principle
concepts.contribution: The paper applies McLachlan's variational principle to continuously project exact Schrödinger dynamics onto the tangent space of a low-dimensional parameter manifold, yielding linear equations governing real-time parameter flow (M_R θ-dot = V_I) and imaginary-time parameter flow (M_R θ-dot = -V_R). This formulation unifies both real- and imaginary-time evolution within a single variational framework requiring identical underlying measurements of the quantum geometric tensor M and gradient vector V. The paper further derives ancilla-free, analog-compatible estimation protocols for M and V using Monte Carlo integration, projective measurements, and a generalized parameter-shift rule.

concepts.name: Imaginary-Time Evolution for Ground-State Preparation
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that imaginary-time evolution can be realized on fixed analog hardware by casting it as a continuous-time control optimization problem within the UAQS framework, enabling exponential convergence to ground states without requiring non-unitary operations directly on the hardware. Numerical benchmarks on the transverse-field Ising model show high-fidelity ground-state convergence with a characteristic transient dip in fidelity that is subsequently suppressed, validating the approach. The framework is further extended to molecular ground-state preparation, demonstrated on the H2 molecule in the STO-3G basis via a qubit Hamiltonian derived through Jordan-Wigner transformation.

concepts.name: Out-of-Time-Order Correlators (OTOCs) and Information Scrambling
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that OTOCs, which diagnose quantum information scrambling and operator growth in many-body systems, can be computed using UAQS by simulating forward and time-reversed analog evolution with an intermediate local operator insertion. Site-resolved OTOC dynamics for a Heisenberg chain show clear light-cone-like propagation with finite spreading velocity, accurately reproducing both the spatiotemporal scrambling structure and operator-dependent features. This establishes UAQS as a practical route to measuring scrambling diagnostics on near-term analog hardware without requiring ancilla-assisted protocols.

2605.06171v1.title: Quantum phase diagrams for bosons in hexagonal optical potentials: A continuous-space quantum Monte Carlo study

concepts.name: Superfluid-Mott Insulator Quantum Phase Transition
concepts.contribution: The paper provides continuous-space quantum Monte Carlo phase diagrams for bosons in honeycomb and h-BN optical lattices, revealing that standard Bose-Hubbard model predictions for Mott lobe boundaries are quantitatively inaccurate even at deep lattice amplitudes. Specifically, the second Mott lobe is strongly suppressed and the third is entirely absent, demonstrating that the SF-MI boundary is significantly reshaped by beyond-Bose-Hubbard physics in hexagonal geometries.

concepts.name: Density-Assisted Tunneling
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies density-assisted tunneling as the dominant correction to the Bose-Hubbard model in honeycomb lattices, systematically quantifying its magnitude using maximally localized Wannier functions. It shows that this interaction-induced hopping renormalization grows with filling, accounting for roughly 30% correction at the second Mott lobe tip and over 100% at the predicted third lobe, explaining the progressive failure of the standard model at higher occupations.

concepts.name: Tight-Binding and Bose-Hubbard Model Validity in Continuous-Space Lattices
concepts.contribution: By comparing continuous-space exact diagonalization band structures against fitted tight-binding models, the paper establishes that single-particle band structure can be reproduced to within ~1% accuracy by tight-binding models at V0 = 15Er, yet the corresponding Bose-Hubbard model still fails to capture the many-body phase diagram beyond the first Mott lobe. This decoupling of single-particle and many-body validity limits highlights that accurate band reproduction does not guarantee accurate interaction physics within a lattice model framework.

concepts.name: Quantum Phase Diagrams in Bipartite Hexagonal Lattices with Sublattice Asymmetry
concepts.contribution: For the h-BN (gapped honeycomb) lattice, the paper maps out a rich phase diagram featuring a cascade of Mott insulator lobes with distinct sublattice occupation patterns such as MI(1,0), MI(2,0), and MI(2,1), driven by the interplay of the sublattice energy offset, tunneling, and interactions. The sublattice offset is shown to grow linearly with the geometric phase and to trigger sequential population of the lower-energy sublattice, with the system transitioning between effective honeycomb, decoupled-triangular, and mixed regimes as the asymmetry increases.

2605.06167v1.title: Matrix encoding method in variational algorithm of calculating eigenvalues and generalized eigenvalues

concepts.name: Variational Quantum Algorithms
concepts.contribution: The paper extends variational quantum algorithms to compute both standard eigenvalues and generalized eigenvalues of arbitrary complex (non-Hermitian) matrices by combining a quantum loss-function evaluator with a classical gradient optimizer. It introduces a matrix-encoding approach that avoids the need to decompose input matrices as linear combinations of unitaries or embed them in Hermitian operators, broadening the class of problems these hybrid algorithms can address. The circuit depth is characterized as O(N² log N) and the qubit count as O(log N).

concepts.name: Quantum State Encoding of Classical Data
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates a method of encoding the elements of two arbitrary complex matrices directly into the probability amplitudes of a pure quantum superposition state, labeling contributions from each matrix via a dedicated ancilla qubit. This encoding sidesteps unitary decomposition and Suzuki-Trotter exponentiation, which are standard but costly techniques in prior quantum linear-algebra algorithms. The approach is shown to support downstream matrix operations such as multiplication by unitary transforms and extraction of off-diagonal elements needed for the loss function.

concepts.name: Generalized Eigenvalue Problem
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a quantum-assisted variational algorithm for solving the generalized eigenvalue problem A|ψ⟩ = λB|ψ⟩ for arbitrary non-Hermitian complex matrices A and B by reducing it to a matrix triangularization task via generalized Schur decomposition. It establishes quantitative relationships between the accuracy of the computed generalized eigenvalues ε, the accuracy of the loss function εL, and the precision σ of encoding optimization parameters, finding εL ~ ε² and ε^(min) ~ √σ. These scaling relations are confirmed numerically on ensembles of random 4×4 complex matrices.

concepts.name: Ancilla Measurement and Garbage Removal in Quantum Circuits
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a structured two-ancilla measurement protocol to probabilistically isolate the physically relevant terms in a superposition state from computational garbage, enabling extraction of the loss function from measurable probabilities. The success probability of this garbage-removal step scales as O(N⁻⁴), and the paper identifies this as a principal resource cost and open challenge for practical implementation. It connects the number of repeated circuit runs required to the desired loss-function accuracy, quantifying the classical-quantum resource trade-off in the hybrid optimization loop.

2605.06159v1.title: Non-abelian field cohomology, its relation with spontaneous symmetry breaking and Morse's Theorem

concepts.name: Gribov Problem
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that in a gauge theory with spontaneous symmetry breaking, the on-shell Gribov operator acquires a positive mass term proportional to the symmetry breaking scale squared, lifting the zero modes responsible for Gribov copies. This means that for perturbative energies below the symmetry breaking scale, the Gribov problem is automatically resolved on-shell without requiring explicit non-local modifications such as the Gribov-Zwanziger action. The result holds for any gauge fixing constructed from a Morse functional of ultraviolet dimension 2, including 't Hooft-type gauges.

concepts.name: BRST Cohomology
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that spontaneous symmetry breaking changes the cohomological structure of a non-abelian gauge theory by creating new field combinations that behave like matter fields rather than gauge fields under the BRST operator. Using the filtration theorem, the filtered BRST operator after symmetry breaking is shown to leave specific combinations of gauge and scalar fields invariant, which can then be lifted to full BRST-invariant observables. This cohomological reclassification is the central mechanism that enables the resolution of the Gribov problem.

concepts.name: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes a precise link between spontaneous symmetry breaking and the cohomological properties of field combinations, showing that the broken vacuum fundamentally alters which field combinations are BRST-closed. In the SU(2) x U(1) example broken to U(1)_em, specific linear combinations of gauge and Higgs fields are identified as cohomologically matter-like, which is the property that ultimately drives the on-shell mass generation in the Gribov operator. This connects the symmetry breaking scale directly to the elimination of gauge copy ambiguities.

concepts.name: Morse Theory in Gauge Fixing
concepts.contribution: The paper reframes gauge fixing as a Morse extremization problem for a functional of ultraviolet dimension 2 and ghost number zero, interpreting the gauge condition as the Euler-Lagrange equation of that functional. It shows that the most general such functional, including scalar field contributions, yields via the BRST and anti-BRST double variation a gauge fixing action whose on-shell Gribov equation contains a mass term in the broken phase. This provides a systematic and renormalizable framework for constructing gauge fixings that are free of the Gribov ambiguity on-shell.

2605.06147v1.title: Cosmological Dynamics of a Non-Canonical Generalised Brans-Dicke Theory

concepts.name: Scalar-Tensor Gravity
concepts.contribution: The paper generalises Brans-Dicke theory by introducing both a non-minimal coupling f(ϕ) = 1 + ξϕ and a non-canonical kinetic term K(ϕ,X) = ωX/f(ϕ), extending the standard scalar-tensor framework. It derives the full modified Friedmann and Klein-Gordon equations for this combined setup and shows that the resulting dynamics differ noticeably from simpler scalar-tensor models even when using analogous dynamical variables. Solar system and stability constraints are used to bound the coupling parameter ξ and the Brans-Dicke-like parameter ω.

concepts.name: Dynamical Systems in Cosmology
concepts.contribution: The paper reformulates the cosmological field equations as a closed autonomous system of dimensionless variables, enabling a systematic search for critical points and their stability for three distinct scalar field potentials. It introduces a compactification scheme for the phase space using the variable u = arctan(λV) to handle unbounded directions, and employs bounded phase portraits to visualise the global flow. The Hartman-Grobman theorem and linear stability analysis are applied to classify each critical point as a source, saddle, or stable attractor relevant to cosmological epochs.

concepts.name: Dark Energy and Cosmological Constant Problem
concepts.contribution: For each of the three potentials studied, the paper identifies late-time attractor critical points where the scalar field mimics a cosmological constant, with equation-of-state parameter wϕ ≈ −1 and deceleration parameter q ≈ −1. It demonstrates that ΛCDM-like background evolution, including the correct sequence of radiation, matter, and dark energy domination, is reproducible within this non-canonical Brans-Dicke framework for appropriately restricted parameter values. The results motivate this class of models as candidates for addressing cosmic tensions through dynamical dark energy.

concepts.name: Non-Canonical Scalar Fields (k-essence)
concepts.contribution: The paper incorporates a non-canonical kinetic term of the form ωX/f(ϕ), which couples the kinetic structure of the scalar field directly to the gravitational coupling function, going beyond standard quintessence or k-essence. Stability conditions against ghost and Laplacian instabilities are derived for this coupled kinetic term in an FLRW background, yielding the constraint ω + 3ξ²/(1+ξϕ) > 0. The analysis shows that restricting ω > 0 ensures a compact phase space, whereas ω < 0 leads to a hyperbolic, non-compact phase space requiring Poincaré compactification.

2605.06138v1.title: Probing the density dependence of nuclear symmetry energy through isospin transport in heavy-ion reactions

concepts.name: Nuclear Symmetry Energy and its Density Dependence
concepts.contribution: The paper extracts confidence regions (1σ, 2σ, 3σ) for the symmetry energy S(ρ) in the density range near saturation by combining experimental isospin transport ratio data with BUU transport model calculations. It demonstrates that the sensitive density region probed by Fermi-energy heavy-ion collisions lies close to saturation density, allowing stiff symmetry energy parametrizations like NL3 to be excluded while favoring softer behaviors consistent with ab initio chiral EFT predictions. The method of weighting the likelihood by the isospin-current-derived density sensitivity function w(ρ/ρ₀) provides more reliable constraints by avoiding uncontrolled extrapolations to density regions not actually probed.

concepts.name: Isospin Transport and Diffusion in Heavy-Ion Collisions
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes that the isospin transport ratio constructed from the quasi-projectile N/Z ratio is a more robust and sensitive probe of the equation of state than the ratio from forward-emitted free nucleons, due to reduced model dependence from clustering and secondary decay effects. It quantifies how the isospin diffusion current through the neck region evolves in time and which baryonic densities it predominantly samples, providing a self-consistent determination of the density interval actually probed by the observable. The INDRA-FAZIA experimental setup enables a model-independent measurement of isospin equilibration as a function of impact parameter, removing the need for surrogate observables used in earlier studies.

concepts.name: Boltzmann-Uehling-Uhlenbeck (BUU) Transport Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper implements a metamodelling approach within the BUU@VECC-McGill framework that represents the nuclear equation of state as a polynomial density expansion, enabling direct incorporation of realistic ab initio and phenomenological energy density functionals beyond simplified analytical forms. This allows the transport code to be confronted with data using EoS inputs derived from chiral effective field theory, Skyrme interactions, and relativistic mean-field models within a single consistent framework. The study also avoids coupling to statistical afterburner codes by analyzing the time asymptotic behavior of the isospin transport ratio directly, reducing systematic uncertainties in the extracted EoS constraints.

concepts.name: Nuclear Equation of State (EoS) Inference and Bayesian Constraints
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a proto-Bayesian protocol in which χ² values comparing experimental and theoretical isospin transport ratios are used to construct posterior probability distributions for the symmetry energy at each density, using quadratic interpolation between a set of realistic EoS models to approximate the full likelihood surface. The density-weighting function derived from the isospin current dynamics is incorporated as a prior that restricts inference to the density region genuinely probed by the experiment, preventing spurious constraints at densities the reaction does not access. The resulting posterior distributions are shown to be consistent with independent constraints from nuclear masses, isobaric analog states, electric dipole polarizability, and neutron skin thickness measurements, and are directly applicable to astrophysical EoS studies.

2605.06131v1.title: Hugoniot Relation for Multi-Temperature Euler Equations of Compressible Plasma Flows

concepts.name: Rankine-Hugoniot Shock Conditions
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that for multi-temperature (non-conservative) Euler equations, the classical total-energy Rankine-Hugoniot relation constrains post-shock states only to a hypersurface in phase space rather than a unique curve, exposing a fundamental non-uniqueness absent in single-fluid systems. Two distinct, physically admissible Hugoniot relations are derived analytically—one from a segment path and one from a vanishing viscosity limit—each selecting a different curve on that hypersurface. This shows that the Hugoniot relation cannot be deduced from the macroscopic PDEs alone and must be supplied by microscopic physics, experiments, or first-principles simulations.

concepts.name: Non-Conservative Hyperbolic Systems and DLM Path Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper connects the physical ambiguity of shock solutions to the mathematical framework of Dal Maso–Le Floch–Murat (DLM) theory, showing that choosing a path for the non-conservative product is equivalent to specifying a Hugoniot relation that closes the shock problem. Both the segment path and the vanishing viscosity path are shown to constitute valid DLM weak formulations, making explicit that path selection is not merely an auxiliary mathematical device but encodes lost microscopic closure information. This provides a concrete geometric interpretation: macroscopic jump conditions fix an admissible surface while the unresolved microscopic physics selects a curve on it.

concepts.name: Thermodynamic Admissibility and Entropy Production in Shocks
concepts.contribution: Following the classical Courant–Friedrichs framework, the paper rigorously verifies that both derived Hugoniot relations satisfy standard admissibility criteria: conservation of total energy, second-order contact with the phasic isentropic curves, and positive phasic entropy production along admissible shock branches. For the vanishing viscosity case in two-temperature plasma, a formal proof (Theorem 3.2) establishes entropy productivity for sufficiently weak shocks via an ODE analysis of traveling wave profiles and an admissible set argument. This extends classical single-fluid shock thermodynamics to the multi-temperature, non-conservative setting.

concepts.name: Numerical Schemes for Compressible Multi-Temperature Plasma Flows
concepts.contribution: The paper provides the first explicit analytical Hugoniot relations that serve as exact reference solutions for evaluating discontinuous numerical approximations of multi-temperature plasma flows. By analyzing the structure-preserving scheme and the vanishing viscosity scheme in a Lagrangian framework, it shows that each scheme implicitly encodes one of the two derived Hugoniot relations, with the difference reducible to how numerical viscosity is distributed between ion and electron energies. Numerical experiments with double-shock Riemann problems confirm that the two schemes produce different post-shock states precisely because they correspond to different physical closures, while agreeing on smooth rarefaction solutions.

2605.06122v1.title: Variationally Compressing Quantum Circuits to Approximate Nonadiabatic Molecular Quantum Dynamics

concepts.name: Nonadiabatic Quantum Dynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that Trotterized quantum circuits representing coupled harmonic potential energy surfaces (the Marcus model) can be variationally compressed while still recovering physically meaningful observables such as electron transfer rate coefficients. By substituting l-local truncated ansatz operators for explicit Trotter terms, it shows that qualitative features of the Marcus rate curve—including the peak location and inverted-regime suppression—are preserved under controlled approximation error. This establishes a proof-of-principle that variational circuit compression is applicable to nonadiabatic molecular processes relevant to quantum chemistry.

concepts.name: Variational Quantum Algorithms
concepts.contribution: The paper develops an l-local truncation strategy for diagonal Walsh operators on binary-encoded qubit registers, reducing the effective variational parameter space from O(n²) to just two parameters for any quadratic potential, independent of register size. It adapts the Quantum-Assisted Quantum Compiling (QAQC) protocol with the Local Hilbert-Schmidt Test cost function and parameter-shift-rule gradients to optimize the ansatz, demonstrating convergence to global minima verified analytically. This provides a concrete, tunable framework for matching logical approximation error to physical hardware gate fidelity in near-term quantum devices.

concepts.name: Variational Fast-Forwarding
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the variational fast-forwarding (VFF) framework by showing that compressed quadratic operators admit rescaling of diagonal parameters for multi-step time evolution without re-optimization, experimentally validating this on IBM Brisbane hardware for n=3 qubits with state fidelity above 0.80 through ten timesteps. It further demonstrates that the WDW† ansatz structure exhibits noise resilience under hardware errors, with fidelity decay leveling off over longer times. This confirms that fast-forwarding is practically viable for adiabatic subsystems even under realistic hardware noise conditions.

concepts.name: Binary Encoding and Product Formula Methods for Quantum Simulation
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies and exploits tensor product commutativity in the explicit Benenti-Strini circuit construction for quadratic operators, reducing the two-qubit gate count by a factor of two before any variational optimization is applied. It establishes that the Walsh function expansion exactly represents quadratic operators at second order on binary-encoded grids, and that l-local truncation of this expansion maps directly to hardware-connectivity-respecting circuits with depth scaling reduced from O(n²) to O(n×l). The total qubit overhead for the full nonadiabatic simulation pipeline is also reduced from 18 to 15 logical qubits through an improved comparator circuit construction.

2605.06101v1.title: Syndrome resampling enhances quantum error correction thresholds

concepts.name: Quantum Error Correction Thresholds
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces syndrome resampling, a decoder-agnostic method that increases the error correction threshold for any decoder without hardware modifications. By biasing syndrome statistics toward high-probability syndromes via a reweighting power parameter α, the method demonstrates threshold increases from ~10.75% to ~17.74% and ~20.93% for α=2 and α=3 respectively in surface codes under bit-flip noise. The approach establishes a continuous family of thresholds parameterized by α, interpolating between standard maximum likelihood decoding and full post-selection.

concepts.name: Rényi Coherent Information
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes a direct analytical connection between the Rényi coherent information (RCI) and powers of the syndrome probability distribution, showing that averaging logical error rates over the modified distribution Qα(s) ∝ P^α(s) realizes the same phase transition structure as the RCI. This connection maps the RCI phase transitions for α=1,2,3 to known statistical mechanical models—the random-bond Ising, Ising, and Ashkin-Teller models respectively—with numerically confirmed critical exponents. The work thus provides an operational, experimentally accessible interpretation of the RCI as a family of achievable performance benchmarks.

concepts.name: Syndrome Probability Distribution in Stabilizer Codes
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a practical framework for estimating and exploiting the syndrome probability distribution (SPD) directly from finite experimental data using an unbiased combinatorial estimator based on binomial coefficients. It derives scaling laws for the required sample sizes in both low and high error rate regimes, showing the method is feasible in experimentally relevant parameter ranges where post-selection becomes impractical. Applied to real experimental lattice surgery data, this SPD-based resampling achieved up to two orders of magnitude reduction in logical error rates while retaining ~40% of samples compared to ~5% for full post-selection.

concepts.name: Post-Selection and Logical Error Mitigation in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
concepts.contribution: The paper positions syndrome resampling as an intermediate strategy between full decoding and post-selection, demonstrating that it suppresses logical errors in regimes where post-selection is infeasible due to exponentially low acceptance rates. When combined with complementary-gap post-selection, the two methods act on complementary subsets of syndromes and together achieve up to four orders of magnitude reduction in logical error rates compared to bare MWPM decoding. Unlike prior confidence-based or code-specific mitigation approaches, the method requires no decoder modifications and applies universally to any stabilizer code.

2605.06099v1.title: Non-relativistic limit of generalized relativistic Pauli operators by Feynman-Kac formulae

concepts.name: Non-relativistic limit of relativistic quantum mechanics
concepts.contribution: The paper rigorously proves that the heat semigroup of a generalized relativistic Pauli operator converges strongly to that of a non-relativistic Pauli operator as the speed of light c tends to infinity. This is established for a broad family of operators parametrized by α, β, γ under the constraint 2α = βγ + γ², extending previous results beyond the standard square-root kinetic energy operator. The limiting non-relativistic generator is shown to be (α/2m)(2/m)^(α−1)(σ·(−i∇−a))² + V, recovering the standard Pauli operator in the special case α=1.

concepts.name: Feynman-Kac formula for relativistic quantum operators
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a Feynman-Kac path integral representation for the heat semigroup of the generalized relativistic Pauli operator, involving three independent stochastic processes: a Brownian motion, an α/2-relativistic subordinator, and a spin process driven by a Poisson process. This representation is then used as the primary technical tool to prove the non-relativistic limit via probabilistic convergence arguments. The approach generalizes earlier Feynman-Kac formulas for the standard relativistic Pauli operator to the full Bernstein function framework.

concepts.name: Bernstein functions and subordinators in quantum mechanics
concepts.contribution: The paper frames the generalized relativistic operators through the lens of Bernstein functions, replacing the standard relativistic symbol √(u + m²c⁴) − mc² with a parametric family Ψ^α_c(u) = (2c^β u + (mc^γ)^(2/α))^(α/2) − mc^γ. The associated α/2-relativistic subordinator is analyzed in detail, including its Lévy–Khintchine representation, stochastic integral decomposition, and the key convergence result that its moments converge to those of the deterministic limit αt/m^(2/α−1) as c→∞. This subordinator mediates the time-changed stochastic processes that appear in the Feynman-Kac formula.

concepts.name: Pauli operator and spin dynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the mathematical treatment of the Pauli operator—which encodes spin-1/2 degrees of freedom via the Pauli matrices—to a generalized relativistic setting with singular vector potentials. The spin degree of freedom is handled by mapping the operator to L²(R³×Z₂) and introducing a spin process (θ_t) = (−1)^(N_t) driven by a Poisson process, allowing a rigorous probabilistic treatment of spin-flip transitions through the magnetic field components. The non-relativistic limit is then proved to hold strongly in this spin-extended Hilbert space setting.

2605.06093v1.title: Singularity Resolution in Quantum Cosmology via Page-Wootters Formalism

concepts.name: Page-Wootters Formalism
concepts.contribution: The paper applies the Page-Wootters relational framework to a plane-symmetric Bianchi type-I minisuperspace model, extending its use beyond simple clock-Hamiltonian setups to one with a quadratic (Klein-Gordon-type) clock Hamiltonian. It demonstrates that conditioning the globally timeless Wheeler-DeWitt state on a definite clock reading recovers relational dynamics, and further shows that positivity of the conditional probability density imposes concrete constraints on admissible clock values that depend on the Gaussian wavepacket parameters.

concepts.name: Wheeler-DeWitt Equation and Quantum Cosmology
