concepts.contribution: The paper constructs the general solution of the Wheeler-DeWitt equation for a plane-symmetric Bianchi type-I universe using Misner variables, yielding a Klein-Gordon-type constraint whose solution is a Gaussian superposition of momentum eigenstates forming an entangled clock-universe state. It uses this solution to show that the conditional probability density vanishes in the zero-volume limit for all clock readings, providing a concrete demonstration of singularity resolution within the canonical quantum gravity framework.

concepts.name: Big Bang Singularity Resolution
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that within the Page-Wootters relational framework, the conditional probability density for the volume variable vanishes as the volume goes to zero (i.e., α → −∞) independently of the clock parameter, indicating that the classical big bang singularity is quantum mechanically resolved. This result complements existing singularity avoidance results from loop quantum cosmology and standard WDW boundary-condition approaches by grounding the resolution in the entanglement structure between clock and universe subsystems.

concepts.name: Klein-Gordon Inner Product in Quantum Gravity
concepts.contribution: The paper adopts the Klein-Gordon inner product as the physically appropriate norm for the WDW wavefunction in this model, deriving that positivity of the norm requires the mean momentum k0 > 0. It further defines the conditional probability density using a Klein-Gordon-type current evaluated at fixed clock readings, and analyzes the parameter space (wavepacket mean k0 and width σ) for which this density remains positive definite, providing explicit numerical bounds.

2605.06079v1.title: Accessory Parameter of Confluent Heun Equations, Voros Periods and classical irregular conformal blocks

concepts.name: Accessory Parameters of Heun Equations
concepts.contribution: The paper derives formal series expansions of accessory parameters for the full confluent family of Heun equations (nine equations total) using Voros periods from exact WKB analysis. It provides a systematic algorithmic prescription—based on choosing vanishing cycles on the spectral curve and imposing partial isomonodromic deformation conditions—for computing these expansions to arbitrary order, extending previous results that covered only select cases.

concepts.name: Exact WKB Analysis and Voros Periods
concepts.contribution: The paper exploits Voros periods (all-order WKB period integrals along cycles on genus-1 spectral curves) as the central tool for encoding monodromy data of confluent Heun equations. It clarifies precisely which cycle on the spectral curve must be chosen—specifically vanishing cycles in various asymptotic limits—to produce expansions that match classical conformal blocks, providing a unified WKB framework applicable to both regular and irregular singular settings.

concepts.name: Classical Conformal Blocks and the Zamolodchikov Conjecture
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the Zamolodchikov conjecture—originally relating classical (large central charge) conformal blocks to accessory parameters of the Heun equation—to all confluent Heun equations and their associated irregular conformal blocks. By comparing accessory parameter expansions with classical limits of Nekrasov-type partition functions recently constructed by Bonelli–Shchechkin–Tanzini via bilinear equations, it provides detailed conjectural identifications (verified to several orders) between the two quantities for every equation in the confluent Heun family.

concepts.name: AGT Correspondence and Nekrasov–Shatashvili Limit
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies the classical conformal blocks under study with NS twisted superpotentials obtained via the Nekrasov–Shatashvili limit of Omega-background partition functions, connecting confluent Heun spectral data to four-dimensional N=2 gauge theories through the AGT correspondence. It explicitly maps spectral parameters (monodromy exponents, Voros period modulus) to gauge theory Coulomb branch and mass parameters for each confluent Heun equation, covering cases including pure SU(2) and theories with up to four hypermultiplets.

2605.06075v1.title: Probing critical phases in quasiperiodic systems via subsystem information capacity

concepts.name: Subsystem Information Capacity (SIC)
concepts.contribution: This paper applies the SIC as a spatially resolved diagnostic tool to quasiperiodic systems, demonstrating that it distinguishes extended, critical, and localized phases more clearly than half-chain entanglement entropy alone. The SIC reveals a stepwise ramp in the steady state unique to the IDZ critical phase and captures site-specific spatial heterogeneity invisible to global probes. The paper further generalizes its use to SPME phases and non-IDZ critical phases, establishing a comparative framework of distinct SIC signatures across localization scenarios.

concepts.name: Multifractal Critical Phases in Quasiperiodic Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper provides dynamical, real-space evidence for the internally fragmented structure underlying multifractal critical states in the extended Harper model, tracing it to incommensurately distributed zeros (IDZs) in the off-diagonal hopping terms. It shows that the IDZs partition the chain into nearly decoupled subregions, which manifests as a stepwise SIC ramp and pronounced spatial heterogeneity absent in extended or localized phases. This connects the static multifractal wavefunction structure to observable dynamical signatures in entanglement and information spreading.

concepts.name: Quasiparticle Picture of Entanglement Dynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the quasiparticle framework, originally developed for integrable systems, to describe information dynamics within IDZ-delimited subregions of a critical quasiperiodic chain. It introduces the concept of subregion echoes—coherent long-lived oscillations in the SIC arising from quasiparticles repeatedly reflected at subregion boundaries—and shows that oscillation periods scale linearly with subregion length, in quantitative agreement with the quasiparticle picture. This provides direct dynamical evidence for quasiparticle confinement induced by the bottlenecked connectivity of the critical phase.

concepts.name: Anderson Localization and Mobility Edges
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the SIC cleanly distinguishes a single-particle mobility edge (SPME) phase, where extended and localized states coexist at different energies, from genuine critical phases through their qualitatively different steady-state profiles and absence of subregion echoes. By applying the SIC to the generalized Aubry-André model, it shows that the SPME phase produces an abrupt initial rise followed by a linear ramp, reflecting simultaneous localization and ballistic transport at distinct energy scales. This enriches the diagnostic toolkit for identifying and differentiating localization phenomena beyond the standard extended-localized dichotomy.

2605.06022v1.title: Lattice fermion formulation via Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Ginsparg-Wilson relation and Overlap fermions

concepts.name: Ginsparg-Wilson Relation
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that a neural network trained with the GW relation as a soft loss constraint can reproduce the overlap Dirac operator to high numerical accuracy in both 2D and 4D without any prescribed polynomial or rational approximation. More strikingly, within a generalized polynomial ansatz, the network autonomously recovers the standard GW relation (c1=1, cn>1=0) from an agnostic initialization, and by shifting the initial search bias discovers a distinct Fujikawa-type generalized GW relation. This establishes machine-learning-based algebraic discovery as a new route to exploring the landscape of chiral lattice fermion structures.

concepts.name: Overlap Fermions
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that a Multi-Layer Perceptron parameterizing the Dirac operator in momentum space can learn the sign-function mapping central to the overlap construction without explicitly encoding Chebyshev or Zolotarev approximations, reproducing the overlap operator spectrum on the GW circle. Real-space checks confirm that the learned operator exhibits exponential locality consistent with theoretical bounds on the overlap fermion, and comparison with Wilson-overlap and Brillouin-overlap operators shows the framework can in principle discover improved kernels by tuning hyperparameters.

concepts.name: Fermion Doubling and the Nielsen-Ninomiya No-Go Theorem
concepts.contribution: The paper recasts doubler decoupling as a differentiable soft constraint in the neural network loss function, explicitly pinning the physical zero mode and pushing unphysical doubler modes to the cutoff scale. By encoding this condition alongside locality and symmetry penalties, the framework autonomously navigates the constraints imposed by the no-go theorem and identifies valid lattice fermion operators without manual analytical construction.

concepts.name: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs)
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the PINN paradigm from solving differential equations to the algebraic design and discovery of lattice quantum field theory operators, treating physical requirements such as chiral symmetry relations, locality, and spectrum conditions as modular loss terms. It further incorporates a DARTS-inspired differentiable architecture search over a generalized polynomial coefficient space, enabling the network to autonomously select the correct algebraic structure of the fermion action rather than merely fitting a pre-specified one.

2605.06019v1.title: Geometric Means and Lebesgue-type Decomposition of Completely Positive Maps

concepts.name: Quantum Channels and Completely Positive Maps
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a rigorous geometric mean and parallel sum for completely positive maps between von Neumann algebras, providing a new operator-theoretic framework for interpolating quantum channels. In finite dimensions, it proves that the geometric mean of CP maps corresponds exactly to the Kubo–Ando geometric mean of their Choi matrices under the Choi–Jamiołkowski isomorphism. This gives a concrete, computable structure for understanding how quantum channels interpolate between extremal cases such as the identity channel and the completely depolarizing channel.

concepts.name: Quantum Information Geometry and Fidelity
concepts.contribution: The paper connects its geometric mean construction to the Uhlmann fidelity and relative entropy by showing that the Pusz–Woronowicz mean of density-matrix functionals reproduces the operator geometric mean of the density matrices. It explicitly distinguishes this construction from the Connes relative modular operator interpolation, clarifying that these two noncommutative geometric interpolations coincide only when the states commute. This sharpens the geometric picture of distinguishability measures in quantum information theory.

concepts.name: Quantum Hypothesis Testing and Error Bounds
concepts.contribution: By establishing the AM–GM–HM inequality for CP maps and proving that the geometric mean satisfies joint monotonicity and the transformer inequality, the paper provides structural tools relevant to composite quantum hypothesis testing. The Choi-matrix characterization allows one to bound error exponents in terms of operator inequalities between interpolated channels. This extends recent work connecting weighted Kubo–Ando geometric means to error bounds in quantum statistical inference.

concepts.name: Open Quantum Systems and Lebesgue Decomposition
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes a canonical Lebesgue-type decomposition of any CP map into an absolutely continuous part and a singular part with respect to a reference map, generalizing both Ando's decomposition of positive operators and Kosaki's decomposition of normal states. Using the Stinespring dilation and Arveson Radon–Nikodym derivatives, absolute continuity and singularity are reduced to closed-subspace inclusion and orthogonality conditions in the dilating Hilbert space. This provides a unified spatial framework for characterizing the structure of noise and information loss in open quantum systems.

2605.06008v1.title: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction as a coherence diagnostic for chirality-induced spin selectivity

concepts.name: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction
concepts.contribution: The paper reframes the DM interaction not merely as a quantitative anisotropy energy scale but as a qualitative coherence order parameter for spin transport through chiral molecules. It proves that DM coupling is nonzero if and only if the tunneling matrix is non-Hermitian, i.e., retains a fixed relative quantum phase between opposite-spin transmission amplitudes. This elevates DM interaction to a binary diagnostic that can distinguish coherent SU(2) spin rotation from incoherent spin filtering, with predicted ratios |D|/JH up to 3, two orders of magnitude beyond intrinsic Rashba SOC in Si/SiGe.

concepts.name: Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS)
concepts.contribution: The paper provides the first proposed single-molecule, amplitude-level test to distinguish the two competing microscopic models of CISS: coherent unitary spin rotation versus incoherent dissipative spin filtering. It derives closed-form predictions for how each model manifests in the superexchange tensor of a double quantum dot, showing the two scenarios are separated by two to three decades in the DM-to-Heisenberg ratio across the full experimentally observed polarization range. Five candidate molecules are predicted to exceed the experimental detection threshold even under conservative interface-amplification assumptions.

concepts.name: Superexchange and Schrieffer-Wolff Transformation
concepts.contribution: The paper applies the Schrieffer-Wolff projection to derive an effective spin Hamiltonian for two quantum-dot spins coupled through a chiral molecular bridge, obtaining the full anisotropic exchange tensor including Heisenberg, DM, and symmetric anisotropic components. It shows that the superexchange amplitude samples the quantum phase between spin channels rather than the spin-dependent transmission probability, making it sensitive to coherence in a way that transport measurements are not. A structural theorem is proven demonstrating that any Hermitian tunneling matrix produces a symmetric exchange tensor with strictly zero DM component.

concepts.name: Quantum Coherence and Decoherence in Spin Qubits
concepts.contribution: The paper proposes using the precision of semiconductor exchange spectroscopy in gate-defined quantum dots, which resolves spin-spin couplings to ~10 kHz, as a probe of quantum coherence in molecular tunneling. A Lindblad analysis is provided showing that dissipative spin filtering cannot generate DM coupling through virtual tunneling on timescales consistent with the Born-Markov approximation, since the virtual-tunneling time (~0.3 ps) far undercuts realistic molecular dephasing times. Monte Carlo simulations of gate fidelity under realistic charge noise confirm that the proposed sqrt(SWAP) measurement remains above 95% fidelity for rotation angles up to 0.3pi, establishing experimental feasibility.

2605.06001v1.title: Ultraviolet-Finite Perturbative Expansion of Quantum Gravity at Null Infinity

concepts.name: Perturbative Quantum Gravity
concepts.contribution: The paper presents a perturbative expansion of quantum gravity that is ultraviolet-finite term by term up to fourth order, without requiring renormalization. This contrasts sharply with covariant perturbative quantum gravity, which generates non-renormalizable divergences already at one loop. The finiteness arises structurally because all interactions involve only on-shell gravitons and all integrations are restricted to the compact celestial sphere at null infinity.

concepts.name: Null Surface Formulation (NSF) and Bondi Shear
concepts.contribution: The paper explicitly constructs the outgoing Bondi shear operators up to fourth order in perturbation theory, with interaction kernels determined recursively from on-shell gravitational data at null infinity. It demonstrates that the map between incoming and outgoing shear operators is unitary order by order, verified through the self-adjointness of the perturbative generator. This extends prior second-order results and establishes the NSF as a concrete computational framework for graviton scattering.

concepts.name: Asymptotic Symmetries and Celestial Holography
concepts.contribution: By formulating the scattering problem entirely in terms of radiative data on the celestial sphere at null infinity, the paper provides a quantum-mechanical realization complementary to the program of asymptotic symmetries, soft theorems, and celestial holography. The infrared singularities arising from collinear graviton configurations are identified as consistent with universal soft graviton theorems. In coherent states, the expectation value of the shear operator reproduces known classical graviton scattering at lowest nontrivial order.

concepts.name: Ultraviolet Divergences and Renormalization
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies the structural reason why the NSF expansion avoids ultraviolet divergences: the absence of off-shell virtual gravitons and loop integrations over four-dimensional momentum space eliminates the source of UV divergences present in the covariant approach. Unlike covariant quantum gravity, which requires an ever-growing set of counterterms, each term in the NSF expansion is finite by construction due to the compactness of the integration domain and the on-shell nature of all fields. The paper also draws an instructive analogy with QED, noting that while QED's perturbative series is asymptotic and requires renormalization at each order, NSF terms are genuinely finite without renormalization.

concepts.name: Quantum Fisher Information and Cramér-Rao Bound
concepts.contribution: The paper derives analytical expressions for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) and classical Fisher information (FI) for estimating spatial Fourier components of an arbitrary incoherent sample, using the symmetric logarithmic derivative formalism. It shows that the ratio of FI to QFI for direct imaging degrades at high spatial frequencies, and that this gap can be partially closed through optical pre-processing. The work thus establishes a concrete quantum-to-classical efficiency metric that guides the design of optimal imaging measurements.

concepts.name: Optical Transfer Function Engineering
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces Fourier Domain Division (FDD), a method that partitions the pupil plane into multiple regions each encoded with a distinct blazed grating, generating separate images whose optical transfer functions have reduced DC values relative to their high-frequency content. By showing that Fisher information scales as the square of the OTF divided by its zero-frequency value, the work reframes quantum measurement optimization as a classical OTF engineering problem. This provides a general and extensible strategy applicable to nonlinear, structured-illumination, and other imaging modalities.

concepts.name: Shot Noise in Photon-Starved Imaging
concepts.contribution: The paper quantitatively analyzes how Poisson shot noise disproportionately buries high spatial frequency components in conventional direct imaging, deriving the minimum photon budget required to achieve a target signal-to-noise ratio as a function of resolution. It demonstrates experimentally that FDD reduces the required photon count by a factor of five for high-frequency components, achieving comparable image quality to direct imaging at one-fifth the photon budget. This directly addresses the fundamental quantum noise limit in low-light microscopy, astronomy, and remote sensing.

concepts.name: Wiener Filter and Image Reconstruction
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a generalized Wiener filter that optimally combines information from multiple FDD sub-images in the Fourier domain by minimizing mean square error, and proves analytically that this estimator saturates the classical Cramér-Rao bound in the low-regularization limit. The filter is applied iteratively to handle its dependence on the unknown ground truth, with convergence validated both theoretically and experimentally. This extends classical Wiener deconvolution to multi-channel measurements with heterogeneous OTFs arising from quantum-optimized pupil segmentation.

2605.05942v1.title: Architecture Shape Governs QNN Trainability: Jacobian Null Space Growth and Parameter Efficiency

concepts.name: Quantum State Space Geometry (CP¹ Manifold)
concepts.contribution: The paper exploits the fact that a single-qubit pure state lives on CP¹ ≅ S², a real two-dimensional manifold, to prove that all parameter gradients share a common global phase at every input point. This geometric constraint is shown to be the root cause of a hard rank ceiling of 2L+1 on the coefficient-matching Jacobian, regardless of how many trainable parameters are added, a result termed structural gradient starvation.

concepts.name: Fourier Analysis of Variational Quantum Circuits
concepts.contribution: Building on the known result that angle-encoded VQCs implement truncated Fourier series, the paper proves that the accessible frequency spectrum depends only on the total encoding budget E=NL and is identical across all architecture shapes at fixed E. It then shows that despite this spectral equivalence, trainability varies dramatically with architecture shape, isolating Jacobian rank deficiency rather than expressivity or spectral bias as the governing mechanism.

concepts.name: Jacobian Rank and Null Space in Parametric Optimization
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces the coefficient-matching Jacobian J as the central diagnostic for QNN trainability, proving that for serial single-qubit circuits rank(J) ≤ 2L+1 generically while the null space dimension grows without bound as parameters are added. For parallel multi-qubit architectures, independent local phases across qubits prevent this rank collapse, maintaining σ_min(J) > 0 generically up to the shared threshold P = 2E+1, providing a structural rather than statistical explanation for the trainability gap.

concepts.name: Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM)
concepts.contribution: The paper employs a data-Jacobian variant of the QFIM, defined as Ĝ = J_data^T J_data / n, as an empirical spectral diagnostic to distinguish two routes of increasing parameter count. It demonstrates that adding feature-map encoding layers monotonically shifts the spectral knee of this matrix rightward, reflecting genuinely new accessible Fourier directions, while adding trainable ansatz blocks leaves the spectral knee frozen at the fixed rank ceiling, confirming that only the encoding-layer route engages a quantum-specific optimization mechanism.

2605.05916v1.title: Squeezed Gravitons and One-Loop Self-Energy under Light-Cone Smearing

concepts.name: Light-Cone Smearing by Graviton Fluctuations
concepts.contribution: The paper systematically extends the framework of light-cone smearing to multiple physically distinct graviton quantum states—vacuum, coherent, and two-mode squeezed—by treating the first-order correction to Synge's world function as a quantum operator. It demonstrates that the smearing width is state-dependent: coherent states (classical gravitational waves) merely shift the light-cone position without broadening it, while squeezed vacuum states genuinely modify the Gaussian smearing width, either enhancing or suppressing it depending on the squeezed quadrature.

concepts.name: Ultraviolet Regularization via Quantum Gravity
concepts.contribution: The paper provides the first concrete demonstration that light-cone smearing from graviton fluctuations renders finite specific one-loop amplitudes that were previously found to retain residual singularities. For the φ³ bubble diagram, the short-distance singularity at coincident points is removed and the smearing variance ⟨σ̂₁²⟩ acts as a physical UV regulator analogous to the 1/ε pole in dimensional regularization, while for the φ⁴ tadpole diagram, the quadratic UV divergence is replaced by a finite expression scaling as the inverse square root of the smearing variance.

concepts.name: Squeezed Graviton States from Inflation
concepts.contribution: The paper calculates explicitly how primordial gravitons produced during inflation, which are naturally described as two-mode squeezed states with large squeezing parameters for superhorizon modes, contribute to the light-cone smearing variance through their long-wavelength power spectrum. It estimates the resulting finite relative correction to the one-loop self-energy to be of order (H/M_pl)² N_eff ∼ 10⁻¹⁰, and discusses its potential—though extremely challenging—observability in high-precision measurements such as the lepton anomalous magnetic moment.

concepts.name: Synge's World Function as a Quantum Operator
concepts.contribution: The paper promotes the geodesic interval Synge's world function to a quantum operator by treating the linear metric perturbation h_μν as a quantum field, and evaluates the expectation value of the exponential e^{iuσ̂₁} using the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff identity to extract a Gaussian characteristic function controlled by the state-dependent variance. This operator-level formalism provides a rigorous and generalizable method for computing state-dependent corrections to field propagators in perturbative quantum gravity, connecting directly to the concept of an effective minimal length at the Planck scale.

2605.05914v1.title: Quantum-enhanced Large Language Models on Quantum Hardware via Cayley Unitary Adapters

concepts.name: Unitary Quantum Circuits and Amplitude Encoding
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces the Cayley Unitary Adapter (CUA), which parameterizes unitary matrices via the Cayley transform of skew-symmetric matrices, guaranteeing exact orthogonality with n(n-1)/2 free parameters per block — a 62.5% reduction over dense parameterization for 4×4 blocks. Classical activation vectors are amplitude-encoded into quantum states, transformed by the unitary gate on hardware, and reconstructed from measurement counts, demonstrating end-to-end unitary circuit execution within a production-scale neural network inference pipeline. This constitutes the first verified execution of such circuits on a 156-qubit superconducting processor for autoregressive language generation.

concepts.name: Quantum Noise and Decoherence
concepts.contribution: The paper characterizes a sharp noise-expressivity phase transition: at 2 qubits (total depolarizing infidelity λ=1.2%), perplexity degrades by only 0.02 points and language structure remains coherent, while at 3 qubits (λ=11.9%) perplexity increases 35-fold and at 4 qubits output degenerates to random tokens. Two-qubit CZ gates are identified as dominating the error budget (59% of gate infidelity despite comprising 17% of gates), precisely locating the exact-synthesis feasibility frontier at 2–3 qubits for current IBM Heron r2 hardware.

concepts.name: Operator Entanglement and Schmidt Decomposition
concepts.contribution: The paper applies operator Schmidt decomposition to diagnose the entanglement structure of trained Cayley unitaries, finding that the block-diagonal unitary saturates the algebraic operator Schmidt rank at its natural 10|2 bipartition (rank 16/16) while trained SmolLM2 unitaries exhibit entropy ratios of only 4.7–7.8% of the Haar-random maximum. This analysis establishes that the CUA is a strictly different ansatz class from brickwork variational quantum circuits, which require at least four layers of depth to match the rank achieved by the CUA at zero circuit depth, motivating approximate compilation as the near-term path to larger qubit scales.

concepts.name: Variational Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Machine Learning
concepts.contribution: Rather than employing standard variational quantum circuits with gate-angle parameterization trained via the parameter-shift rule, the paper introduces a complementary approach where unitary parameters are trained entirely classically through the Cayley transform and then frozen on the QPU, avoiding the overhead of on-hardware gradient evaluation. The quantum scaling argument demonstrates that a depth-D brickwork circuit on n qubits uses O(nD) gate parameters to explore a 2^n-dimensional unitary space, providing exponentially compressed parameterization compared to the classical Cayley representation requiring 2^n(2^n-1)/2 parameters — framing QPU execution as a parameter-efficient structured prior rather than a computational speedup.

2605.05903v1.title: Trace anomaly, effective approach, and gravitational potential

concepts.name: Quantum Corrections to the Newtonian Potential
concepts.contribution: The paper computes one-loop semiclassical corrections to the Newtonian gravitational potential using two distinct methods: the effective quantum gravity approach and the anomaly-induced effective action approach. It finds that the effective approach yields an O(1/r³) correction, consistent with prior work, while the anomaly-induced approach in the Boulware vacuum yields a sub-leading O(1/r⁴) correction. This discrepancy reveals a fundamental tension between the two frameworks that remains unresolved.

concepts.name: Trace (Conformal) Anomaly and Anomaly-Induced Effective Action
concepts.contribution: The paper applies the anomaly-induced effective action of gravity, localized via two auxiliary scalar fields satisfying fourth-order Paneitz-operator equations, to derive the stress-energy tensor of conformal matter fields on a Schwarzschild background. It demonstrates explicitly that the asymptotic behavior of the anomaly-induced stress tensor in the Boulware vacuum falls off as r⁻⁶, and shows through a systematic power-series analysis that no choice of integration constants can produce the r⁻⁵ falloff that would be needed to match the effective approach result.

concepts.name: Vacuum States in Curved Spacetime (Boulware Vacuum)
concepts.contribution: The paper highlights that, unlike the effective quantum gravity approach, the anomaly-induced method requires an explicit choice of quantum vacuum state through boundary conditions on the auxiliary fields. By selecting the Boulware vacuum—appropriate for a static observer far from a black hole—the authors show that the resulting stress tensor and gravitational potential correction differ qualitatively from those obtained without a vacuum-state specification, underscoring the physical importance of vacuum ambiguity in semiclassical gravity calculations.

concepts.name: Effective Field Theory Approach to Quantum Gravity
concepts.contribution: The paper adapts the gauge-fixing-independent scheme of Dalvit-Mazzitelli and de Paula Netto et al. to the specific case of massless conformal matter fields, deriving the invariant beta-function combination that governs the leading logarithmic correction to the gravitational action. It confirms that this approach produces O(1/r³) corrections to the Newtonian potential regardless of whether gravitons or conformal matter fields run in the loops, demonstrating the universality of the functional form while the coefficient changes with field content.

2605.05881v1.title: Surface-Code Thresholds and Qubit Footprints in Shuttling-Based Spin-Qubit Railways

concepts.name: Quantum Error Correction Thresholds
concepts.contribution: The paper quantifies fault-tolerant thresholds for rotated surface codes (both CSS and XZZX variants) mapped onto a 2×N railway architecture under circuit-level biased noise. It demonstrates that shuttling check qubits instead of data qubits systematically raises thresholds, with the XZZX code under Z-biased noise reaching up to 4.0×10⁻³, compared to approximately 2.2×10⁻³ for symmetric depolarizing noise. This establishes that code choice and shuttling strategy together determine the effective threshold in constrained linear geometries.

concepts.name: Biased Noise Channels in Quantum Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a physically grounded, asymmetric Pauli error channel for shuttling spin qubits by decomposing noise contributions from micromagnet field gradients, trajectory deviations, and spin-orbit coupling into additive covariance terms. It provides explicit analytical expressions relating geometric parameters of the shuttling path to the resulting Z-to-X error bias ratios, showing how confinement geometry and crystallographic alignment can be used to engineer the noise asymmetry. This connects device-level physical parameters directly to the circuit-level error model used in threshold simulations.

concepts.name: Topological Code Design for Hardware-Specific Noise
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that matching the XZZX surface code structure to the inherent dephasing bias of silicon spin-qubit shuttling operations yields footprint reductions of 33–75% compared to a symmetric noise baseline. Specifically, it shows that a distance-7 XZZX code at a physical error rate of p=10⁻³ under full bias can reach the Megaquop regime with only 97 physical qubits. This establishes hardware-aware code selection as a critical design principle for early fault-tolerant processors.

concepts.name: Coherent Electron Shuttling in Semiconductor Qubits
concepts.contribution: The paper models the spin dynamics of an electron transported through a spatially inhomogeneous micromagnet field and spin-orbit coupling environment, decomposing the evolution into deterministic coherent rotations and stochastic incoherent errors. It proposes a 'Train Schedule' shuttling protocol for the 2×N railway that minimizes idling and shuttling instances while satisfying stabilizer commutation constraints and suppressing hook errors. This provides a concrete, physically motivated protocol for implementing syndrome extraction in a linear spin-qubit architecture.

2605.05841v1.title: Non-Abelian String-Breaking Dynamics on a Qudit Quantum Computer

concepts.name: Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theories and Confinement
concepts.contribution: This paper provides the first real-time quantum simulation of string breaking in a pure SU(2) lattice gauge theory, where gauge-field self-interactions alone drive the breaking process without dynamical matter. It experimentally distinguishes between unbreakable half-integer-flux strings (fundamental charges) and breakable integer-flux strings (adjoint charges), demonstrating that the non-Abelian fusion rule 1/2 ⊗ 1/2 = 0 ⊕ 1 is the essential mechanism enabling gluonic screening. The work resolves coherent, phase-sensitive string oscillations and glueball production in real time, phenomena inaccessible to classical simulation methods.

concepts.name: Qudit Quantum Computing and Hardware-Efficient Encoding
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces a hardware-optimized encoding that maps truncated SU(2) gauge fields onto native multi-level trapped-ion qudits (up to d=8), using a basis transformation called the bubble-chain representation to convert multi-body plaquette interactions into single-qudit operations. This approach reduces the entangling gate count by approximately a factor of 16 compared to an equivalent qubit-based implementation, demonstrating a concrete resource advantage. The work establishes qudit processors as a natural and scalable platform for simulating non-Abelian gauge theories whose physical Hilbert spaces are intrinsically higher-dimensional.

concepts.name: Trotterized Digital Quantum Simulation
concepts.contribution: The experiment implements second-order Suzuki-Trotter time evolution to simulate the real-time dynamics of the SU(2) lattice gauge theory Hamiltonian, validating that the digital circuit faithfully captures full-Hamiltonian dynamics beyond a perturbative effective model. The paper carefully characterizes Trotter errors by comparing exact, Trotterized, and experimental results, showing systematic resonance peak shifts attributable to finite step-size errors. It also exploits gauge constraints (Gauss's law) to reduce circuit complexity, since unphysical transitions need not be generated or canceled at the circuit level.

concepts.name: Quantum Simulation of High-Energy Physics Phenomena
concepts.contribution: This work extends quantum simulation of confinement and string breaking from previously studied Abelian gauge theories to the qualitatively distinct non-Abelian regime relevant to QCD. By observing coherent, resonance-tunable string breaking driven purely by gluonic excitations on a minimal three-plaquette ladder geometry, it demonstrates spatio-temporal resolution of non-perturbative dynamics that are inaccessible to high-energy collider experiments or classical lattice QCD at real time. The results establish a proof-of-principle pathway toward simulating larger SU(2) and eventually SU(3) gauge theories on quantum hardware.

2605.05830v1.title: Three wave mixing vacuum squeezing generation in a SNAIL-based Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier with alternated flux polarity

concepts.name: Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplification
concepts.contribution: This paper demonstrates that residual three-wave mixing (3WM), arising from fabrication imperfections in a SNAIL-based JTWPA designed for four-wave mixing (4WM), can be harnessed for vacuum squeezing generation. It provides an experimental procedure to identify optimal magnetic flux bias points that minimize competing 4WM processes, enabling effective 3WM parametric amplification. The work extends the known operating regimes of JTWPAs beyond their nominal design intent.

concepts.name: Microwave Squeezed State Generation
concepts.contribution: The paper presents the first experimental demonstration of both single-mode and two-mode vacuum squeezing via residual 3WM in a SNAIL JTWPA, achieving approximately 3 dB of single-mode squeezing below the vacuum level. It shows that competing 4WM nonlinearities critically degrade squeezing performance, and that careful flux-bias selection is necessary to suppress this competition. The 3WM regime offers a practical advantage by placing the pump frequency well separated from the squeezed photon band, simplifying pump filtering.

concepts.name: Nonlinear Mixing Competition in Josephson Metamaterials
concepts.contribution: The paper systematically investigates how simultaneous activation of 3WM and 4WM nonlinearities in a flux-tunable SNAIL array degrades phase-sensitive gain, single-mode squeezing, and two-mode entanglement. By comparing two flux operating points with similar 3WM idler power but differing 4WM idler power, it isolates the detrimental role of 4WM competition on squeezing. This provides new quantitative insight into how nonlinear process competition limits quantum state generation in Josephson metamaterial devices.

concepts.name: Continuous-Variable Entanglement and Logarithmic Negativity
concepts.contribution: The paper reconstructs full two-mode covariance matrices from repeated quadrature measurements and uses logarithmic negativity as a witness for signal-idler entanglement generated via residual 3WM. It demonstrates that entanglement is observable only at the optimized flux point where 4WM is suppressed, and documents the pump-power-dependent rise and subsequent degradation of logarithmic negativity consistent with prior TWPA squeezer observations. This contributes experimental evidence linking nonlinear process competition directly to the quality of generated continuous-variable entangled states in the microwave domain.

2605.05827v1.title: Pontus-Mpemba effect in cavity quantum electrodynamics

concepts.name: Quantum Mpemba Effect
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the quantum Mpemba effect to the Pontus-Mpemba variant, where accelerated relaxation arises from a two-step evolution protocol applied to identical initial states rather than distinct initial states. It demonstrates this in the dissipative Jaynes-Cummings model, providing a concrete and experimentally accessible realization that clarifies the physical mechanism as selective population of fast-decaying Liouvillian eigenmodes.

concepts.name: Dissipative Jaynes-Cummings Model
concepts.contribution: The paper applies the single-excitation sector of the Lindblad-governed Jaynes-Cummings model as a minimal platform to exhibit non-trivial non-equilibrium relaxation phenomena, fully characterizing the Liouvillian eigenspectrum including an exceptional point at a critical cavity decay rate. It shows that the spectral separation between slow (Purcell-enhanced atomic decay at rate ~4g²/κ) and fast (cavity relaxation at rate ~κ) eigenmodes is the key structural feature enabling the Pontus-Mpemba effect.

concepts.name: Liouvillian Exceptional Points and Spectral Structure
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies an exceptional point in the Liouvillian superoperator at a critical normalized decay rate (κ/g)_c = 4, separating underdamped oscillatory relaxation from overdamped exponential decay. It demonstrates that the Pontus-Mpemba protocol operates above this exceptional point, exploiting the pronounced separation between slow and fast decay rates to engineer accelerated thermalization via a cavity Q-switching quench.

concepts.name: Open Quantum Systems and Dissipation Engineering
concepts.contribution: The paper proposes a sudden quench of the cavity decay rate as a practical control knob for steering relaxation trajectories in open quantum systems, showing that coherent vacuum Rabi oscillations during a low-loss stage can transfer population from a slow-decaying initial state into a fast-decaying intermediate state. It demonstrates robustness of the effect against detuning, spontaneous emission, finite switching times, and small thermal photon populations, connecting the results directly to achievable circuit QED and optical cavity QED experimental parameters.

2605.05821v1.title: Quasi-normal modes of a multi-dimensional rotating Kerr black hole

concepts.name: Quasi-Normal Modes (QNMs) of Black Holes
concepts.contribution: The paper derives the quasi-normal modes of a six-dimensional rotating Kerr black hole with compactified extra dimensions by extending the Teukolsky formalism to higher dimensions. It provides numerical tables of fundamental QNM frequencies for various values of the spin parameter, compactification radius, and angular quantum number of the extra dimensions. A key finding is that the imaginary parts of the QNMs exhibit non-monotonic behavior with spin (decreasing for a > 0.2), in contrast to the 4D case, offering a potential observational signature of compactified extra dimensions.

concepts.name: Newman-Penrose Formalism
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs a higher-dimensional analogue of the Newman-Penrose formalism using a new mathematical object called multispinors, which are vectors of two-spinors built from tensor products of SU(2) matrices. It derives the full set of spin coefficients (24 in 6D), null vielbein, Weyl and Ricci scalars, commutation relations of directional derivatives, and Bianchi identities in this extended framework. This provides a working higher-dimensional spinor calculus that mirrors the utility of the original 4D Newman-Penrose approach for analyzing gravitational perturbations.

concepts.name: Teukolsky Equation for Gravitational Perturbations
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a higher-dimensional analogue of the Teukolsky equation for gravitational perturbations of a rotating Kerr black hole in six spacetime dimensions with two extra dimensions compactified to a two-sphere. It demonstrates that the equation is separable when the extra dimensions are compactified, resolving the known non-separability of the generic higher-dimensional case, and reduces to a radial equation that matches results from prior literature with an additional potential term depending on the compactification radius and extra-dimensional eigenvalues.

concepts.name: Higher-Dimensional Spacetime and Extra Dimensions
concepts.contribution: The paper develops a systematic spinor-based framework applicable to even-dimensional spacetimes of arbitrary dimension d > 4 by embedding coordinates into tensor products of SU(2) matrices and introducing multispinors as generalized two-spinor vectors. It shows how Lorentz transformations in 6D and 8D are represented through products of SU(2) operators, recovering the higher-dimensional Lorentz group. The framework is explicitly applied to a 6D Kerr metric with compactified extra dimensions modeled as a two-sphere of curvature radius R, establishing how the compactification radius and extra-dimensional quantum numbers modify observable gravitational wave signatures.

2605.05817v1.title: Classical General Relativity as a Non-Conservative Action-Dependent Field Theory

concepts.name: Conformal Decomposition of the Metric in General Relativity
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the conformal factor of the spacetime metric is a redundant degree of freedom from the perspective of observable dynamics, applying Leibniz's Identity of Indiscernibles to justify its elimination. It shows that the full dynamical content of the Einstein-Hilbert action can be recovered from a scale-free Lagrangian depending only on the unimodular metric Gµν and an action-density sector, without any reference to the conformal factor. This provides a complete field-theoretic generalization of results previously known only for homogeneous cosmological models.

concepts.name: Contact Geometry and Non-Conservative Field Theory (Herglotz Variational Principle)
concepts.contribution: The paper applies a contact reduction by scaling symmetry to the first-order (Palatini) formulation of General Relativity, yielding an action-dependent (Herglotz) Lagrangian that is intrinsically non-conservative. It extends the multicontact Lagrangian framework to a singular, gauge field-theoretic setting, showing that eliminating the scaling variable necessarily introduces frictional, action-dependent terms to compensate for the removed degree of freedom. The resulting field equations explicitly couple the geometric degrees of freedom to an action-density sector sµ, making the non-conservative structure manifest.

concepts.name: Gravitational Wave Perturbation Theory and Backreaction
concepts.contribution: At linear order, the paper shows that metric perturbations around flat space satisfy the standard free wave equation, with the action-dependent sector serving only to reorganize gauge degrees of freedom rather than alter propagation. At second order, however, the backreaction of gravitational waves is shown to be governed by non-conservative dynamics: energy is exchanged between the geometric perturbations and the action-density sector sµ, preventing a description in terms of an effective conserved energy-momentum tensor. This provides a qualitatively distinct interpretation of gravitational wave self-interaction that is dynamically equivalent to, but structurally different from, the standard general relativistic picture.

concepts.name: Unimodular Gravity and Reduced Diffeomorphism Symmetry
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs a reformulation of General Relativity that is invariant only under volume-preserving (unimodular) diffeomorphisms rather than the full diffeomorphism group, as a natural consequence of fixing the metric determinant. It carefully distinguishes this construction from standard unimodular gravity, emphasizing that the reduction of gauge symmetry must be accompanied by a compensatory action-dependent term to faithfully reproduce all of General Relativity's dynamics, not merely its trace-free sector. The interplay between the reduced gauge freedom and dynamical constraints is analyzed explicitly in the weak-field limit, showing that the two physical gravitational wave polarizations are correctly recovered.

2605.05816v1.title: Massive hybrid stars within the extended three-flavor quark-meson diquark model

concepts.name: Equation of State for Dense Quark Matter
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a stiff intermediate-density equation of state using the extended three-flavor quark-meson diquark (EQMD) model, which incorporates vector and axial-vector mesons as essential degrees of freedom. The inclusion of these vector mesons is shown to be necessary to stiffen the EoS sufficiently at intermediate densities, enabling the construction of hybrid stars consistent with astrophysical mass-radius observations and perturbative QCD constraints simultaneously. The bag constant is determined self-consistently by matching number densities at the quark-hadron transition boundary.

concepts.name: Color Superconductivity in Neutron Stars
concepts.contribution: The paper models the transition from normal quark matter to the color-flavor locked (CFL) phase within a renormalizable low-energy effective model that includes diquark condensates as explicit degrees of freedom. It finds that stars with masses above roughly 2 solar masses harbor a quark core with central baryon densities at or above 3.9 times nuclear saturation density, suggesting the presence of a color superconducting phase. The model also reproduces the expected asymptotic behavior of equal diquark gaps and vanishing quark condensates at high density characteristic of the ideal CFL phase.

concepts.name: Speed of Sound in Dense Matter
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies a double-peak structure in the speed of sound squared as a function of baryon chemical potential, attributing the dip between the peaks to the melting of the strange quark condensate as density increases. It derives analytically that the speed of sound approaches the conformal limit from above at asymptotically large chemical potentials when a nonzero quartic vector coupling is present, contrasting with the behavior seen in the NJL model with vector interactions. This three-flavor feature is shown to be absent in a two-flavor system, highlighting the physical role of strange quark dynamics.

concepts.name: Hybrid Star Mass-Radius Relation
concepts.contribution: By solving the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkov equation with the EQMD equation of state matched to a realistic nuclear EoS via a Maxwell-like density-matching construction, the paper produces hybrid star mass-radius curves consistent with multiple NICER and radio-timing pulsar observations including objects near 2 solar masses. The results indicate that the quark-vector meson coupling constant is the dominant parameter controlling EoS stiffness and hence maximum stellar mass, with three parameter sets spanning the range of current observational constraints. The study also shows that quark core radii for maximum-mass stars range from approximately 3.8 to 4.6 km depending on parameter choice.

2605.05815v1.title: Room temperature Purcell enhanced single erbium ions in silicon-carbide-on-insulator microring resonators

concepts.name: Purcell Enhancement
concepts.contribution: This paper demonstrates a Purcell factor of 69.8 for single erbium ions in a 4H-SiCOI microring resonator operating at room temperature, achieved by optimizing mode overlap between the cavity and the Er3+ emission dipole. This represents nearly an order of magnitude improvement over previously reported Purcell factors for color centers in 4H-SiCOI microring resonators. The enhancement reduces the intrinsic millisecond-scale optical lifetime of Er3+ to tens of microseconds, making single-photon detection practically feasible.

concepts.name: Single-Photon Emission
concepts.contribution: The paper reports the first observation of fully integrated single-photon emission from ion-implanted Er3+ defects in a 4H-SiCOI photonic platform at room temperature, confirmed by a photon autocorrelation value of g(2)(0) = 0.04 without background correction. This result is achieved using a single-detector photon correlation scheme enabled by the long Purcell-reduced lifetime relative to detector dead time. The work establishes that room-temperature single-photon emission in the telecom C-band is achievable without cryogenic cooling in this material system.

concepts.name: Spectral Diffusion in Solid-State Emitters
concepts.contribution: The paper measures spectral diffusion linewidths as narrow as 54.76 ± 1.8 MHz for single Er3+ transitions in 4H-SiCOI at room temperature, which is narrower than previously reported values for Er3+ in silicon-on-insulator measured at cryogenic temperatures below 4K. This result is attributed to the stable lattice incorporation and reduced local strain of Er3+ in 4H-SiC, and suggests the 4H-SiCOI host offers superior spectral stability for telecom-band emitters.

concepts.name: Zeeman Effect in Spin-Photon Interfaces
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates magnetic-field-dependent Zeeman splitting of single Er3+ optical transitions in 4H-SiCOI, extracting a differential g-factor of Δg = 17.59 ± 0.6 GHz/T consistent with a spin-preserving Er3+ transition. This confirms the spin-1/2 nature of individual Er3+ defects and their potential as spin qubits addressable via optical transitions in the telecom C-band. The observed splitting is consistent with C3v defect symmetry, suggesting Er3+ occupies a silicon-substitutional site in the SiC lattice.

2605.05785v1.title: Optical Pulling Force in Carbon Nanotubes: Manifestation of Nonlocal Conductivity

concepts.name: Nonlocal (Spatially Dispersive) Conductivity
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a nonlocal surface conductivity for finite-length zigzag carbon nanotubes using the Kubo formalism adapted for Dirac pseudospin electrons, decomposing it into interband and intraband components. It shows that spatial dispersion introduces a second-order spatial derivative correction to the current-field relation, and demonstrates that this nonlocality is the direct physical origin of the optical pulling force, which vanishes entirely in the local limit.

concepts.name: Optical Pulling Force (Negative Optical Force)
concepts.contribution: The paper provides the first theoretical demonstration of a negative optical force (pulling) in a carbon nanotube, showing it arises exclusively from the nonlocal conductivity rather than from structured illumination or interference effects. The pulling effect is localized to specific frequency windows tied to the threshold for collisionless (Landau) attenuation and is most pronounced for short CNTs (100–200 nm), disappearing for longer tubes where nonlocality becomes negligible.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic Scattering from Finite-Length Cylindrical Conductors (Edge Effects)
concepts.contribution: The paper formulates the optical force problem using a Fredholm integral equation of the second kind for the axial surface current on a finite-length CNT, rigorously incorporating edge (end-termination) effects through additional boundary conditions and Dirichlet Green functions. It shows that edge effects are essential for the emergence of the pulling force and that an infinite-length approximation fails to capture this optomechanical behavior.

concepts.name: Maxwell Stress Tensor and Optomechanical Forces on Low-Dimensional Conductors
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a regularized expression for the axial optical force by integrating the Maxwell stress tensor over the CNT surface, expressing the result in terms of surface current density and axial electric field rather than volume fields. It demonstrates that the local conductivity model produces nonintegrable singularities in the stress tensor diagonal elements, while the nonlocal model removes these divergences, making the force integral mathematically well-posed and physically consistent.

2605.05783v1.title: Isomer depletion via nuclear excitation by inelastic electron scattering

concepts.name: Nuclear Excitation by Inelastic Electron Scattering (NEIES)
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the theoretical treatment of NEIES into the low-electron-energy and low-nuclear-transition-energy regime, which had been previously understudied. Using the Dirac distorted wave Born approximation, it systematically maps how cross sections depend on atomic number, ion charge state, transition energy, and multipole order. It reveals that NEIES has a weaker dependence on transition energy and multipolarity compared to radiative decay, making it relatively more effective for high-multipolarity or low-energy transitions.

concepts.name: Nuclear Isomer Depletion
concepts.contribution: The paper applies the NEIES mechanism as a controllable method to trigger isomer depletion by exciting a nucleus from its isomeric state to a gateway state that can then decay below the isomer. It quantitatively evaluates this approach for three physically distinct isomers—93mMo, 152mEu, and 178mHf—covering E2, M1, and M2 transition scenarios. Estimated depletion event rates of up to ~10^8 per second are reported under realistic electron flux conditions, demonstrating practical feasibility.

concepts.name: Electron Screening and Ionic State Effects on Nuclear Processes
concepts.contribution: By comparing cross sections for neutral atoms and fully stripped bare nuclei across all cases studied, the paper quantifies the screening effect of bound electrons on the NEIES process. It finds that the screening effect is weak—cross sections for neutral atoms and bare nuclei differ by less than an order of magnitude—especially at higher electron energies, contrasting sharply with strongly ionic-state-dependent processes like NEEC and NEET.

concepts.name: Nuclear Transition Multipole Matrix Elements and Selection Rules
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a comprehensive numerical analysis showing that higher multipole transitions (e.g., E4, M3) are strongly suppressed in NEIES due to the requirement for large angular momentum quantum numbers in the partial-wave expansion of low-energy electrons. It demonstrates that the suppression per order of multipolarity in NEIES (roughly 5–7 orders of magnitude) is substantially less severe than the corresponding suppression in radiative decay rates, offering insight into when electron-driven excitation is advantageous over photon-driven excitation.

2605.05764v1.title: Weighted Phase-Space Paths for Exact Wigner Dynamics

concepts.name: Wigner Function and Phase-Space Quantum Mechanics
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes that the Wigner function is the unique phase-space object selected by requiring reproduction of all Weyl-ordered expectation values, not merely Born marginals. It clarifies that Wigner negativity is not a representational defect but a structural necessity: exact quantum phase-space dynamics cannot generally be encoded in a positive probability density. The paper also introduces a residual diagnostic that quantifies how much the Wigner–Moyal generator departs from classical Liouville transport at the level of the generator itself.

concepts.name: Wigner–Moyal Equation and Fokker–Planck Incompatibility
concepts.contribution: The paper provides a precise, generator-level proof that for non-quadratic potentials the Wigner–Moyal operator contains higher odd momentum derivatives that cannot be reproduced by any positive second-order Fokker–Planck operator. This is demonstrated numerically with a quartic oscillator, where omitting the signed Moyal residual produces an order-10^-2 Wigner L2 error, while restoring it reduces the error to order 10^-5. The paper thereby concretely isolates what classical carrier transport misses in anharmonic quantum dynamics.

concepts.name: Weighted Stochastic Phase-Space Representations
concepts.contribution: The paper reframes Wigner dynamics as a weighted empirical measure, F_W(z,t) = E_P[W_t δ(z−z_t)], where carrier paths are sampled from a positive measure but the quantum state is reconstructed through signed weights rather than unweighted trajectory densities. Choosing classical Hamiltonian flow as the carrier cleanly separates classical Liouville transport from the nonclassical Moyal residual, which can then be represented by signed weights or branching events. This resolves the three-way tension between positivity, phase space, and exact quantum dynamics by abandoning the requirement that the Wigner function itself be a positive trajectory density.

concepts.name: Forward–Reverse Path Measures and Interference Parity
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a signed analogue of classical fluctuation relations for Wigner path measures, decomposing the forward-to-reversed signed-measure ratio as A_sign · exp(A_mag), where A_mag captures carrier and absolute-weight asymmetries and A_sign is a sign factor with no classical probabilistic counterpart. This sign factor, called the interference parity, records whether forward and time-reversed path contributions enter constructively or destructively in the Wigner quasiprobability reconstruction. The paper explicitly distinguishes this quantity from thermodynamic entropy production, situating it instead within quasiprobability frameworks where signed contributions encode genuinely quantum interference effects.

2605.05721v1.title: Electronic and Photonic Integration of Single Quantum Emitters in 2D Materials

concepts.name: Purcell Effect
concepts.contribution: The paper surveys how coupling 2D material quantum emitters to on-chip resonators (photonic crystal nanobeams, microrings) and off-chip cavities (open Fabry-Pérot, circular Bragg gratings) modifies the local density of optical states to enhance spontaneous emission rates. It connects measured lifetime shortening on resonance to practical metrics such as increased photon flux and reduced effective emission timescale, and frames Purcell enhancement as a lever that also eases downstream electrical switching constraints by lowering the required drive current.

concepts.name: Quantum-Confined Stark Effect
concepts.contribution: The paper reviews how applied vertical electric fields shift the optical transition energies of localized excitons in TMDs and defect color centers in hBN through both linear (permanent dipole) and quadratic (polarizability) Stark responses, with reported tuning ranges spanning a few meV to tens of meV. It positions this tunability not merely as spectral adjustment but as a co-functional tool with charge stabilization, enabling spectral matching between emitters and narrowband photonic resonances and directly impacting photon indistinguishability metrics.

concepts.name: Charge Noise and Spectral Diffusion in Solid-State Emitters
concepts.contribution: The paper systematically connects fluctuating nearby charges in the solid-state host to stochastic Stark shifts, optical dephasing, linewidth broadening, and temporal spectral wandering that degrade the coherence time T2 and photon indistinguishability. It reviews how electrostatic gating suppresses these mechanisms by sweeping mobile carriers toward electrodes and controlling trap occupation, reporting near-transform-limited linewidths as low as 89 MHz under optimized gate conditions, and frames charge control as essential rather than optional for reproducible quantum-light-source operation.

concepts.name: Electroluminescence from Localized Excitonic and Defect States
concepts.contribution: The paper organizes the progression of electrically injected single-photon emission in 2D materials across three device archetypes—vertical vdW tunnel junctions, double-barrier LEDs, and gate-defined lateral p-i-n junctions—and benchmarks their performance from early demonstrations (g(2)(0) ≈ 0.29) to improved lateral junction devices (g(2)(0) ≈ 0.085 at nanoampere currents). It extends this analysis to hBN color centers where wide-bandgap defect-state-assisted tunneling governs excitation, identifying the competition between radiative recombination and tunneling escape as the key design parameter and outlining pathways toward GHz-rate pulsed operation through contact engineering and radiative-rate enhancement.

2605.05663v1.title: Scalar-Field Reconstruction of Ricci--Gauss--Bonnet Dark Energy in Hořava--Lifshitz Cosmology

concepts.name: Hořava–Lifshitz Gravity
concepts.contribution: The paper embeds a Ricci–Gauss–Bonnet dark energy model within the Hořava–Lifshitz cosmological framework, deriving modified Friedmann equations and effective dark-energy density and pressure expressions that reflect the theory's anisotropic scaling and higher-order spatial curvature terms. It demonstrates that the modified gravitational dynamics of HL gravity alter the scalar-field reconstruction procedure and influence the resulting stability and thermodynamic behavior of the dark-energy sector. The effective gravitational coupling appearing in the horizon entropy is treated as a phenomenological parameter encoding deviations from standard General Relativity.

concepts.name: Scalar-Field Reconstruction of Dark Energy
concepts.contribution: The paper derives explicit analytical expressions for the kinetic term and potential of an effective scalar field that reproduces the Ricci–Gauss–Bonnet dark energy density and pressure under a power-law scale factor ansatz within Hořava–Lifshitz cosmology. The reconstructed potential gradient, phase-space trajectories, and equation-of-state parameter are analyzed, revealing a smooth transition from a Gauss–Bonnet-dominated early-time regime to a Ricci-driven late-time accelerated phase. The effective equation-of-state parameter exhibits quintessence-like behavior and remains above the phantom boundary without encountering divergences for physically admissible parameter choices.

concepts.name: Classical Stability of Dark Energy Perturbations
concepts.contribution: The paper evaluates the squared sound speed of the effective Ricci–Gauss–Bonnet dark energy fluid and identifies the parameter-space regions where it remains positive, establishing classical stability against small perturbations. It finds that stability requires the Gauss–Bonnet coupling parameter to be sufficiently large and the power-law index to satisfy 1 < n < 4/3, so that the higher-curvature Gauss–Bonnet contribution dominates over the Ricci term in the numerator of the sound speed expression. The analysis highlights that classical stability is inherently regime-dependent within the Hořava–Lifshitz framework, with ultraviolet Gauss–Bonnet effects governing early times and Ricci curvature governing the infrared limit.

concepts.name: Generalized Second Law of Thermodynamics in Cosmology
concepts.contribution: The paper investigates the validity of the generalized second law of thermodynamics at the apparent horizon by computing the total entropy production rate as the sum of the horizon entropy and the entropy of the effective dark-energy fluid enclosed by it. It shows analytically that the total entropy variation remains non-negative throughout cosmic evolution for a wide range of model parameters, with the monotonic growth of the apparent horizon providing the dominant contribution to entropy production. The analysis incorporates the modified gravitational dynamics of Hořava–Lifshitz gravity through an effective gravitational coupling in the horizon entropy and through the reconstructed dark-energy sector controlling the cosmological evolution.

2605.05658v1.title: Quantum-classical solvation hydrodynamics: Hamiltonian functionals and dissipation

concepts.name: Mixed Quantum-Classical Dynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper replaces the standard quantum-classical Liouville equation with a Koopman wavefunction-based model that preserves positive-definite probability densities and the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. By encoding backreaction between the quantum solute and classical solvent as an explicit energy term in a Hamiltonian functional, the framework captures electronic decoherence beyond what Ehrenfest dynamics can achieve. This is demonstrated concretely for pure-dephasing systems, such as nitric oxide in supercritical argon, where Ehrenfest dynamics fails to retain solute-solvent coupling.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian Hydrodynamics and Poisson Bracket Structure
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a hierarchy of hydrodynamic moment equations by applying closures directly at the level of the Hamiltonian energy functional rather than on the equations of motion, ensuring the resulting systems inherit a rigorous Lie-Poisson bracket structure. New Poisson brackets are constructed systematically to incorporate transported scalars such as specific entropy and backreaction fields, with the Jacobi identity guaranteed by identifying the systems as semidirect-product Lie-Poisson structures. Casimir invariants, including generalizations of hydrodynamic helicity and potential vorticity, are identified for each closure level.

concepts.name: Micropolar and Polar Fluid Theory in Solvation
concepts.contribution: The paper extends Eringen's micropolar fluid theory to the quantum-classical setting by coupling the solvent's orientational degrees of freedom directly to the quantum solute density matrix, so the quantum state remains correlated to both position and molecular orientation. A hybrid Ehrenfest-Koopman closure is introduced in which translational backreaction is treated at the Ehrenfest level while orientational backreaction is fully captured via a sphere Poisson bracket term, reducing computational complexity without sacrificing the key solute-solvent correlations. The framework is then specialized to nonlocal dielectric continua and further simplified via Marcus's local approximation, yielding a tractable Marcus hydrodynamics model.

concepts.name: Dissipation and Polarization Relaxation in Quantum-Classical Systems
concepts.contribution: Beyond conventional viscosity and friction terms, the paper introduces a novel polarization diffusion operator inspired by dynamical density-functional theory that acts selectively on the orientational solvent dynamics without inducing mass diffusion or breaking the unitary evolution of the quantum solute. The dissipative term is constructed so that its spatial average reproduces standard linear polarization diffusion when the fluid density is uniform, while its coefficient can be estimated directly from the experimentally accessible correlation length of the liquid. This provides a physically transparent and thermodynamically consistent route to incorporating dielectric relaxation into a fully quantum-classical hydrodynamic framework.

2605.05635v1.title: Adaptive ray tracing and photon ring signatures of rotating dark-matter-dressed black holes

concepts.name: Black Hole Shadow and Photon Ring Structure
concepts.contribution: The paper systematically compares shadow boundaries, lensing bands, and higher-order photon ring contributions across Kerr, Einasto-supported, and cored-NFW black hole geometries using numerical backward ray tracing. It demonstrates that dark matter dressing modifies not just the primary shadow size but also the location and width of lensing bands and higher-order image structure, with the cored-NFW profile producing the most visible departure from Kerr. This establishes that higher-order lensed images can carry stronger discriminating signatures of dark matter than the shadow boundary alone.

concepts.name: Dark-Matter-Dressed Black Hole Spacetimes
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs effective rotating extensions of two physically motivated static dark matter seed geometries—an Einasto-type regular black hole and a cored-NFW halo black hole—using a modified Newman–Janis procedure, enabling a comparative phenomenological study. It shows that the two profiles produce qualitatively different optical signatures, with the Einasto-supported geometry remaining close to Kerr while the cored-NFW case yields a systematically larger apparent image scale. This comparative framework allows profile-dependent effects to be separated from generic Kerr-like rotational features.

concepts.name: Adaptive Numerical Ray Tracing for Non-Kerr Spacetimes
concepts.contribution: The paper develops a lightweight Hamiltonian-based backward ray-tracing framework that avoids assuming Carter-constant separability, making it applicable to general rotating dark-matter-dressed geometries where analytical separability cannot be guaranteed. An adaptive boundary-search method is used to resolve the shadow contour and lensing bands efficiently without requiring a uniformly dense image-plane grid. The framework is validated against the known analytical Kerr critical curve and shown to be extensible to future radiative-transfer and GRMHD-inspired emission studies.

concepts.name: Spin–Dark Matter Parameter Degeneracy in Black Hole Imaging
concepts.contribution: The paper identifies and characterizes a partial degeneracy between the black hole spin parameter, observer inclination, and dark matter profile parameters, showing that changes in the dark matter dressing can mimic modifications in image size and asymmetry typically attributed to spin or viewing geometry. This degeneracy is present at the level of the shadow boundary, transfer maps, and synthetic intensity distributions, and persists across both the direct and higher-order lensed image components. The results imply that interpreting horizon-scale images purely within the Kerr framework may absorb genuine dark matter effects into inferred spin or inclination values.

2605.05634v1.title: Relativistic mean-field study of the neutron star inner crust using the asymmetric finite difference method

concepts.name: Relativistic Mean-Field Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper applies the RMF framework with TM1-family parameter sets to neutron-rich nuclear clusters in the neutron star inner crust, systematically varying the symmetry-energy slope L and nucleon effective mass. It demonstrates that both parameters critically regulate binding energies, density distributions, neutron radii, and chemical potentials within Wigner-Seitz cells. This extends RMF applications to extremely neutron-rich regimes where continuum and weakly bound states dominate.

concepts.name: Asymmetric Finite Difference Method for the Dirac Equation
concepts.contribution: The paper implements the asymmetric finite difference method to solve radial Dirac equations in Wigner-Seitz cells, eliminating spurious states arising from the fermion-doubling problem without introducing artificial Wilson mass terms. By assigning forward or backward difference formulas to the large and small spinor components based on the sign of the quantum number κ, hermiticity of the Hamiltonian matrix is preserved. This enables a fully quantum-mechanical treatment of dripped neutron states in the inner crust that is more accurate than semiclassical Thomas-Fermi approaches.

concepts.name: Nuclear Symmetry Energy and Its Density Dependence
concepts.contribution: The paper quantifies how the symmetry-energy slope parameter L, varied from 40 to 110 MeV, systematically affects neutron density profiles, root-mean-square radii, and chemical potentials in inner crust layers spanning a wide range of baryon densities. It shows that larger L reduces central neutron density while enhancing surface density, and significantly lowers the neutron chemical potential, with effects that grow more pronounced at higher densities. These results underscore the importance of constraining L for accurately modeling neutron star crust microphysics.

concepts.name: Quantum Shell Effects in Neutron Star Crusts
concepts.contribution: By comparing AFD results with Thomas-Fermi calculations, the paper demonstrates that quantum shell effects produce oscillatory density distributions in the nuclear interior that are entirely absent in the semiclassical approximation. These shell effects enhance the neutron chemical potential and modify neutron radii, with the discrepancy between the two methods being most significant in low-density layers. The findings establish that shell effects are non-negligible for the microscopic structure and equilibrium composition of the inner crust.

2605.05633v1.title: Eigenstate-Selective Entangled Two-Photon Absorption in Monolayer WSe$_2$

concepts.name: Entangled Two-Photon Absorption (ETPA)
concepts.contribution: The paper moves beyond disputed rate-enhancement claims by identifying a symmetry-enforced, qualitatively distinct observable: the Bell-state phase controls which biexciton eigenstates are populated, producing a selection rule with no classical analogue. It also establishes that the Bell state achieves at least twice the dark-eigenstate pumping rate of any separable source, providing a quantitative entanglement benchmark grounded in the Peres-Horodecki separability criterion.

concepts.name: Valley Optical Selection Rules in Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the polarization-to-valley mapping principle from single-exciton to two-photon excitation, showing that the chiral selection rules of monolayer WSe2 enforce a one-to-one correspondence between each circular-polarization branch of an entangled photon pair and a distinct valley pathway. Time-reversal symmetry guaranteeing identical K and K′ response functions is identified as the key condition that allows the Bell-state phase to factorize exactly from the material response.

concepts.name: Biexciton Fine Structure and Electron-Hole Exchange Interaction
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the exchange-split biexciton eigenstates of WSe2 partition into symmetric and antisymmetric superpositions of the cross-circular configurations, and that this symmetry directly maps onto the Bell-state phase to selectively address bright versus exchange-dark eigenstates. It further proposes that the symmetry-based initial-state preparation at φ = π constitutes a novel probe of the otherwise inaccessible Φ3 → Φ2 inter-eigenstate relaxation rate.

concepts.name: Quantum Entanglement and Concurrence in Biphoton States
concepts.contribution: The paper derives an operational identity between the phase-scan visibility of the eigenstate selection rule and the two-qubit concurrence of the biphoton source under local polarization filtering, suggesting that the biexciton manifold of a TMD monolayer can serve as a solid-state readout of source concurrence. It also shows that the Bell state's confinement of all flux to the cross-circular sector—violating the PPT bound by the maximum margin—is the structural origin of the doubled dark-eigenstate pumping rate over any classical source.

2605.05631v1.title: Wandering Exponents and the Free Energy of the High-Dimensional Elastic Polymer

concepts.name: Wandering Exponent and Superdiffusivity
concepts.contribution: The paper provides the first rigorous asymptotic computation of the wandering exponent for the elastic polymer in the high-dimensional (mean-field) limit. It establishes that exponential spatial correlations always yield diffusive behavior (η = 1/2), while power-law correlations with exponent γ < 1 yield superdiffusive behavior with η = 3/(2(γ+2)), confirming and making rigorous the predictions of Mézard and Parisi. A general formula linking the mean-squared displacement to the Parisi overlap measure is derived, from which these exponents follow.

concepts.name: Replica Symmetry Breaking (RSB)
