concepts.contribution: The paper rigorously establishes the replica symmetry breaking phase structure of the elastic polymer in the high-dimensional limit, characterizing the RS, 1RSB, and FRSB phases in terms of explicit conditions on the spatial correlation function B. It proves that the transition from diffusive to superdiffusive behavior coincides exactly with a transition from 1RSB to FRSB in the overlap distribution, providing the first rigorous confirmation of this coincidence. Explicit Parisi measures are computed for the power-law correlator cases.

concepts.name: Quenched Free Energy of Disordered Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a rigorous asymptotic formula for the quenched free energy of the elastic polymer in the high-dimensional continuum limit, expressed as a Parisi-type variational problem over an overlap measure and a radius parameter. It proves that this variational problem has a unique critical point, the Parisi pair (q_c, ζ_c), and that the finite-dimensional Parisi functionals converge to their continuum counterpart as both the system size and spatial dimension diverge. This extends prior rigorous free energy computations from one-site (spin glass) models to a genuine polymer with spatial extent.

concepts.name: Directed Polymer in Random Potential
concepts.contribution: The paper advances the mathematical theory of directed polymers in spatially correlated Gaussian random environments by working in the analytically tractable high-dimensional limit rather than fixed low dimension. It provides the first rigorous asymptotic characterization of both the free energy and the spatial statistics (overlap distribution, mean-squared displacement) of a continuous-space directed polymer with general isotropic spatial correlations. The results rigorously confirm the mean-field picture of Mézard and Parisi and complement existing finite-dimensional lower bounds on the wandering exponent due to Lacoin.

2605.05625v1.title: Quantum Kernels for Parity-Structured Classification: A Hybrid Pipeline

concepts.name: Quantum Hilbert Space Expressivity
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates empirically that a 2^n-dimensional Hilbert space, accessed via the ZZ feature map on n qubits, provides exponentially growing discriminative capacity relative to classical Hamming-based similarity as n increases. This exponential scaling is shown to be the operative source of advantage at high parity complexity, not preprocessing or encoding alone. The work quantifies this via a phase transition at n≈9 where the quantum Hilbert space dimensionality begins to meaningfully outpace classical kernel capacity.

concepts.name: Quantum Phase Interference in Feature Maps
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that binary {0,π} encoding maximizes phase separation in the ZZ feature map's ZiZj entangling gates, creating interference patterns that distinguish parity-flipped quantum states. The product structure (π−xi)(π−xj) of the ZZ gates is shown to encode pairwise bit correlations simultaneously across all qubit pairs, efficiently representing XOR combinatorial structure. This constitutes a concrete demonstration of how quantum phase interference can be deliberately engineered to match a specific problem's discrete symmetry.

concepts.name: Quantum Kernel Methods
concepts.contribution: The paper contributes a controlled ablation methodology that cleanly separates quantum circuit effects from classical preprocessing effects by training a classical RBF SVM on the identical binary-encoded features used by the quantum kernel. It identifies parity complexity as a concrete, tunable axis along which genuine quantum kernel advantage emerges, reaching a 7× improvement in kernel-target alignment at n=11. The work also confirms that theoretical kernel capacity (e.g., a degree-11 polynomial SVM) does not translate to practical advantage at realistic sample sizes, whereas the quantum kernel's implicit Hilbert-space structure does.

concepts.name: Kernel-Target Alignment
concepts.contribution: The paper applies kernel-target alignment as a diagnostic to confirm that the quantum ZZ kernel's geometric structure is intrinsically better matched to the parity label geometry, yielding KTA of 0.094 versus 0.013 for RBF at n=11. KTA is shown to increase monotonically with parity complexity n for the quantum kernel, providing a theoretically grounded explanation for why the accuracy advantage grows with n. This establishes KTA as a reliable early indicator of quantum kernel utility on combinatorially structured problems.

2605.05624v1.title: The General Structure of Trilinear Equations

concepts.name: Hirota Bilinear Formalism and Integrable Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the Hirota bilinear formalism to a trilinear level by introducing a Z3-symmetric trilinear Hirota operator acting on three tau-function slots. It proposes that trilinear equations represent a second universal integrable structure, analogous to but distinct from the bilinear Grassmannian structure of Sato theory, and formulates a precise kernel criterion for identifying such structures.

concepts.name: Ernst Equation and Stationary Axisymmetric Gravity
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that when the Ernst potential is written in tau-ratio form, the nonlinear equation naturally decomposes into a cubic sector containing all second-derivative terms and a quartic gradient envelope containing only first derivatives. This decomposition reveals that the dynamical kernel of the stationary axisymmetric Einstein equations is trilinear, not quartic, providing a new algebraic perspective on the integrability of these gravitational systems.

concepts.name: Tomimatsu–Sato Solutions
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that both the δ=2 and δ=3 Tomimatsu–Sato solutions possess the same YTSF-type trilinear kernel structure, with a universal normalization constant κ = −4p²q² independent of δ. This result supports a universality conjecture that the entire Tomimatsu–Sato hierarchy shares a common trilinear integrable kernel governing its second-derivative sector.

concepts.name: Ostrogradsky Instability and Higher-Derivative Field Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper connects the emergence of a trilinear (cubic) tau-function kernel to the second-order character of the underlying field equations, noting that higher-derivative theories suffer from Ostrogradsky instabilities and ghost modes. It argues that the trilinear structure represents the maximal nontrivial integrable kernel compatible with a well-posed second-order dynamical equation, linking algebraic structure to physical causality and unitarity constraints.

2605.05617v1.title: Static-Field Tunneling Ionization in Space-Fractional Quantum Mechanics

concepts.name: Tunneling Ionization and ADK/PPT Theory
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a closed-form 'fractional-ADK' (fADK) tunneling exponent that generalizes the standard ADK result to space-fractional quantum mechanics, replacing the conventional I_p^(3/2) scaling with I_p^(1+1/α) and introducing a sin(π/α) phase factor. This provides the first static-field ionization benchmark in the explicit ADK/PPT sense for nonlocal kinetic operators, reducing exactly to the standard ADK exponent in the α=2 limit. Numerical validation via time-dependent fractional Schrödinger equation simulations confirms the exponential tunneling form persists across fractional orders, while revealing systematic deviations from the fADK prediction that signal genuinely nonlocal transport effects.

concepts.name: Space-Fractional Quantum Mechanics (Riesz Fractional Laplacian)
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the application of space-fractional quantum mechanics, governed by the Riesz fractional Laplacian with dispersion T(p) ∝ |p|^α, into the domain of strong-field and tunneling-driven processes for the first time in an ADK-style framework. It establishes that the nonlocal kinetic operator systematically enhances tunneling ionization rates relative to conventional quantum mechanics, with the enhancement growing as α decreases, and that this effect persists even when the ionization potential is held fixed. The work also introduces a concrete convention (D_α = 1/2) that ensures a smooth α→2 limit and clean attribution of effects to fractional nonlocality.

concepts.name: WKB Semiclassical Action for Tunneling
concepts.contribution: The paper generalizes the WKB under-barrier action to a fractional dispersion relation by identifying the physically consistent complex momentum branch p(x) = e^(iπ/α)[2W(x)]^(1/α), which smoothly recovers the standard imaginary WKB momentum at α=2. Application of the triangular exit-barrier approximation to this fractional momentum yields a closed-form imaginary action whose structure directly encodes how anomalous dispersion deforms the classical forbidden-region dynamics. This fractional WKB action is shown to serve as a unifying semiclassical reference for numerical benchmarking, analogous to the role the standard WKB action plays in conventional strong-field theory.

concepts.name: Bound-State Structure and Ionization Potential in Nonlocal Quantum Dynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates numerically that reducing the fractional order α progressively delocalizes the ground-state wavefunction and raises the ground-state energy, showing that standard quadratic quantum mechanics corresponds to the most strongly bound realization of a Coulomb problem within its fractional generalizations. Two complementary protocols—one with fixed potential and α-dependent I_p, and one with fixed I_p achieved by tuning the soft-core parameter—are introduced to disentangle bound-state renormalization effects from dynamical nonlocality in the tunneling process. The comparison between protocols establishes that fractional tunneling enhancement is not simply reducible to a shift in ionization potential, but reflects genuine nonlocal transport in the classically forbidden region.

2605.05608v1.title: Dynamical Signatures of Floquet Topology in Wave Packet Dynamics

concepts.name: Floquet Topology and Topological Phase Transitions
concepts.contribution: The paper develops a framework for dynamically detecting Floquet topological invariants—including both the standard winding number ν₀ and the anomalous invariant νπ—without requiring direct band structure measurement. It demonstrates that band inversions at topological phase transitions leave distinct imprints on center-of-mass dynamics, specifically through the emergence of new low-frequency oscillatory modes and phase shifts in the trajectory. The paper also formally proves the equivalence between winding numbers computed from the time-evolution operator and those from the extended Floquet Hamiltonian using inversion symmetry.

concepts.name: Zitterbewegung in Periodically Driven Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper extends the concept of Zitterbewegung from static band structures to Floquet systems, showing that periodic driving generates multi-frequency oscillations in the center-of-mass position whose frequency components correspond to quasienergy gaps between Floquet sidebands. It derives analytically that driving-induced sideband interference produces additional oscillatory terms beyond the intrinsic band-gap frequency, with amplitudes scaling as A/ω. This establishes multi-frequency Zitterbewegung as a direct spectroscopic probe of the Floquet band structure.

concepts.name: Perturbation Theory in Extended Hilbert Space
concepts.contribution: The paper constructs a perturbation theory for Floquet systems using the coupling strength V as the small parameter rather than the conventional inverse-frequency expansion of the Floquet-Magnus approach, enabling accurate treatment beyond the high-frequency limit. It derives first-order corrections to Floquet eigenstates and shows that the Floquet-Magnus expansion emerges as a further high-frequency approximation of this more general framework. The formalism explicitly captures the energy-gap dependence of oscillation amplitudes and provides transparent interpretation of multi-frequency center-of-mass dynamics.

concepts.name: Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) Model under Periodic Driving
concepts.contribution: The paper applies the driven SSH model as a concrete testbed to demonstrate how both frequency-tuned and amplitude-tuned topological phase transitions manifest in center-of-mass dynamics, covering transitions in both the 0-gap and π-gap invariants. It shows that dynamical signatures of band inversion—phase reversals and low-frequency mode dominance—persist robustly even outside the perturbative regime A/ω ≪ 1. The analysis connects local massive Dirac point contributions of ±1/2 topological charge to changes in bulk winding numbers across the phase diagram.

2605.05605v1.title: Mixed Global Dynamics of the Forced Vibro-Impact Oscillator with Coulomb Friction and its Symplectic Structure, KAM Tori, and Persistence

concepts.name: Symplectic Mechanics and Area-Preserving Maps
concepts.contribution: The paper proves rigorously that the stroboscopic (Poincaré) map of the forced vibro-impact oscillator is exact symplectic on the maximal forward-invariant non-sticking subset of phase space, upgrading a determinant identity from prior numerical work to a full structural symplectic result. This is achieved via a universal-cover lift using a triangular wave projection, which transforms the piecewise-smooth bouncing system into a smooth Hamiltonian system on a covering manifold where Liouville's theorem applies directly. The symplectic structure is further extended to N-particle systems with elastic binary collisions.

concepts.name: KAM Theory (Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser)
concepts.contribution: The paper establishes the existence of invariant Cantor families of closed curves (KAM tori) surrounding elliptic non-sticking periodic orbits, with the complement having Lebesgue measure O(δ⁵/²), providing the rigorous mathematical foundation for the Hamiltonian stability islands observed numerically in prior work. By lifting to the smooth covering manifold, the authors avoid the need for a piecewise-smooth KAM theory and apply Moser's classical twist theorem directly. A computer-assisted proof using interval arithmetic certifies the ellipticity and order-four non-resonance conditions at a specific parameter point, making the KAM result constructive.

concepts.name: Mixed Conservative-Dissipative Dynamics
concepts.contribution: The paper provides the first complete rigorous analysis of a non-reversible system exhibiting simultaneous Hamiltonian and dissipative behavior in a single connected phase space at identical parameter values. The mechanism is shown to be geometric: trajectories that never cross zero velocity preserve symplectic area via unit-determinant saltation matrices, while any trajectory with a velocity-zero or sticking event contracts area due to a saltation factor strictly less than one. The paper further quantifies how this mixed structure is destroyed under physical perturbations, showing that any positive restitution defect or viscous damping converts elliptic islands into asymptotically stable attractors at a rate ρ(ε, μᵥ) = 1 − 2n*ε − μᵥT.

concepts.name: Homoclinic Chaos and the Melnikov Method
concepts.contribution: The paper derives a closed-form Melnikov function M(t₀) = A cos(ωt₀) + B for the splitting of the homoclinic loop near the saddle-center bifurcation, with explicit expressions for the oscillatory amplitude A and the friction-driven constant B. When |A| > |B|, transverse zeros of the Melnikov function are established, and the Smale-Birkhoff theorem is invoked to prove the existence of an invariant hyperbolic Cantor set on which the dynamics is conjugate to a Bernoulli shift, rigorously explaining the chaotic sea surrounding the KAM islands. This provides the first analytical characterization of the chaotic boundary region observed in prior numerical simulations of this system.

2605.05604v1.title: Temporal Coarse-Graining as the Origin of Macroscopic Friction in Quantum Spin Chains via Data-Driven Liouvillian Extraction

concepts.name: Quantum-to-Classical Emergence of Irreversibility
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that macroscopic friction and viscosity in isolated quantum systems are not intrinsic microscopic properties but emergent phenomena contingent on the observer's temporal resolution. By showing that exact unitary dynamics yields zero net dissipation while finite temporal coarse-graining produces strictly positive friction and viscosity, it provides a mechanistic account of how irreversibility arises from reversible Schrödinger evolution. This reframes macroscopic dissipation as an epistemological artifact of timescale separation rather than an ontological feature of the system.

concepts.name: Hydrodynamics in Quantum Many-Body Systems
concepts.contribution: Rather than fitting spin density dynamics to a purely diffusive Fick's law model, the paper extracts the full Navier-Stokes hydrodynamic coefficients—mechanical elasticity, local friction, and kinematic viscosity—directly and independently from unitary spin chain dynamics. It reveals that the direct density-to-density diffusion coefficient is strictly zero, meaning macroscopic transport must proceed through the intermediate generation of spin current and momentum dissipation. This exposes a fundamental flaw in conventional diffusion-fitting paradigms and clarifies the correct two-step mechanical structure of transport in quantum spin chains.

concepts.name: Mori-Zwanzig Projection and Temporal Coarse-Graining
concepts.contribution: The paper integrates the Mori-Zwanzig projection formalism with a data-driven generalized Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition framework, demonstrating that spatial projection alone (tracing out unobserved degrees of freedom) is insufficient to produce stable macroscopic dissipation without accompanying temporal coarse-graining. It identifies a distinct crossover timescale at which microscopic coherent oscillations are averaged out, establishing an intermediate functional regime of genuine Markovian hydrodynamics. The framework also shows that excessive coarse-graining destroys the fluid picture via a sinc-filter effect, bounding the regime where classical hydrodynamics is valid.

concepts.name: Eigenstate Thermalization and Quantum Chaos
concepts.contribution: By simulating a next-nearest-neighbor XXZ spin chain specifically tuned to be quantum chaotic and non-integrable, the paper provides a concrete setting in which ETH-driven thermalization and the emergence of transport coefficients can be directly observed and quantified without thermodynamic limit approximations. The data-driven Liouvillian extraction shows that spectral information—particularly the distribution of eigenvalue real parts—directly encodes the transition between reversible unitary dynamics and emergent dissipation as a function of observable dictionary choice and temporal resolution. This connects the abstract predictions of ETH to measurable, finite-system hydrodynamic coefficients.

2605.05589v1.title: Galois Solvability of Finite-Size Bethe Solutions in the Heisenberg Chain

concepts.name: Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that the Bethe ansatz equations for the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain, while formally exact, yield finite-size solutions whose algebraic complexity grows rapidly with system size. It explicitly shows that the irreducible polynomials governing the Bethe-roots become Galois unsolvable for chains of eight or more sites, establishing that quantum integrability does not guarantee analytic closed-form solvability of the resulting equations.

concepts.name: Galois Theory and Solvability by Radicals
concepts.contribution: The paper applies Galois theory to the characteristic polynomials of finite-size Bethe solutions, computing their Galois groups using Stauduhar's method and the Fieker-Klüners algorithm. It finds that the Galois group of the eight-site Bethe-polynomial is the symmetric group S6, which is unsolvable, providing a rigorous algebraic proof that the roots cannot be expressed in radicals and establishing a concrete threshold for the onset of algebraic intractability.

concepts.name: Valence-Bond and Resonating-Valence-Bond States
concepts.contribution: The paper reconstructs exact symbolic ground states in the non-crossing valence-bond basis from Bethe ansatz solutions for chains up to ten sites, extending previously known symbolic results beyond the six-site case. It shows that the algebraic degree of the ground state wavefunction coefficients tracks the number of rotationally inequivalent non-crossing valence-bond configurations, connecting the combinatorial structure of the RVB basis to the algebraic complexity of the many-body ground state.

concepts.name: Exact Solvability in Quantum Many-Body Systems
concepts.contribution: The paper sharply distinguishes between two notions of exact solvability: the existence of exact defining equations for the spectrum, and the existence of elementary closed-form expressions for the solutions of those equations. By showing that these two notions diverge already at small finite system sizes in the paradigmatic Heisenberg chain, the paper provides a concrete, rigorous basis for understanding why numerical methods are indispensable even in exactly integrable models.

2605.05565v1.title: Squeezed spectra and back-to-back correlations of protons and antiprotons at RHIC energies

concepts.name: In-Medium Mass Modification of Hadrons
concepts.contribution: The paper constrains the range of momentum-dependent in-medium mass modification for protons and antiprotons by comparing theoretical calculations with STAR experimental transverse momentum spectra and yield ratios across six RHIC collision energies. It demonstrates that a momentum-independent mass modification is insufficient to describe the data, and introduces a Gaussian momentum-dependent form (δm(p) = δm0 exp[−p²/Λ²]) that successfully reproduces the experimental observations. The results provide indirect evidence that protons and antiprotons undergo in-medium mass modification consistent with a δm0 of 20 MeV across all collision energies studied.

concepts.name: Fermion Back-to-Back Correlations (fBBC)
concepts.contribution: The paper provides theoretical predictions for the p-pbar fermion back-to-back correlation strength at multiple RHIC energies (11.5 to 200 GeV) using constrained in-medium mass modification parameters, extending prior work that found only a ~2% (statistically insignificant) signal in a narrow momentum window. It shows that the fBBC signal is highly sensitive to the assumed source time distribution: a Lorentzian form produces a pronounced high-momentum signal while an α-stable Lévy form produces a pronounced low-momentum signal, and that signal suppression grows with the time distribution width parameter Δt. The study further predicts that events with a larger p-bar/p yield ratio within the same collision system are more likely to exhibit a detectable fBBC signal, proposing a new experimental strategy for observation.

concepts.name: Bogoliubov-Valatin Transformation in Hot Dense Matter
concepts.contribution: The paper applies the fermionic Bogoliubov-Valatin transformation to relate vacuum and in-medium particle creation/annihilation operators, establishing the theoretical link between a non-zero in-medium mass modification and the emergence of squeezed back-to-back correlations for proton-antiproton pairs. It extends this framework to incorporate a momentum-dependent mass modification parameter, improving the physical realism of prior treatments that assumed a constant δm. This formalism simultaneously governs both the single-particle spectra modifications and the fBBC correlation function within a unified framework.

concepts.name: Lévy-Stable Source Distributions in Heavy-Ion Collisions
concepts.contribution: The paper contrasts two freeze-out time distribution models—Lorentzian and α-stable Lévy—and demonstrates that their choice fundamentally determines the momentum-dependence and detectability of the p-pbar fBBC signal. For the α-stable Lévy form, the paper finds that α = 1.35 (consistent with PHENIX measurements in the range 0.2 < pT < 2 GeV/c) suppresses the fBBC to unobservable levels, whereas α = 1 yields a potentially observable low-momentum signal at Δt = 0.8 fm/c. This highlights the Lévy distribution as a critical input for interpreting or designing future back-to-back correlation measurements at RHIC.

2605.05537v1.title: Implications of the LISA stochastic signal from eccentric stellar mass black hole binaries in vacuum

concepts.name: Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background (SGWB)
concepts.contribution: The paper develops an improved phenomenological fitting model for the SGWB from eccentric stellar-mass binary black holes, valid across all eccentricities from quasi-circular to near-unity, correcting the asymptotic low-frequency behavior that prior fits failed to capture. It extends this model from an idealized Dirac-delta eccentricity distribution to the astrophysically motivated thermal distribution, and uses a fully Bayesian framework to quantify when the eccentric SGWB is distinguishable from a circular background in LISA data.

concepts.name: Orbital Eccentricity in Binary Inspiral
concepts.contribution: The paper quantifies how residual orbital eccentricity in the LISA mHz band redistributes gravitational-wave power from the dominant quadrupole harmonic into higher harmonics, producing a characteristic spectral suppression and turnover at low frequencies. It establishes that eccentricities e0 ≳ 0.9 at an orbital frequency of 10⁻⁴ Hz are robustly measurable by LISA, while lower eccentricities or thermal distributions at lower formation frequencies are largely degenerate with quasi-circular evolution.

concepts.name: Environmental Effects on Binary Evolution (Dynamical Friction)
concepts.contribution: The paper demonstrates that including eccentricity in the vacuum SGWB model reduces the statistical evidence for dynamical friction from astrophysical environments, because both effects similarly suppress the SGWB at low frequencies. It establishes a revised threshold, finding that only gas densities ρ ≳ 10⁻⁷ g cm⁻³ allow dynamical friction to be distinguished from eccentric vacuum evolution, a stricter requirement than found when eccentricity is neglected.

concepts.name: Multi-Band Gravitational-Wave Astronomy
concepts.contribution: The paper shows that a LISA detection of the sBBH SGWB consistent with quasi-circular evolution places an upper bound on the maximum eccentricity of the sBBH population at ground-based detector frequencies, excluding mean eccentricities ē₂₀Hz ≳ 10⁻² for generic distributions. This cross-band constraint directly informs template modeling and population inference for next-generation ground-based detectors such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer operating concurrently with LISA.
